Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

מוסר קשור להתנהגות הנכונה והשגויה. טוהר הוא היעדר פגם מוסרי או אשמה, מסומן בכנות מינית ובשלמות אישית. טוהר אינו מכיל דבר שאינו שייך שם כהלכה. כפי שהכותרת מרמזת, מאמר זה יתמקד בעשיית הראוי ובהיותנו חפים מפגם מוסרי ואשמה, בחיי שלמות ובהבטחת שכל מה שבפנים ובחוץ יהיה נקי מדברים שאינם שייכים.

שימו לב למה שהתנ"ך אומר על היותנו טהורים. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

להיות טהור מבחינה מוסרית לא יקרה בלי נחישות ודיסיפלינה חזקה. זה תמיד היה כך, אך אפילו יותר כיום עם עליית הטכנולוגיה וזמינות הרע בקצות אצבעותינו.

חטאים מיניים אינם זרים לכנסייה. למעשה, הם אינם זרים לאף עם ולאף גזע. איננו יכולים להירגע ולהוריד את המשמר ולסבור שילדינו יהיו בטוחים מפני רעי החברה והאדם. עלינו להראות בדוגמה וללמד את ילדינו ונוערנו אם אנו מצפים שהם יישארו טהורים בחברה מושחתת זו. איננו יכולים להניח שאם אדם מתלבש בצורה מסוימת — הכול תקין בפנים. הסיפור אינו מסופר במלואו רק על ידי המראה החיצוני. הפרושים גרמו לחיצוניות להיראות טובה, בעוד שהפנים היו מלאים בשחיתות. ישוע אמר, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). גם אנו צריכים לתת תשומת לב עיקרית לנושאי הלב. כשהלב נקי, גם החיצוניות תוכל להיות מטוהרת.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

מסר זה נועד להיות מסר של תקווה, לא ייאוש. אם יש לך נקודה חשוכה סודית, התוודה עליה והיפטר ממנה. אתה יכול להשתחרר! אפשר להשתחרר מאחיזתו של השטן ולחיות חיים פתוחים ושקופים עם שמחה בנפש. אינך צריך לעבור את החיים מנסה להסתיר את חשכת הרע. ישוע רוצה לסלוח ולרפא.

השטן אכזר. ב־John 10:10 ישוע אמר, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

חטא מוסרי כל כך מביש וקשה להודות בו. הדבר הטבעי הוא לנסות להסתיר כשעוברים על החוק. ילדים הלומדים להסתיר מעשים רעים בגיל צעיר מפתחים באופן טבעי לנוער שמסתיר דברים מהורים, ממורים ומשרתי כנסייה. אדם כזה יצטרך ללמוד להיות פתוח ושקוף, או שיגיע הזמן שבו יתחיל להסתיר דברים גם ממלווהו. ההסתרה גורמת לחיים כפולים ומובילה ליותר עבדות ולמערכות יחסים שבורות. אנשים שיש להם דלתות סגורות בפינות מסוימות של חייהם יהיו קנאים לגבי הטלפונים שלהם ולא יסכימו לשתף סיסמאות עם בן/בת זוג מהימן. נדמה שאנו שוכחים בקלות כמה חסר תועלת להסתיר מאלוהים. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” כיצד נוכל להיות כה תמימים וטפשים לחשוב שנוכל להסתיר משהו מאלוהים? או לקחת צעד נוסף: למה היינו רוצים להסתיר משהו ממנו? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” אלוהים אוהב אותך יותר מדי כדי לא לאפשר לך להמשיך להסתיר מה שצריך להיחשף ולהיות מסולח.

חטאים מיניים גם הם מטעות ביותר. בדרך כלל זה קורה כפי ש־James תיאר בפרק הראשון. אנו מתפתים, נמשכים הצידה, נמשך כמו מגנט ממוקד, מרגישים גל של תשוקה, מוודאים שאיש אינו מסתכל, מכסים את עקבותינו, מתקרבים צעד קרוב יותר לאסור, מרגישים עוד תשוקה, ומתחילים מהר לאבד שיקול דעת ומחשבה שפויה, לא מסוגלים לחשב תוצאות בדומה לאדם שכר, ואז James 1:15 קורה: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James יאמר לנו שלא להשתוקק לדברים שאינם שלנו, אפילו לא כהרף עין. התנ"ך מצווה אותנו לברוח משלושה דברים. אחד מהם הוא זנון, שניתן להרחיבו לכל החטאים המיניים. אל תתעסקו עם זה; אל תביטו שוב; התרחקו ממנו! החליפו את המחשבות הללו במחשבות בונות על אלוהים ודרכו. שירו המנון ישן; תודה לאל שאיננו יכולים לחשוב על שני דברים בו־זמנית. לא משנה מה צריך, ברח מהתשוקה הזו. היא תקח אותך רחוק יותר ממה שתרצה ותעלה לך יותר ממה שתהיה מוכן לשלם. רוץ את הסרט עד הסוף ושאל את עצמך, אם אלך אחרי מה שמתפתים אליו, האם אקבל את מה שאני רוצה? השטן תמיד מבטיח עונג, אך מספק כאב. זכרו, השטן מעולם לא המציא הנאה; הוא רק לוקח מה שאלוהים עשה טהור וטוב, מקלקל אותו, ומציע אותו חזרה בצורה מעוותת. זכרו, חרב השטן שלופה כדי להרוג בנקודה זו. ברחו מהרצונות הרעים!

אל תלכו אחרי התשוקה שלכם. פורנוגרפיה ממכרת מאוד ושיתקה רבים. Promise Keepers אמרו שסקר שלהם מצא כי 65% מהגברים התמכרו. התמכרות לפורנו דומה להתמכרות לאלכוהול או לסמים. הם אומרים לנו שהמוח דורש שאנדורפינים יוזרמו אליו, בין אם מהתמכרות לאלכוהול, לסמים או לפורנו. אני מדגיש שוב שהגברים והנשים שיעלו לניצחון יהיו אלה ש, כמו דניאל בימי קדם, יתחייבו בלבם לא להתנכר.

נושא זה גם מיועד לאחיותינו, וכמה שאלות נראות הולמות. מה בחייך הפנימיים מסודר ומוסתר היטב? האם אכזבות החיים יצרו ריק שמוביל לנטילת ׳טיילנול רגשי׳ שגורם לך להרגיש טוב לזמן קצר? האם הקשר הרגשי שלך בטוח במקום שאלוהים תכנן שיהיה?

נערות צעירות צריכות ללמוד לפתח שמירת מרחק בריאה מול גברים. לא בגישה מתנשאת ולעולם לא ללא חיוך, אך גם לא בחופשיות יתר בקשר לנערים. החברה שלנו מכוונת בדיוק להפך, ומגן ילדים מבית הספר היסודי והלאה מציקים לבנים ולבנות לגבי חברות מיוחדות. כתוצאה מכך, ילדים גדלים עם מעט או בלי שמירת מרחק. יש להימנע מהתכתבות חברתית בין המינים מחוץ ליחסים משפחתיים. זה יפתח אצל הנוער הרגל שיום אחד יצטרך להישבר אם הם מצפים לחיות חיים פתוחים ושקופים עם בן/בת זוג. חשבו על זה כך: האם היית רוצה שבן/בת זוגך תתכתב חברתית עם המין השני ברשתות החברתיות?

אחיות, היזהרו מספרי קריאה שאתם קוראות. רומנים רומנטיים מקהים את התאווה לתורת האלוהים ויוצרים ציפיות בלתי מציאותיות מחיי נישואין. ספרים אלה מעבירים את הרעיון שהאיש הנכון אי שם יהיה המפתח למימוש ואושר בחיים. רק ישוע יכול למלא את החור שהחטא גרם לכל אדם היום. אף גבר או אישה לא יוכלו אי פעם לתת את הביטחון והשקט של הנפש שכולנו כל כך כוונים אליו. הכאב הזה בלב לעולם לא ישותה על ידי פלסטרים או משככי כאבים. הם עוזרים רק לרגע, וכאשר הם פגתים, הצעקה של הלב חזקה אף יותר. ספרים בלתי בריאים מקהים את הטעם לדברים של אלוהים, ובמקומם יוצרים תאווה למזון מהיר ונכסים מרגיעי כאב.

דאגה נוספת לאחיות היא כמות הזמן שאתן מבלות ברשת. אין גבול להאכיל את התאווה ליופי, ייחודיות, חן ומראה. אל תתנו לדברים אלה להניע את חייכן כי הם לעולם לא יאמרו 'די' ולא ימלאו את הנפש ולא יכוונו את ילדיכן בדרך הנכונה. שקלו את כמות הזמן שאתן משקיעות באירוח מסיבות. במהלך השנים ראיתי שמות של הזדמנויות עסקיות ומוצרים שבמשך תקופה צריך היה להחזיק — אך לצערי, אחרי כמה שנים איננו זוכרים אפילו את השמות האלה ובינתיים הילדים גדלו וכעת הם בוגרים. שקלו את הצרכים האמיתיים בחייכן ואת אחריותכן, ואז החליטו מה יביא השקעה נצחית. נשים עם ילדים צריכות להגביל תחביבים שנהנות מהם מאוד כיוון שלרגע זה, הן מבורכות בילדים בעלי נשמות נצחיות וזמן איתם הוא השקעה נצחית. זכרו שבעליכן וילדיכן ראויים בהרבה לזמנכן מאשר בילוי שעות במסיבה נוספת.

A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

Une chose merveilleuse d'être chrétien est d'anticiper le jour où nous pourrons contempler la beauté magnifique de notre Dieu. Il est fort probable que nous ayons tous créé des images mentales de ce à quoi nous pensons que Dieu pourrait ressembler, bien que nous sachions que nos imaginations les plus folles seront dépassées. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). La Bible regorge de descriptions imagées tentant de nous donner un bref aperçu des domaines célestes. Le paysage sur les collines de la gloire, les créatures merveilleuses qui y demeurent, et surtout, l'Être Suprême sur le trône, défient tous notre effort humain pour saisir et comprendre la beauté et la gloire de notre Dieu.

Parfois nous admirons la beauté dans un chant, une œuvre d'art, une histoire, ou même une autre personne, mais David décrit le délice de contempler la beauté de Dieu. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). Dieu est beau parce que Son excellence est attirante— Son caractère est sans défaut. David a éprouvé le plaisir qui vient de connaître et d'expérimenter Dieu dans toute Sa plénitude. Comment Dieu exprime-t-Il Sa Beauté ?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). Dans l'horreur de la Passion du Christ, nous trouvons une beauté profonde et grave — la beauté d'un sacrifice accompli par un Sauveur sans péché pour une humanité indigne. Parfois, le type de beauté le plus poignant se trouve dans des choses que nous ne pouvons pas entièrement comprendre.

Il y a de la beauté dans les pleurs de Marie et des disciples autour de la croix qui retenait le corps sans vie de leur bien-aimé Maître. Mais quand l'aube se leva le matin de la résurrection, le désespoir se changea en espérance et le deuil en joie.

Nous voyons une scène belle au Mont des Oliviers quarante jours plus tard lorsque les mêmes disciples regardaient mélancoliquement le ciel, regardant leur Seigneur ressuscité disparaître dans les cieux. Avec une grande joie, ils retournèrent à Jérusalem, la promesse de Son retour brûlant dans leurs cœurs, pour attendre la venue du Saint-Esprit.

Aujourd'hui nous attendons avec espérance que le Fils de Dieu paraisse du ciel avec puissance et grande gloire pour compléter l'œuvre du salut. Alors nous Le contemplerons dans toute Sa splendeur et Sa beauté. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

Comment devrions-nous, en tant qu'images porteuses de Dieu, refléter Sa beauté à travers l'Évangile ? Dieu est un être éternel non créé, et l'homme a été créé à Son image pour refléter Sa gloire et Sa beauté. Cependant, cette beauté a été entachée par le péché et n'est plus une représentation digne du caractère de Dieu. Mais, il y a la rédemption ! Peu de choses surpassent la beauté d'une vie qui fut autrefois meurtrie et brisée par le péché mais qui est maintenant restaurée, rachetée et rendue entière par l'Évangile. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Les athées contestent l'existence de Dieu, les scientifiques débattent contre la création biblique, les savants mettent en question l'inerrance des Écritures, mais personne ne peut contester le témoignage d'une vie rachetée.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). Toute beauté dans le monde créé vient de Dieu. Un coucher de soleil splendide, une rose délicate, un séquoia imposant, un pic de montagne majestueux, témoignent tous de la beauté de Dieu illustrée dans la création. Comme des panneaux routiers le long de l'autoroute nous guident vers notre destination, ainsi la création dirige l'humanité vers Dieu lui-même. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). Ces dons de la création sont donnés pour nous offrir un bref aperçu de Celui qui les a créés.

Comment devrions-nous, en tant que partie de la création de Dieu, refléter Sa beauté créatrice ? Bien que nous ne puissions pas faire quelque chose à partir de rien, Dieu nous a conçus pour être créatifs, utilisant les ressources de Sa création et nos capacités intellectuelles pour rendre la vie pratique. Le sentiment d'accomplissement gratifiant qui découle d'un travail bien fait a son origine dans la création, où Dieu regarda Son ouvrage et le déclara bon. Dans notre tentative de mener des vies non extravagantes, nous manquons parfois de prendre plaisir aux belles choses de la vie. Il est juste et bon et en harmonie avec notre création de trouver du plaisir dans les choses de beauté. Les hommes impies ont utilisé ce don de créativité à maintes reprises à des fins mauvaises. D'autant plus, glorifions Dieu en utilisant Sa création de manières qui reflètent Son caractère.

Un avertissement pour tous ceux qui aiment la nature et la création (naturelle et faite par l'homme) : prenons garde à ne pas élever la beauté terrestre au-dessus du Créateur, ce qui conduit à l'idolâtrie. Les couchers de soleil s'estompent, les séquoias tombent, les roses se fanent, le corps humain redevient poussière, mais Dieu demeure. La vie et toute sa beauté commencent et finissent avec Dieu.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) Selon le livre de l'Apocalypse, le trône de Dieu est entouré de sons : tonnerre et éclairs ; louanges émanant des anges, des quatre créatures et des vingt-quatre vieillards, et la grande multitude qu'aucun homme ne peut dénombrer ; et le nouveau cantique des cent quarante-quatre mille.

Dieu a créé la beauté du son pour se glorifier d'une manière que de simples mots ne peuvent accomplir. L'intricité de Sa créativité se révèle puissamment dans la façon dont différentes fréquences sonores s'assemblent pour créer une harmonie belle et céleste. Il est honorable pour Dieu que l'humanité prenne plaisir à la beauté des sons qu'Il a créés pour Sa gloire. La personne qui aime Dieu sera attirée vers Lui chaque fois qu'Il est bercé par des sons agréables : le peuple de Dieu chantant les cantiques de Sion, les prières des saints, le vent chuchotant à travers les cimes des arbres, l'oiseau chanteur louant son Créateur, le grondement du tonnerre, ou le simple clapotis de la pluie sur le toit.

Comment devrions-nous, en tant qu'instruments de son, refléter la beauté de Dieu par le son ? Nous devrions toujours chercher à écouter et à ressembler aux sons et aux harmonies du ciel. Bien que nous ne pourrons jamais complètement accomplir cela sur terre, cela devrait être un effort de toute une vie. Les questions ont été posées : “Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” et “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” Nous ne pourrons jamais atteindre la perfection céleste, donc la question devrait plutôt être : “Are we giving God the best we have?” Certaines personnes ont plus de capacités de chant que d'autres, mais la question demeure. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Soyons des producteurs de sons qui honorent Dieu et qui apportent de la joie au cœur du Créateur !

Through the Church:

La Bible parle abondamment de la beauté du peuple de Dieu. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” sont des expressions synonymes tissées tout au long des Écritures se référant à l'habitation du peuple de Dieu sur la terre. Il est le désir de Dieu que Sa beauté soit reflétée dans la vie de Son peuple. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Rien n'est plus cher au cœur de Dieu que Son Église. Lorsque les enfants d'Israël voyagèrent à travers le désert, ils édifièrent le tabernacle comme un lieu où Dieu pourrait demeurer parmi eux. Lorsque Salomon dédia le temple comme demeure de Dieu, Dieu fut très agréé et 2 Chronicles 7:1 dit que la gloire de l'Éternel remplit le temple. Le temple était considéré comme la Maison de l'Éternel – Jésus lui-même s'y référa à de nombreuses reprises comme la maison de Dieu et fut très passionné pour qu'elle soit gardée sainte.

Aujourd'hui, ni le tabernacle ni le temple n'accueillent la présence de Dieu mais plutôt Sa passion divine est concentrée sur l'Église de Jésus-Christ. Ici sont les gens qui L'aiment véritablement et qui sont prêts à donner leur vie pour Lui. Ici sont les personnes qui sont disposées à renoncer à leurs droits individuels et à se livrer à une cause plus grande. Ici beaucoup de saints ont donné leur propre sang pour l'Évangile. Et ici est l'endroit où un jour notre Sauveur reviendra comme Il l'a promis, et transportera Son épouse, l'Église, vers sa demeure éternelle. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

Comment devrions-nous, en tant que peuple de Dieu, refléter Sa beauté dans l'Église ? En demeurant ensemble dans l'unité et l'harmonie avec amour pour tous les hommes, spécialement la maison de Dieu. L'Église devrait être un endroit où le monde peut entrevoir ce qui se passe au ciel. Elle devrait être un lieu où Christ est toujours élevé comme le conquérant victorieux du péché, de la mort et de l'enfer.

Hélas, beaucoup de gens se sont désorientés à cause des échecs de l'Église et se sont éloignés de la véritable foi apostolique. En dépit de nos déceptions, relevons “the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) et persévérons. Nous n'aurons jamais un appel plus élevé, ni une guerre plus noble à mener.

Enfin, comment devrions-nous refléter Sa beauté dans nos vies ? En nous réjouissant en Lui. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). La plus grande plénitude dans la vie vient du plaisir de réjouir le cœur de Dieu en se délectant de ce qu'Il se délecte et en aimant ce qu'Il aime. Ne perdons jamais l'émerveillement de la beauté de notre Salut !

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

These nobler works of Thine,

These new births more divine:

This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;

Through the new earth and Heaven.

“Get out of my shop! I don’t need people like you around me! And never come back!” My lips quivered as I looked into the dark, angry eyes of the yelling man. I blinked back the unbidden tears, realizing that once more, I had to leave this man that I loved. All night I could sense that we were coming to this, and I had tried so hard not to let it happen. With one last attempt, I feebly yelled above the tension, “Ken, we don’t want to ...” but once more, I was rudely cut off. With slumped shoulders and downcast eyes, I turned to escape the confines of his dingy, pawn shop, his ever-crescendoing voice drowning the last hope of respite.

The lingering smell of smoke and the echo of his angry voice joined the troubled thoughts of my emotionally overwrought mind, as I slowly walked up the street. “What do you think, Josh?” I asked my faithful, quiet friend.

“I don’t know, " he responded, and we fell back into silent anguish at the outcome of our supposed Bible study, grasping for an explanation for the terrible response. What could we have done differently? Why could he not accept the truth? What lay behind those flashing eyes, and what memories are stored beneath his ever-crowning beanie?

Ken was born on a country farm in the rolling hills of Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, a splendid place for a curious and adventurous little boy to live.

When Ken was four years old, his parents separated. He had heard them fighting a lot, but he didn’t know that it was possible for Mom and Dad to separate. It crushed his heart and confused his innocent soul. He did not know how to handle the stress and change that was tossed on his peaceful life.

The terror and confusion of his mom hurriedly packing their belongings, loading him and his siblings in the car, and driving away are still riveted in his mind. It made no sense! Why couldn’t they just go home? In his musty bedroom at their little, dingy apartment, he lay staring at the moldy ceiling, wondering endlessly what had gone so wrong.

Ken soon adjusted to his new home in the city of Pottsville with only cars, people, and sidewalks instead of cows, frogs, and mud. But fate did not leave the small security his new lifestyle provided him. His mom was not able to properly care for him and his siblings, and so the children were placed in different foster homes. That was even worse than leaving Dad! The clothes he wore were the only things familiar to him. Instead of understanding and loving him, each new family brought more yelling, hatred, and beating. Terror, tears, loneliness, and pain accompanied him.

Ken thought the second foster home that he was placed in would be a safe, loving home. The dad was tall and strong and appeared to be gentle. The mom was overweight, but her friendly smile resolved his fears. But the first night, when he reached for the food, he accidentally dumped a cup of water. She screamed at him and told him that he was worthless, and she wished they had never gotten him. The dad continued eating as if he didn't hear or care. Why didn’t the strong man stop her?

That evening, Ken crawled into his big, strange bed, already crying in loneliness, when he heard the mom yell. He quickly jumped out of bed and, with trembling legs, slipped behind the door to hide. She charged up the stairs bellowing angrily, and Ken was sure that he was in trouble. To his relief, she continued down the hall. He was still too scared to leave his hiding place for fear of receiving a beating. He wiped his tears as he began to sing under his breath a song he had heard in Sunday school, “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” He stopped to think, and his crying quit. “Then why am I here? " he wondered. “Have I done something wrong? God must not love little children. That song is not true! If God loved me I would not be here!" With that conclusion, he burst into tears and lost hope in God. He woke the next morning, still hidden behind the door.

Darkness had long fallen, and my family was all peacefully sleeping in our old farmhouse. I cried myself to sleep, crying for Ken's soul, crying because I didn’t know what to do, crying because my friend, the man I longed to see at peace with God, hated me.

Ken continued to fire questions. “How can God be good and allow so much bad? How could God let children suffer?” I listened on as he continued saying the same things that I heard so many times before, giving me no chance to talk.

Again, it was time to leave, and I was so glad to do so. He kept talking as we backed out the door. Once more, my friend and I walked up the street —tired, frustrated, and wishing never to come back.

Ken was 13 years old, and his life was no better than it had been when he was first put into the foster system. His life was in turmoil. He was continually yelled at and belittled at home. Ken was tired of crying. No one cared, and there was no one with whom he could share his problem. That’s when he came up with his clever plan. His school friend was a hippie, and his parents traveled a lot. They were called Gypsies. He heard that they were headed to California. So, Ken told them about his terrible life and asked if they would give him a ride. They were glad to help.

That exciting morning, he just did his usual thing. He left for school and instead went to California. He didn’t mind leaving all his stuff behind—he really didn’t have much anyway. His foster parents didn’t even care that he left.

In California, Ken lived on the beach and worked for fishermen, and whoever else needed help. He always had enough to eat and something to do. He had his fellow beach bums, but he was still alone inside. His heart was still empty. He longed for love.

Ken lived on the beach for a year and a half and then hitchhiked to Arizona. There he found a home in a homeless shelter and got a job. He did well and soon was on his own, but his search for love took him down the wrong roads. Ken really wanted to be married to a loving wife and have a family, but the girl he married did not marry him because of love. She was hurt, and Ken’s own hurt soul was attracted to her. They got married and all was well for a few years until he found out that his wife was seeing other men. His heart was broken, and his world was thrown into turmoil. Ken wanted desperately to provide security for the children that were born to them, and so he tried his best to stay together. He did not want to put his children through the life that he experienced. But after eight rough years, they got a divorce.

Ken moved on and tried to recover from the devastation of the divorce. His search for love brought him only more sadness and pain. Since Ken was hurt and unhappy, he found satisfaction in making others happy. He spent all his money on them, and when he had nothing more to offer, they left.

Now Ken is sitting in his pawn shop, alone, hurt, sad, and hiding. He found through his sad life that no one cared. Every time that he opened himself to love, he was always hurt. Deep down inside, he truly felt that God did not care. He lost hope in God, people, and last of all, he lost hope in love itself. That is why we were still visiting the dingy, smoke-stained shop after six years of very little apparent success. God kept bringing us back. He put in us a persistent love and relentless burden for this wounded soul. That is why we spent many hours hearing the same criticisms over and over. The same problems, the same confusion.

Nearly every month, he would fluctuate between hope and despair, love and hate, new life in God, and sadness and sin. We never knew what the next visit would bring. We could be swelling with hope and filled with blessing, or torn with angry words and sickened with dread. But we kept going back, and slowly he emerged from the pit of despair, and slowly allowed himself to be wrapped in the wonderful love of God and the glorious message of His redeeming grace. It was amazing to see the change in his life and to hear his ever-growing confidence in the love of Christ.

Today Ken loves the Lord. He is learning to walk with God. He has seen the love of God. He has found hope in God. He has experienced the unconditional love of God. He is still growing, and we are excited to see what God has for him.

I’m so glad that God brought Ken into my life. God had a plan for Ken and I. God wanted to show Ken that He loved him and that He would be there for him even when Josh turned his back on Him. God also wanted me to carry a burden in my youth. He knew how easily I would be distracted with money and fun. He knew that I needed a burden to carry, a soul to care for. He wanted me to be able to see beneath the shell of a hard soul and see a hurting child within. He wanted to give me a burden too big for me to carry so that I would learn to lean on Him. And most of all, He wanted to equip me to serve Him in broader ways.

Fellow Christians, open your lives to the work of God. Find an opportunity to love a hurting soul. Search out someone who needs a friend and love them, and wait and see what God has in store for you. Love until it hurts so badly that you don’t know what to do, and then turn to Jesus, who is there to help you through. God may be waiting for you to make the first step before He will use you. Your life is before you. You can choose to live a comfortable, happy life, or you can open yourself up to be hurt and find that after years pass, your life is overflowing with meaning and purpose. Jesus opened Himself to the pain and anguish of this world, and only through that do we have hope. He is asking us to follow His example, to open ourselves to pain so that others can have hope. And as He was glorified, so will we be glorified, in some measure, someday, and we will never regret the pain that we faced.

“میری دکان سے باہر نکل جاؤ! مجھے تم جیسے لوگوں کی یہاں ضرورت نہیں! اور دوبارہ کبھی مت آنا!” جب میں نے چیختے ہوئے آدمی کی تاریک، غصّے سے بھرپور آنکھوں میں دیکھا تو میرے ہونٹ لرز اُٹھے۔ میں نے بے اختیار آنسو چھپاتے ہوئے محسوس کیا کہ مجھے پھر سے اس آدمی کو چھوڑنا پڑے گا جس سے میں محبت کرتی تھی۔ ساری رات مجھے لگ رہا تھا کہ یہ ہونے والا ہے، اور میں نے اسے ہونے سے روکنے کی پوری کوشش کی تھی۔ ایک آخری کوشش میں میں نے دبے لہجے میں زور دے کر کہا، “کین، ہم نہیں چاہتے کہ ...” مگر پھر سے مجھے بے دردی سے کاٹ دیا گیا۔ کندھوں کو جھکائے اور نظر نیچی کرکے میں اس کے تنگ، گروی رکھنے والے دکانداری کے محدود حصے سے باہر نکلنے کے لیے مڑی، اس کی بڑھتی ہوئی آواز میری آخری امیدِ آرام کو دبا رہی تھی۔

دھواں کی باقی ماندہ بو اور اس کی غصّہ بھری آواز میرے جذباتی طور پر اذیت زدہ ذہن کے کشیدہ خیالات کے ساتھ مل گئی جب میں آہستگی سے سٹریٹ پر چل رہی تھی۔ “تُو کیا سمجھتا ہے، جوش؟” میں نے اپنے وفادار، خاموش دوست سے پوچھا۔

“میں نہیں جانتا، ” اُس نے جواب دیا، اور ہم اپنے خیال کے مطابق ہونے والی بائبل سٹڈی کے نتیجے پر خاموش غم میں ڈوب گئے، اس خوفناک ردِ عمل کی کوئی وضاحت ڈھونڈتے ہوئے۔ ہم مختلف کیوں نہیں کر سکے؟ وہ سچ کیوں قبول نہیں کر سکا؟ ان چمکتی ہوئی آنکھوں کے پیچھے کیا تھا، اور اس کے ہمیشہ پہنے جانے والے ٹوپی کے نیچے کون سی یادیں چھپی تھیں؟

کین کا پیدا ہونا پینسلوینیا کے شُائلکل کے لہراتی پہاڑی علاقوں کے ایک دیہاتی فارم میں ہوا، جو ایک تجسس اور مہم جو چھوٹے لڑکے کے لیے زبردست جگہ تھی۔

جب کین چار سال کا تھا تو اس کے والدین علیحدہ ہو گئے۔ وہ اکثر اُن کی لڑائی سن چکا تھا، مگر اسے معلوم نہیں تھا کہ ماں اور باپ الگ بھی ہو سکتے ہیں۔ اس سے اُس کا دل ٹوٹ گیا اور اُس کی معصوم روح الجھن کا شکار ہو گئی۔ وہ نہیں جانتا تھا کہ اس دباؤ اور تبدیلی کو کیسے سنبھالنا ہے جو اس کی پرامن زندگی پر ڈال دی گئی تھی۔

اُس کی ماں کے جلدی سے اپنے سامان پیک کرنے، اسے اور اس کے بہن بھائیوں کو گاڑی میں بٹھانے اور دور ڈرائیو کر جانے کی دہشت اور الجھن اب بھی اُس کے ذہن میں گہرائی سے نقش ہے۔ یہ کوئی معنی نہیں رکھتا تھا! وہ کیوں گھر واپس نہیں جا سکتے تھے؟ اپنے چھوٹے، بدبودار اپارٹمنٹ کے باسی کمرے میں وہ پھپھوندی سے بھرے چھت کی طرف گھور کر بے انتہا سوچتا رہا کہ آخر کیا غلط ہو گیا۔

کین جلد ہی پوٹس ویل شہر میں اپنی نئی زندگی کے مطابق ہو گیا جس میں گاڑیاں، لوگ، اور فٹ پاتھ تھے، گائوں کی گائیں، مینڈک اور کیچڑ کے بجائے۔ مگر قسمت نے اُس نئی طرزِ زندگی کی جو معمولی سیکیورٹی فراہم کرتی تھی، اسے بھی بخشا نہیں۔ اس کی ماں اُس کا اور اس کے بہن بھائیوں کا مناسب خیال نہیں رکھ سکی، اور بچوں کو مختلف فرسٹ ہومز میں رکھ دیا گیا۔ یہ والد کو چھوڑنے سے بھی بدتر تھا! جو کپڑے وہ پہنے ہوتے تھے وہی اُس کے لیے مانوس چیزیں تھیں۔ ہر نئے خاندان نے اسے سمجھنے یا محبت کرنے کے بجائے مزید چلّانے، نفرت کرنے، اور مار پیٹ کرنے کا رویہ دکھایا۔ دہشت، آنسو، تنہائی، اور درد اُس کا ساتھ دیتے رہے۔

کین نے سوچا کہ جس دوسرے فرسٹ ہوم میں اسے رکھا گیا ہے وہ محفوظ، محبت بھرا گھر ہوگا۔ باپ لمبا اور مضبوط تھا اور نرمی ظاہر کرتا دکھائی دیا۔ ماں موٹی تھی، مگر اس کی دوستانہ مسکان نے اس کے خوف دور کر دیے۔ مگر پہلی رات، جب وہ کھانے کے لیے ہاتھ بڑھا کر ایک پیالہ پانی الٹ بیٹھا، اُس نے چیخ کر کہا کہ وہ بے وقعت ہے اور وہ خواہش کرتی ہے کہ وہ کبھی انہیں نہ ملتا۔ باپ نے ایسے کھانا جاری رکھا جیسے اُس نے سنا ہی نہ ہو یا اسے پرواہ نہ ہو۔ مضبوط آدمی نے اسے کیوں نہیں روکا؟

اُس شام، کین اپنے بڑے، اجنبی بستر میں رینگ کر گیا، پہلے ہی تنہائی میں رو رہا تھا، جب اُس نے ماں کو چلّاتے سنا۔ وہ جلدی سے بستر سے کودا اور کانپتے پیر لے کر دروازے کے پیچھے چھپ گیا۔ وہ غصّے سے چڑھ کر سیڑھیاں چڑھی، اور کین کو یقین تھا کہ وہ اُسے مارے گی۔ خوشی سے وہ صحن میں آگے بڑھ گئی۔ وہ اب بھی مار کھانے کے خوف سے اپنی چھپنے والی جگہ سے باہر آنے کے قابل نہیں تھا۔ اس نے آنسو پونچھتے ہوئے آہستگی سے جمعہ سکول میں سنی گئی ایک گیت کی ہلکی سی سرگوشی شروع کر دی: “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” وہ رک گیا اور سوچنے لگا، اور اس کا رونا بند ہو گیا۔ “تو پھر میں یہاں کیوں ہوں؟ ” وہ سوچنے لگا۔ “کیا میں نے کوئی غلط کام کیا ہے؟ خدا چھوٹے بچوں سے محبت نہیں کرتا۔ وہ گیت سچا نہیں ہے! اگر خدا مجھ سے محبت کرتا تو میں یہاں نہ ہوتا!” اسی نتیجے پر پہنچ کر وہ پھوٹ کر رونے لگا اور خدا پر امید کھو بیٹھا۔ وہ اگلی صبح اٹھا، پھر بھی دروازے کے پیچھے چھپا ہوا۔

رات کا اندھیرا کافی دیر سے چھا چکا تھا، اور میرا خاندان ہمارے پرانے فارم ہاؤس میں پرسکون نیند میں تھا۔ میں کین کی روُح کے لیے روتی ہوئی سو گئی، روتی کیونکہ مجھے معلوم نہیں تھا کیا کرنا ہے، روتی کیونکہ وہ آدمی جسے میں خدا کے ساتھ سکون میں دیکھنا چاہتی تھی، مجھ سے نفرت کرتا تھا۔

کین نے سوالات کی بارش جاری رکھی۔ “خدا اچھا کیسے ہو سکتا ہے اور اتنا برا کیوں ہونے دیتا ہے؟ خدا بچوں کو تکلیف کیسے ہونے دے سکتا ہے؟” میں نے سنا جب وہ وہی باتیں دوہرا رہا تھا جو میں نے پہلے بھی کئی بار سنی تھیں، مجھے بولنے کا موقع نہ دیتے ہوئے۔

دوبارہ وقت تھا جانے کا، اور میں جانے پر خوش تھی۔ وہ ہمیں دروازے سے پیچھے کرتے ہوئے باتیں کرتا رہا۔ ایک بار پھر، میرا دوست اور میں سڑک پر چلے —تھکے ہوئے، مایوس، اور کبھی واپس نہ آنے کی خواہش لیے۔

کین 13 سال کا تھا، اور اس کی زندگی پہلے کی طرح اچھی نہیں تھی جب اسے فرسٹ سسٹم میں رکھا گیا تھا۔ اس کی زندگی انتشار کا شکار تھی۔ گھر میں مسلسل چلاتے اور کمتر سمجھائے جاتے تھے۔ کین رونا بند کر چکا تھا۔ کسی کو پرواہ نہیں تھی، اور شئیر کرنے کے لیے کوئی نہیں تھا۔ تب اس نے اپنا ہوشیار منصوبہ بنایا۔ اس کا اسکول کا ایک دوست ایک ہپی تھا، جن کے والدین بہت سفر کرتے تھے۔ انہیں جِپسی کہا جاتا تھا۔ اس نے سنا کہ وہ کیلیفورنیا جا رہے ہیں۔ تو کین نے انہیں اپنی وحشتناک زندگی کے بارے میں بتایا اور پوچھا کیا وہ اسے سواری دے سکتے ہیں۔ وہ خوشی سے مدد کرنے کو تیار ہو گئے۔

اُس پرجوش صبح، اُس نے معمول کے مطابق نکل کر اسکول کی بجائے کیلیفورنیا چلا گیا۔ اسے اپنا سامان پیچھے چھوڑنے کی پرواہ نہیں تھی—ویسے بھی اُس کے پاس زیادہ کچھ نہیں تھا۔ اس کے فرسٹ والدین کو بھی اس کے جانے کی پرواہ نہیں ہوئی۔

کیلیفورنیا میں، کین ساحل پر رہا اور مچھیر یوں کے لیے اور جو کوئی بھی مدد چاہتا تھا اس کے لیے کام کیا۔ اسے ہمیشہ کھانے کے لیے کافی اور کام کرنے کے لیے کچھ نہ کچھ مل جاتا۔ اس کے اپنے ساحلی ساتھی تھے، مگر وہ اندر سے پھر بھی اکیلا تھا۔ اس کا دل خالی تھا۔ وہ محبت کی تمنا کرتا تھا۔

کین نے ڈیڑھ سال ساحل پر گزارے اور پھر ہِچ ہائک کر کے ایریزونا چلا گیا۔ وہاں اسے ایک بے گھر شیلٹر میں گھر ملا اور نوکری مل گئی۔ وہ اچھا کر رہا تھا اور جلد ہی خود مختار ہو گیا، مگر اس کی محبت کی تلاش نے اُسے غلط راستوں پر ڈال دیا۔ کین واقعی محبت کرنے والی بیوی سے شادی کرنا چاہتا تھا اور خاندان چاہتا تھا، مگر جس لڑکی سے اس نے شادی کی وہ اسے محبت کے سبب نہیں ملی۔ وہ زخمی تھی، اور کین کی اپنی زخمی روح اُس کی طرف کھنچی۔ وہ شادی کے بندھن میں بندھ گئے اور کچھ سال اچھے گزرے جب تک کین کو پتہ چلا کہ اس کی بیوی دوسرے مردوں کو دیکھ رہی ہے۔ اس کا دل ٹوٹ گیا اور اس کی دنیا انتشار کا شکار ہو گئی۔ کین زبردست کوشش کرنا چاہتا تھا بچوں کے لیے سلامتی فراہم کرنے کی جو اُن سے پیدا ہوئے تھے، اسی لیے اس نے ساتھ رہنے کی پوری کوشش کی۔ وہ اپنے بچوں کو وہ زندگی دینا نہیں چاہتا تھا جو اس نے خود جھیلی تھی۔ مگر آٹھ سخت سالوں کے بعد، وہ طلاق لے بیٹھے۔

کین آگے بڑھا اور طلاق کے زخم سے بحالی کی کوشش کرنے لگا۔ محبت کی تلاش نے اسے صرف مزید غم اور درد دیا۔ چونکہ کین زخمی اور ناخوش تھا، اس نے دوسروں کو خوش کر کے خوشی حاصل کرنے کی طرف رجوع کیا۔ اس نے اپنی ساری رقم اُن پر خرچ کر دی، اور جب دینے کے لیے کچھ باقی نہ رہا تو وہ چھوڑ گئے۔

اب کین اپنے گروی رکھے گئے دکان میں بیٹھا ہے، اکیلا، زخمی، افسردہ، اور چھپا ہوا۔ اپنی اس دکھ بھری زندگی کے دوران اس نے پایا کہ کوئی پرواہ نہیں کرتا۔ ہر بار جب وہ محبت کے لیے خود کو کھولتا، وہ ہمیشہ زخمی ہوتا۔ اندر سے وہ واقعی محسوس کرتا تھا کہ خدا کو پرواہ نہیں ہے۔ اس نے خدا، لوگوں، اور آخر کار محبت کی خود امید کھو دی۔ اسی لیے ہم چھ سال کی کم نظر آنے والی کامیابی کے باوجود اس بدبودار، دھوئیں سے رنگے ہوے دکان کو بار بار دیکھنے آتے رہے۔ خدا ہمیں واپس لاتا رہا۔ اُس نے ہم میں ایک مستقل محبت اور اس زخمی روح کے لیے ایک مسلسل بوجھ رکھا۔ اسی لیے ہم نے کئی گھنٹے ایک جیسے تنقیدیں بار بار سنی۔ ایک ہی مسائل، ایک ہی الجھن۔

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

"Adrianna, vad är det för temperatur ute?" frågade Asher. Han och Adrianna satt vid bordet och gjorde skolarbete med sina syskon Emily och Kianna.

"Kanske runt 10 grader." Adrianna tittade slött på termometern. "Hej, det är 18 grader! Mamma, får vi äta lunch ute?"

Mamma tittade upp från diskhon. "Om ni gör ett bra jobb med skolarbetet tills dess får ni det," sa hon. "Och om ni blir klara före lunch får ni leka ute en stund i eftermiddag."

Asher gav ifrån sig ett hojt och började skriva fort. Flickorna log mot varandra och tog upp sina pennor.

Alla arbetade flitigt fram till lunchtid. Sedan gjorde Adrianna mackor medan Asher la kakor i påsar, Emily samlade ihop chipspåsar och Kianna sprang ner i källaren för att hämta några äpplen. De packade varsin lunch i en handelsväska och gick ut till sin picknickplats, en stor, platt sten i en glänta i skogen.

De åt snabbt, och sedan föreslog Adrianna: "Låt oss paddla kajak på dammen!"

"Jag antar att vi skulle kunna det," sa Asher långsamt. "Men sa inte mamma att Emily och Kianna är för små för att hantera kajakerna?"

"Åh, jo, det tror jag att hon gjorde. Nåväl, de kan väl leka i gungorna eller något," ryckte hon på axlarna.

"Jag tycker vi borde leka något som alla kan hjälpa till med," sa Asher. Han vände sig mot Emily och Kianna. "Vad vill ni göra?"

"Låt oss bygga en lekstuga!" föreslog Kianna.

"Ja, låt oss!" höll Emily med. "Du kan leta åt oss," sa hon till Asher.

"Och Adrianna kan vara mamman!" sa Kianna.

Adrianna stod med en rynkad panna. Lekstuga, verkligen! Hon var alldeles för gammal för det! "Jag ska paddla kajak," meddelade hon. "Ni kan få er lekstuga själva." Hon tog upp sin handelsväska och la i sin macka och sina kakpåsar. Hon kastade sitt äppelskal till hundarna och började gå mot huset.

"Adrianna, kan du snälla ta våra också?" bad Emily. "Du ska ju ändå till huset."

"Ni kan ta hand om era egna saker," ropade Adrianna tillbaka, irriterat. Hon slängde sin handelsväska på bänken i hopp om att smita ut ur huset innan mamma såg henne.

Hon hörde sin mammas röst. "Vänta, Adrianna, vad är det för fel? Ditt ansikte ser ut som ett åskväder!"

Adrianna suckade. Hon hade inte varit tillräckligt snabb. "Jag ville paddla kajak, men Asher vill inte," gnällde hon.

"Tja," sa mamma långsamt, "jag tror Asher kommer ihåg att de andra flickorna inte kan hantera kajaker än. Vad gör de?"

"De bygger en lekstuga. Jag är alldeles för gammal för det!" brast Adrianna ut.

Mamma log, "Varför tror du det?"

"Jag är säker på att inga flickor i min ålder gör sådant med sina små syskon."

"Är du säker på att du inte är självisk?" frågade mamma. "Ibland måste vi ge upp det vi vill ha så att andra kan bli glada."

Adrianna ryckte på axlarna och gick ut till förrådet för att hämta en kajak. Hon lyfte ner sin blå kajak från stället och bar den ner till dammen. Hon satte ihop paddeln, hoppade i sätet och puttade kajaken ut på vattnets släta yta. Hon suckade av behag. Det här var så mycket bättre än att bygga en lekstuga i skogen! Hon gjorde några varv runt dammen innan paddlingen började tappa fart. På något sätt var det inte lika roligt den här gången. Hon hörde Asher och flickorna skratta och ropa medan de lekte. Kanske hade mamma rätt, tänkte hon. Kanske skulle jag vara lyckligare om jag gav upp det jag vill så att vi alla kan leka tillsammans. Sakta paddlade hon mot dammkanten. Hon klev ur kajaken, drog upp den ur vattnet och vände den upp och ner för att torka. Bestämt gick hon ut ur hagarna för att hitta Asher och flickorna.

"Hej! Här kommer Adrianna!" ropade Emily lyckligt när Adrianna kom fram.

Adrianna log, "Det ser ut som om ni har nästan fått upp huset," sa hon uppmuntrande. "Vad behöver ni för att bli klara?"

"Vi behöver fortfarande en spis och något till en arbetsbänk," sa Kianna.

"Jag kan hjälpa er att hitta något," sa Adrianna. Tillsammans letade de i skogen och i förrådet efter brädor och stockar för att färdigställa huset. När det blev kväll och de gick in för kvällsmat var Adrianna mycket glad. Mamma hade haft rätt, tänkte hon. Det är roligare att ge upp mitt sätt och göra det som alla andra vill."

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

Divine Redeemer, Thee I bless;
I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

But O these wonders of Thy grace,
These nobler works of Thine,
These marvels sweeter far to trace,
These new births more divine:

This new-born glow of faith so strong,
This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

Kucintai Engkau dalam keelokan

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

“아드리아나, 밖에 온도 몇 도야?” 애셔가 물었다. 그는 형제자매인 에밀리와 키애나와 함께 탁자에 앉아 학교 공부를 하고 있었다.

“아마 50도쯤일 거야.” 아드리아나는 게으르게 온도계를 흘낏 보았다. “어머, 65도네! 엄마, 밖에서 점심 먹어도 돼요?”

엄마가 싱크대에서 고개를 들었다. “점심 시간까지 숙제를 잘 하면 그래도 된다.” 그녀가 말했다. “그리고 점심 전에 숙제를 끝내면 오후에 잠깐 밖에서 놀아도 돼.”

애셔는 환호성을 지르며 글씨를 빠르게 썼다. 소녀들은 서로 환하게 웃으며 연필을 집어 들었다.

모두 점심때까지 부지런히 일했다. 그러고는 아드리아나가 샌드위치를 만들고 애셔가 쿠키를 낱개 봉지에 담고, 에밀리는 감자칩 봉지를 모으고, 키애나는 지하실로 달려가 사과 몇 개를 가져왔다. 각자 점심을 쇼핑백에 넣고 숲속 공터의 큰 평평한 바위에 있는 소풍 장소로 나갔다.

그들은 빨리 먹고, 그러자 아드리아나가 제안했다. “연못에서 카약 탈래!”

“그럴 수도 있지,” 애셔가 느릿하게 말했다. “근데 엄마가 에밀리랑 키애나는 카약 다루기에는 아직 작다고 하지 않았어?”

“아, 그러네, 그랬나 봐. 음, 그럼 그애들은 그네나 타게 놔두자,” 그녀가 어깨를 으쓱했다.

“다 같이 할 수 있는 걸 하면 좋겠어,” 애셔가 말했다. 그는 에밀리와 키애나를 바라보며 물었다. “뭐 하고 싶어?”

“우리 놀이집 만들자!” 키애나가 제안했다.

“좋아, 하자!” 에밀리가 동의했다. “애셔는 우리를 위해 재료 찾기 해줘,” 그녀가 말했다.

“그리고 아드리아나는 엄마 역할 해!” 키애나가 말했다.

아드리아나는 얼굴에 찡그린 표정을 지었다. 놀이집이라니! 그녀는 그런 건 하기엔 너무 나이가 많았다! “나는 카약 탈 거야,” 그녀가 선언했다. “너희들 놀아.” 그녀는 쇼핑백을 집어 샌드위치와 쿠키 봉지를 넣었다. 사과 껍질을 개들에게 던져 주고 집으로 향했다.

“아드리아나, 우리 거도 가져가 줄래?” 에밀리가 애원했다. “어차피 집에 가는 거잖아.”

“네 물건은 네가 알아서 해,” 아드리아나는 짜증을 내며 소리쳤다. 그녀는 엄마가 보기 전에 집을 빠져나가려고 쇼핑백을 카운터에 떨어뜨렸다.

엄마의 목소리가 들렸다. “기다려, 아드리아나, 무슨 일이니? 얼굴이 천둥 번개 같구나!”

아드리아나는 한숨을 쉬었다. 그녀는 충분히 빨리 하지 못했다. “카약 타고 싶었는데 애셔가 안 가려고 해,” 그녀가 투덜거렸다.

“음,” 엄마가 천천히 말했다. “애셔는 다른 아이들이 아직 카약을 다룰 수 없다는 것을 기억하는 것 같구나. 얘네는 지금 뭐 하고 있니?”

“놀이집을 짓고 있어요. 저는 그런 거 하기엔 너무 나이가 많아요!” 아드리아나는 터져 나왔다.

엄마가 미소 지었다. “왜 그렇게 생각하니?”

“제 또래 여자애들은 동생들이랑 그런 거 안 할 걸요.”

“혹시 이기적인 건 아닌지 확신하니?” 엄마가 물었다. “때로는 다른 사람들이 기뻐하도록 우리가 원하는 것을 포기해야 할 때가 있어.”

아드리아나는 어깨를 으쓱하고 카약을 가지러 창고로 나갔다. 그녀는 파란 카약을 걸이에서 들어 올려 연못으로 끌고 갔다. 패들을 조립하고 좌석에 올라타 연못의 고요한 물 위로 카약을 밀어 넣었다. 그녀는 기쁨으로 한숨을 쉬었다. 이건 숲에서 놀이집을 짓는 것보다 훨씬 낫다! 그녀는 연못을 몇 바퀴 돌다가 패들이 느려지기 시작했다. 어쩐지 이번에는 재미가 덜했다. 그녀는 놀고 있는 애셔와 소녀들의 웃음소리와 외침을 들었다. 아마 엄마 말이 맞는지도 몰라, 그녀는 생각했다. 모두가 함께 놀 수 있게 내가 원하는 것을 포기하면 더 기쁠지도 몰라. 천천히 그녀는 연못 가장자리로 노를 저어 갔다. 카약에서 내려 물가에서 끌어낸 뒤 뒤집어 말렸다. 단단히 결심하고 목초지를 나와 애셔와 소녀들을 찾으러 걸어갔다.

“얘들아! 아드리아나 왔어!” 에밀리가 기쁘게 외쳤다. 아드리아나가 걸어오자.

아드리아나는 웃으며 말했다. “집은 거의 다 지어진 것 같네. 마무리하려면 뭐가 필요해?” 격려하는 어조로.

“우리 아직 난로랑 조리대 같은 게 필요해,” 키애나가 말했다.

“뭔가 찾아줄게,” 아드리아나가 말했다. 함께 그들은 놀이집을 완성하기 위해 숲과 창고에서 널빤지들과 통나무들을 찾아다녔다. 저녁 시간이 되어 집으로 들어가 저녁을 먹을 때, 아드리아나는 매우 기뻤다. 엄마 말이 옳았다고 생각했다. 내 방식만 고집하지 않고 모두가 원한 것을 하니 더 즐거웠다.
