Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Η ηθική αφορά τη σωστή και λανθασμένη συμπεριφορά. Η αγνότητα είναι η απαλλαγή από ηθικό σφάλμα ή ενοχή, χαρακτηρίζεται από αγνότητα και σεμνότητα, που είναι προσωπική ακεραιότητα. Η αγνότητα δεν περιέχει τίποτε που να μην ανήκει εκεί. Όπως υποδηλώνει ο τίτλος, αυτό το άρθρο θα αφορά το να κάνουμε το σωστό και να είμαστε απαλλαγμένοι από ηθικά σφάλματα και ενοχές, να ζούμε μια ζωή ακεραιότητας και να διατηρούμε το εσωτερικό και το εξωτερικό μας απαλλαγμένα από οτιδήποτε δεν ανήκει σωστά.

Παρατηρήστε τι λέγει η γραφή για την αγνότητα. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Το να είσαι ηθικά αγνός δεν θα συμβεί χωρίς ισχυρή αποφασιστικότητα και πειθαρχία. Πάντοτε έτσι ήταν, αλλά ακόμη περισσότερο σήμερα με την άνοδο της τεχνολογίας και τη διαθεσιμότητα του κακού στο άγγιγμα των δακτύλων μας.

Τα σεξουαλικά αμαρτήματα δεν είναι ξένα προς την εκκλησία. Στην πραγματικότητα, δεν είναι ξένα προς κανένα λαό οποιασδήποτε φυλής. Δεν μπορούμε να χαλαρώσουμε και να αφήσουμε την επιφυλακή μας, υποθέτοντας ότι τα παιδιά μας θα είναι ασφαλή από τα κακά της κοινωνίας και της ανθρώπινης φύσης μας. Πρέπει να δείξουμε με το παράδειγμα και να διδάξουμε τα παιδιά και τη νεολαία μας αν αναμένουμε να παραμείνουν καθαροί σε αυτή τη διεφθαρμένη κοινωνία. Δεν μπορούμε να υποθέτουμε ότι αν κάποιος ντύνεται με έναν συγκεκριμένο τρόπο, όλα είναι καλά και στο εσωτερικό του. Η ιστορία δεν εξιστορείται πλήρως από το εξωτερικό. Οι Φαρισαίοι έκαναν το εξωτερικό να φαίνεται καλό, ενώ το εσωτερικό ήταν γεμάτο διαφθορά. Ο Ιησούς είπε, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Και εμείς πρέπει να δώσουμε πρωτεύουσα προσοχή στα θέματα της καρδιάς. Όταν η καρδιά είναι καθαρή, τότε και το εξωτερικό θα μπορεί να καθαριστεί επίσης.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Η εσωτερική σκοτεινιά πάντα θα καταστρέφει τη κοινωνία και θα σκοτώνει σχέσεις—κάθε φορά.

Αυτό προορίζεται να είναι μήνυμα ελπίδας, όχι αποθάρρυνσης. Εάν έχετε ένα κρυφό σκοτεινό σημείο, εξομολογηθείτε το και απαλλαγείτε. Μπορείτε να είστε ελεύθεροι! Είναι δυνατόν να ελευθερωθείτε από τα νύχια του Σατανά και να ζήσετε μια ανοιχτή, διαφανή ζωή με χαρά στην ψυχή σας. Δεν χρειάζεται να περνάτε τη ζωή προσπαθώντας να κρύψετε το σκοτάδι του κακού. Ο Ιησούς θέλει να συγχωρήσει και να θεραπεύσει.

Ο Σατανάς είναι σκληρός. Στο John 10:10, ο Ιησούς είπε, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” όλες τις θεϊκές σχέσεις. Το ενδιαφέρον του είναι να διαλύσει το σπίτι σας, να καταστρέψει το σεβασμό σας, και να σας στείλει στην κολάση. Όλο αυτόν τον καιρό, σας δελεάζει μέσω της ηδονής της σάρκας σας, με το σπαθί του σηκωμένο για να δεσμεύσει και να σκοτώσει.

Το ηθικό αμάρτημα είναι τόσο ντροπιαστικό και δύσκολο να το παραδεχτεί κανείς. Το φυσιολογικό είναι να προσπαθούμε να κρυφτούμε όταν κάνουμε λάθος. Τα παιδιά που μαθαίνουν να κρύβουν τα λάθη νωρίς στη ζωή φυσιολογικά αναπτύσσονται σε νέους που κρύβουν πράγματα από γονείς, δασκάλους και ποιμένες. Αυτό το άτομο θα χρειαστεί να μάθει να είναι ανοιχτό και διαφανές, αλλιώς θα έρθει χρόνος που θα κρύβει πράγματα από τον σύντροφό του. Η κρυψίνοια έχει ως αποτέλεσμα μια διπλή ζωή και οδηγεί σε περισσότερη δέσμευση και σπασμένες σχέσεις. Άνθρωποι που έχουν κλειστές πόρτες σε κάποιες γωνιές της ζωής τους θα είναι ιδιοτελείς με τα τηλέφωνά τους και απρόθυμοι να μοιραστούν τους κωδικούς με έναν αξιόπιστο σύντροφο. Φαίνεται ότι εύκολα ξεχνάμε πόσο μάταιο είναι να κρύβουμε από τον Θεό. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Πώς μπορούμε να είμαστε τόσο αφελείς και ανόητοι ώστε να νομίζουμε ότι μπορούμε να κρύψουμε οτιδήποτε από τον Θεό; Ή να προχωρήσουμε ένα βήμα παραπέρα: γιατί θα θέλαμε να κρύψουμε κάτι απ' Αυτόν; Numbers 32:23 είναι ακόμη πολύ αληθινό, λέγοντας, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Ο Θεός σ' αγαπάει υπερβολικά για να σε αφήσει να συνεχίσεις να κρύβεις ό,τι χρειάζεται να βγει προς εξομολόγηση και συγχώρεση.

Τα σεξουαλικά αμαρτήματα είναι επίσης εξαιρετικά παραπλανητικά. Συμβαίνει συνήθως όπως το περιέγραψε ο Ιάκωβος στο πρώτο κεφάλαιο. Μας δελεάζουν, απομακρυνόμαστε, τραβιόμαστε σαν μαγνήτης εκτός κέντρου, νιώθουμε ένα κύμα επιθυμίας, βεβαιωνόμαστε ότι κανείς δεν κοιτάζει, σκεπάζουμε τα ίχνη μας, κάνουμε ένα βήμα πιο κοντά στο απαγορευμένο, νιώθουμε περισσότερη επιθυμία, και αρχίζουμε πολύ γρήγορα να χάνουμε τη λογική και την ορθή σκέψη, μη ικανοί να υπολογίσουμε τις συνέπειες, λίγο σαν μεθυσμένο άτομο, τότε συμβαίνει το James 1:15: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Το στίχο 16 λέει, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

Ο Ιάκωβος θα μας έλεγε να μην επιθυμούμε ό,τι δεν είναι δικό μας, ούτε καν ως υπόνοια. Η Βίβλος μας λέει να φεύγουμε από τρία πράγματα. Ένα από αυτά είναι η πορνεία, που μπορεί να επεκταθεί σε όλα τα σεξουαλικά αμαρτήματα. Μην παίζετε με αυτό· μην ρίξετε δεύτερη ματιά· φύγετε μακριά! Αντικαταστήστε αυτές τις σκέψεις με οικοδομητικές σκέψεις για τον Θεό και τον δρόμο Του. Τραγουδήστε έναν παλιό ύμνο· ευτυχώς δεν μπορούμε να σκεφτόμαστε δύο πράγματα ταυτόχρονα. Ό,τι κι αν χρειαστεί, φύγετε από αυτή την επιθυμία της σάρκας. Θα σας οδηγήσει πιο μακριά απ' ό,τι θέλετε να πάτε και θα κοστίσει περισσότερο απ' ό,τι θέλετε να πληρώσετε. Τρέξτε το φιλμ μέχρι το τέλος και ρωτήστε τον εαυτό σας, αν ακολουθήσω αυτό που με δελεάζει, θα έχω αυτό που θέλω; Ο Σατανάς πάντα υπόσχεται απόλαυση, αλλά μετά φέρνει πόνο. Θυμηθείτε, ο Σατανάς δεν έχει εφεύρει ποτέ μια απόλαυση· μόνο παίρνει ό,τι ο Θεός δημιούργησε ως καθαρό και καλό, το διαστρέφει και το προσφέρει πίσω με τη διαστρεβλωμένη του μορφή. Θυμηθείτε, το σπαθί του Σατανά είναι σηκωμένο για να σκοτώσει σε αυτό το σημείο. Φύγετε από τις κακές επιθυμίες!

Μην ακολουθείτε την επιθυμία σας. Η πορνογραφία είναι εξαιρετικά εθιστική και έχει παγιδέψει πολλούς ανθρώπους. Οι Promise Keepers ανέφεραν ότι το 65% των ανδρών στην έρευνά τους ήταν εθισμένοι. Ο εθισμός στην πορνογραφία είναι όπως το αλκοόλ ή τα ναρκωτικά. Μας λένε ότι ο εγκέφαλος ζητά ενδορφίνες να εκχυλιστούν σε αυτόν, είτε από εθισμό στο αλκοόλ, στα ναρκωτικά ή στην πορνογραφία. Τονίζω ξανά ότι οι άνδρες και οι γυναίκες που θα φτάσουν στη νίκη θα είναι εκείνοι που, όπως ο Δανιήλ παλιά, αποφασίζουν στην καρδιά τους να μην αχθοῦν/μολυνθούν.

Αυτό το θέμα απευθύνεται και στις αδελφές μας, και μερικές ερωτήσεις φαίνονται κατάλληλες. Τι υπάρχει κρυμμένο μέσα στη ζωή σας, προσεκτικά διπλωμένο και κρυμμένο; Έχουν οι απογοητεύσεις της ζωής προκαλέσει ένα κενό που κάνει τη λήψη ενός «συναισθηματικού Τάιλερ» να σας κάνει να αισθανθείτε καλύτερα για λίγο; Είναι η συναισθηματική σας σύνδεση ασφαλής εκεί όπου ο Θεός έχει σχεδιάσει να είναι;

Τα νεαρά κορίτσια θα πρέπει να διδαχθούν να αναπτύσσουν μια υγιή μετριοπάθεια προς τους άντρες. Όχι με αλαζονική στάση και ποτέ χωρίς χαμόγελο, αλλά επίσης όχι υπερβολικά ελεύθερα στη σχέση με τους νέους άντρες. Η κοινωνία μας είναι διαμορφωμένη ακριβώς αντίθετα, και από το νηπιαγωγείο τα αγόρια και τα κορίτσια πειράζονται για ειδικές φιλίες. Ως αποτέλεσμα, τα παιδιά μεγαλώνουν με λίγη ή καθόλου μετριοπάθεια. Η επικοινωνία με μηνύματα μεταξύ των φύλων πρέπει να αποφεύγεται εκτός οικογενειακών σχέσεων. Αυτό θα αναπτύξει μια συνήθεια στους νέους που μια μέρα θα χρειαστεί να σπάσει αν περιμένουν να ζήσουν μια ανοιχτή, διαφανή ζωή με σύζυγο. Σκεφτείτε το έτσι: θα θέλατε ο/η σύζυγός σας να συναναστρέφεται με το αντίθετο φύλο στα κοινωνικά μέσα;

Αδελφές, προσέξτε τι βιβλία διαβάζετε. Τα ρομαντικά μυθιστορήματα αμβλύνουν την επιθυμία για τον Λόγο του Θεού και δημιουργούν μη ρεαλιστικές προσδοκίες για τη συζυγική ζωή. Αυτά τα βιβλία δίνουν την ιδέα ότι ο σωστός άνδρας κάπου θα ήταν το κλειδί σας για την ολοκλήρωση και την ευτυχία στη ζωή. Μόνο ο Ιησούς μπορεί να γεμίσει το κενό που η αμαρτία έχει φέρει σε κάθε άνθρωπο σήμερα. Κανένας άντρας ή γυναίκα δεν θα μπορέσει ποτέ να δώσει την ασφάλεια και την ηρεμία της ψυχής που όλοι επιθυμούμε τόσο έντονα. Αυτός ο πόνος στην καρδιά δεν θα σβηστεί ποτέ με επιδέσεις ή παυσίπονα. Βοηθούν μόνο για μια στιγμή, και όταν φθαρούν, το κλάμα της καρδιάς είναι ακόμη πιο δυνατό. Τα ανθυγιεινά βιβλία αμβλύνουν τη γεύση για τα πράγματα του Θεού και αντί γι' αυτό δημιουργούν μια λαχτάρα για πρόχειρο φαγητό και παυσίπονα.

Ένα ακόμη μέλημα για τις αδελφές είναι ο χρόνος που περνάτε διαδικτυακά. Δεν υπάρχει τέλος στη σίτιση της λαχτάρας για κομψότητα, μοναδικότητα, γοητεία και ομορφιά. Μη αφήσετε αυτά τα πράγματα να γίνουν το κίνητρο της ζωής σας γιατί ποτέ δεν θα φωνάξουν «αρκετά» και δεν θα ικανοποιήσουν την ψυχή ούτε θα δείξουν στα παιδιά σας τη σωστή κατεύθυνση. Σκεφτείτε τον χρόνο που ξοδεύετε φιλοξενώντας πάρτι. Με τα χρόνια, έχω δει ονόματα ευκαιριών επιχειρήσεων και προϊόντων που έρχονται και φεύγουν, τα οποία πρέπει οπωσδήποτε να έχεις. Αλλά δυστυχώς, σε λίγα χρόνια δεν μπορούμε καν να θυμηθούμε αυτά τα ονόματα και, όλο αυτόν τον καιρό, τα παιδιά μεγαλώνανε και τώρα είναι ενήλικες. Σκεφτείτε τις πραγματικές ανάγκες στη ζωή σας και τις ευθύνες σας, και στη συνέχεια αποφασίστε τι θα φέρει αιώνιες επενδύσεις. Οι γυναίκες με παιδιά χρειάζεται να περιορίσουν τα χόμπι που τόσο απολαμβάνουν γιατί, αυτή τη στιγμή, είναι ευλογημένες με παιδιά που έχουν ψυχές που ποτέ δεν πεθαίνουν και ο χρόνος μαζί τους είναι μια αιώνια επένδυση. Θυμηθείτε ότι ο σύζυγός σας και τα παιδιά σας είναι πολύ πιο άξια του χρόνου σας από το να περνάτε ώρες σε άλλο πάρτι.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

Ο Θεός μας δημιούργησε έτσι ώστε όταν αγαπάμε τα πράγματα που αγαπά Εκείνος, η καρδιά μας να έχει ακόμη χώρο για να αγαπήσει περισσότερο. Όσο παιδιά, εγγόνια ή θεοσεβείς φίλους κι αν έχουμε, η καρδιά μας έχει ακόμη χώρο να αγαπήσει και άλλους. Αλλά τη στιγμή που αρχίζουμε να αγαπάμε όσα ο Θεός έχει απαγορεύσει, αρχίζει να αντικαθιστά και να καταστρέφει κάθε άλλη αγάπη, γεμίζοντας τις καρδιές μας με κενότητα, πόνο και μοναξιά, που οδηγεί σε πικρό τέλος.

Πολλοί άνδρες έχουν συνέλθει και είδαν την απόλυτη ανοησία του δρόμου που ακολούθησαν. Κάποιοι προσπάθησαν να κρύψουν την ακάθαρτη συμπεριφορά και τα κατάφεραν μέχρι αργά στη ζωή. Άλλοι το κράτησαν κρυφό μέχρι μετά τον θάνατό τους. Μια ερώτηση για σκέψη: Αξίζει; Φυσικά, η απάντηση είναι ένα ηχηρό ΟΧΙ!

Πόσο υπέροχο είναι να ζεις μια ανοιχτή ζωή χωρίς ενοχές και να έχεις ειρήνη με τον Θεό και τη βεβαιότητα των συγχωρεμένων αμαρτιών, ώστε μια μέρα να μας πάρουν έξω από αυτόν τον κακό κόσμο και να μας οδηγήσουν στην παρουσία του Αγίου Θεού μας.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

La morale riguarda il comportamento giusto e sbagliato. La purezza consiste nell'essere liberi da colpe o difetti morali, caratterizzata dalla castità, che è integrità personale. La purezza non contiene nulla che non le appartenga propriamente. Come suggerisce il titolo, questo articolo tratterà del fare il bene ed essere liberi da colpe e difetti morali, del vivere una vita di integrità e del mantenere il nostro interno e l'esterno liberi da qualsiasi cosa che non vi appartenga correttamente.

Nota ciò che le Scritture dicono sulla purezza. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Essere moralmente puri non avverrà senza forte determinazione e disciplina. È sempre stato così, ma ancor più oggi con l'avanzare della tecnologia e la disponibilità del male a portata di mano.

I peccati sessuali non sono estranei alla chiesa. In realtà, non sono estranei a nessun popolo di qualsiasi razza. Non possiamo rilassarci e abbassare la guardia pensando che i nostri figli saranno al sicuro dai mali della società e della nostra umanità. Dobbiamo mostrare con l'esempio e insegnare ai nostri figli e ai giovani se ci aspettiamo che rimangano puri in questa società corrotta. Non possiamo presumere che se una persona si veste in un certo modo, tutto vada bene dentro. La storia non è raccontata completamente dall'esterno. I farisei facevano apparire l'esterno buono, mentre l'interno era pieno di corruzione. Gesù disse: “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Anche noi dovremmo dare attenzione primaria alle questioni del cuore. Quando il cuore è pulito, anche l'esterno potrà essere purificato.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” L'oscurità interiore distruggerà sempre la comunione e ucciderà le relazioni—ogni volta.

Questo è inteso come un messaggio di speranza, non di scoraggiamento. Se hai un punto oscuro nascosto, confessa e liberatene. Puoi essere libero! È possibile essere liberi dalle grinfie di Satana e vivere una vita aperta e trasparente con gioia nell'anima. Non devi attraversare la vita cercando di nascondere l'oscurità del male. Gesù vuole perdonare e guarire.

Satana è crudele. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. Il suo interesse è rompere la tua casa, distruggere il tuo rispetto e mandarti all'inferno. Nel frattempo, ti lusinga attraverso la concupiscenza della carne, con la sua spada sguainata per legare e uccidere.

Il peccato morale è così vergognoso e difficile da ammettere. La cosa naturale è cercare di nascondersi quando facciamo del male. I bambini che imparano a nascondere il male fin da piccoli diventano naturalmente giovani che nascondono cose ai genitori, agli insegnanti e ai ministri. Questa persona dovrà imparare a essere aperta e trasparente, altrimenti arriverà il momento in cui nasconderà cose al suo compagno. Nascondere comporta una doppia vita e porta a più schiavitù e relazioni spezzate. Le persone che hanno porte chiuse in alcuni angoli della loro vita saranno gelose dei loro telefoni e riluttanti a condividere le password con un partner di fiducia. Sembra che dimentichiamo facilmente quanto sia futile nascondersi da Dio. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Come possiamo essere così ingenui e sciocchi da pensare di poter nascondere qualcosa a Dio? O andare oltre: Perché vorremmo nascondere qualcosa a Lui? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Dio ti ama troppo per lasciarti continuare a nascondere ciò che deve essere portato alla luce e perdonato.

I peccati sessuali sono anche estremamente ingannevoli. Di solito accade come lo ha descritto Giacomo nel capitolo uno. Siamo sedotti, attratti, tirati come da una calamita fuori centro, sentiamo un'ondata di desiderio, ci assicuriamo che nessuno stia guardando, copriamo le nostre tracce, ci avviciniamo al proibito, sentiamo più desiderio e cominciamo molto rapidamente a perdere il ragionamento e il pensiero sano, incapaci di calcolare le conseguenze molto simili a una persona intossicata, poi avviene James 1:15: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

Giacomo ci direbbe di non desiderare ciò che non ci appartiene, neppure un accenno. La Bibbia ci dice di fuggire da tre cose. Una di queste è la fornicazione, che può essere estesa a tutti i peccati sessuali. Non scherzarci; non dare un secondo sguardo; allontanati! Sostituisci quei pensieri con pensieri edificanti su Dio e sul suo modo. Canta un vecchio inno; fortunatamente non possiamo pensare a due cose contemporaneamente. Qualunque cosa ci voglia, fuggi da quel desiderio lussurioso. Ti porterà più lontano di quanto vuoi andare e costerà più di quanto sei disposto a pagare. Fai scorrere il nastro fino alla fine e chiediti: se seguo ciò per cui sono tentato, otterrò ciò che desidero? Satana promette sempre piacere, ma poi consegna dolore. Ricorda, Satana non ha mai inventato un piacere; prende solo ciò che Dio ha fatto puro e buono, lo perverte e lo offre nella sua forma pervertita. Ricorda, la spada di Satana è sguainata per uccidere a questo punto. Fuggi i desideri perversi!

Non seguire la tua lussuria. La pornografia è estremamente dipendente e ha incatenato molte persone. Promise Keepers ha detto che il 65% degli uomini nel loro sondaggio era dipendente. La dipendenza dalla pornografia è come l'alcol o la droga. Dicono che il cervello chiede che gli vengano versate endorfine, sia che si tratti di dipendenza da alcol, droghe o pornografia. Ribadisco che gli uomini e le donne che giungono alla vittoria saranno quelli che, come Daniele d'altri tempi, decidono nel cuore di non contaminarsi.

Questo argomento riguarda anche le nostre sorelle, e alcune domande sembrano appropriate. Cosa c'è dentro la tua vita che è ordinatamente riposto e nascosto? Le delusioni della vita hanno causato un vuoto che ti porta a prendere un 'paracetamolo emotivo' per sentirti meglio per un breve periodo? La tua connessione emotiva è sicura dove Dio ha previsto che sia?

Le ragazze dovrebbero imparare a sviluppare una riserva sana nei confronti degli uomini. Non con un atteggiamento altezzoso e mai un sorriso, ma neppure troppo libere nel rapportarsi ai giovani. La nostra società è esattamente orientata al contrario, e dalla scuola materna in poi, maschi e femmine vengono presi in giro per amicizie speciali. Di conseguenza, i bambini crescono con poca o nessuna riserva. Socializzare via messaggi tra i sessi dovrebbe essere evitato al di fuori delle relazioni familiari. Questo svilupperà un'abitudine nei giovani che un giorno dovrà essere spezzata se si aspettano di vivere una vita aperta e trasparente con un coniuge. Pensalo così: vorresti che il tuo coniuge socializzasse con il sesso opposto sui social media?

Sorelle, fate attenzione ai libri che leggete. I romanzi rosa intorpidiscono il desiderio della Parola di Dio e danno aspettative irrealistiche sulla vita coniugale. Questi libri suggeriscono che l'uomo giusto da qualche parte sarebbe la chiave della tua realizzazione e felicità nella vita. Solo Gesù può riempire il vuoto che il peccato ha portato in ogni essere umano oggi. Nessun uomo o donna potrà mai dare la sicurezza e la tranquillità dell'anima che tutti desideriamo così intensamente. Questo dolore nel cuore non sarà mai placato da cerotti o antidolorifici. Aiutano solo per un momento, e quando svaniscono, il grido del cuore è ancora più forte. Libri disonesti intorpidiscono il gusto per le cose di Dio e invece creano una brama per cibo spazzatura e antidolorifici.

Un'altra preoccupazione per le sorelle è la quantità di tempo che passate online. Non c'è fine nell'alimentare la brama di sfarzo, unicità, fascino e bellezza. Non lasciare che queste cose guidino la tua vita perché non grideranno mai 'basta' e non soddisferanno mai l'anima né indirizzeranno i tuoi figli nella giusta direzione. Considera il tempo che passi ad organizzare feste. Negli anni ho visto nomi andare e venire di opportunità di business e prodotti indispensabili. Ma ahimè, in pochi anni non ricordiamo neppure quei nomi e nel frattempo i bambini crescevano e ora sono adulti. Considera i bisogni reali nella tua vita e le tue responsabilità, poi decidi cosa porterà investimenti eterni. Le donne con figli devono limitare gli hobby che tanto amano perché, in questo momento, sono benedette con figli che hanno anime immortali e il tempo con loro è un investimento eterno. Ricorda che tuo marito e i tuoi figli sono molto più degni del tuo tempo che passare ore in un'altra festa.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

Dio ci ha creati in modo tale che quando amiamo le cose che Egli ama, il nostro cuore ha ancora spazio per amare di più. Non importa quanti figli, nipoti o amici pii abbiamo, i nostri cuori hanno ancora spazio per amare di più. Ma nel momento in cui cominciamo ad amare ciò che Dio ha proibito, questo inizia a sostituire e distruggere ogni altro amore, riempiendo i nostri cuori di vuoto, dolore e solitudine, che porta a una fine amara.

Molti uomini hanno fatto ritorno a sé stessi e visto l'assoluta stoltezza del cammino intrapreso. Alcuni hanno cercato di nascondere comportamenti impuri e ci sono riusciti fino a tarda età. Altri lo hanno tenuto nascosto fino a quando non se ne sono andati. Una domanda su cui riflettere: ne vale la pena? Naturalmente la risposta è un sonoro NO!

Quanto è meraviglioso vivere una vita aperta, libera da sensi di colpa, avere pace con Dio e l'assicurazione dei peccati perdonati, così che un giorno saremo tolti da questo mondo malvagio e introdotti nella presenza del nostro Santo Dio.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.

L'inverno del 1882 si svolse nella piccola cittadina meridionale di Tuscumbia, Alabama. Una felice e normale bambina di due anni si ammalò gravemente con una strana febbre. La febbre andava e veniva, andava e veniva, e tornava ancora. Il medico di famiglia temeva che la bambina sarebbe morta per lo sforzo, ma la bambina era forte e un giorno la febbre finalmente se ne andò per sempre. Il giorno dopo la madre fece scorrere una mano davanti al volto della figlia, ma la bambina non batté ciglio. I tentativi successivi non produssero risultati e un nuovo giorno si affacciò sulla famiglia con una figlia cieca.

Man mano che la bambina recuperava la forza per riprendere a giocare, la grande campana della cena rintoccò per tutti i dintorni, ma Helen non rispose. Altri rumori produssero risultati simili e la famiglia Keller giunse alla netta consapevolezza che la vita non sarebbe mai più stata la stessa. La maggior parte di noi potrebbe non affrontare mai le cupe circostanze che affrontò la famiglia di Helen Keller, ma ciascuno di noi sopporterà certamente difficoltà modellate appositamente dal nostro Dio.

La mente umana è una creazione sorprendente e intricata. Sebbene molti abbiano cercato di comprenderla, la sua capacità operativa rimane incomprensibile all'umanità. Non è poca meraviglia che una parte dell'intuizione più acuta sulla salute della mente sia rivelata nella Parola di Dio. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

La paura è l'oscuro avversario di una mente sana. Si erge sopra l'anima e prende in giro il santo con la sua derisione minacciosa. La paura può trasformare un prato assolato in un deserto solitario. Può rendere una grande celebrazione nuziale buia come una caverna e trasformare un banchetto degno di un re in una esperienza nauseante. È lo strumento più potente e devastante nell'impiego del diavolo. Nonostante molte dichiarazioni audaci, nessuno è esente dalla sua impugnatura. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) È la paura che sta per attaccare e spegnere tutta la prosperità dell'anima. Se intendiamo resisterle in questi giorni, dobbiamo sorgere con ogni diligenza in guerra di sfida.

Non dobbiamo guardare molto lontano per ammirare lo smantellamento e l'indebolimento della mente dell'uomo. I medicinali per la mente sono tra le prescrizioni principali consumate oggi in America. Questa non è un'accusa diretta nei confronti di individui che possono trovarsi nel bisogno di assistenza medica per controllare la propria mente. Ma non serve uno studioso per guardare all'obesità e considerare la dieta, per vedere adolescenti ribelli e collegarlo all'infrastruttura della casa, o per vedere i cuori (le menti) degli uomini venir meno e credere che la paura sia alla radice. Mentre alcuni possono padroneggiare totalmente la loro dieta, pochi possono vantare di essere genitori compiuti. Ancor meno sono coloro che non vengono, a volte, assaliti dalla paura. Sebbene l'orgoglio e il buon senso possano tenere l'uomo esteriore sotto controllo, rimanendo perfettamente calmo, l'uomo interiore, almeno a livello subconscio, deve fare i conti con la tensione. Gli americani amano proclamare il motto, "No fear!" ma il nostro consumo di medicinali racconta una storia diversa. Paolo non si dichiarò esente, poiché era “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

Di cosa abbiamo paura? Perdita, dolore e umiliazione. A nessuno piace perdere qualcosa che ha lottato per ottenere. A nessuno piace il dolore. A nessuno piace essere umiliato. Eppure, non dobbiamo leggere molto nelle Scritture per rendersi conto che queste sono spesso le vie che Dio usa per spingere ulteriormente i Suoi servi lungo il cammino verso la Sua somiglianza. Non esiste assicurazione sulla terra che possa garantire la vitalità della giovinezza, l'amore di una famiglia o il rispetto degli amici. Le cose che ci danno le più grandi avanguardie terrene sono tutte vulnerabili ai rischi di perdita. Perciò, abbiamo paura. Anche se restiamo a letto fino all'alba, non possiamo in alcun modo aumentare il nostro status né alleviare la perdita che Dio ha posto sulle nostre vite. Questa ansia non fa che aggravare il nostro dolore e aggiungere carburante alle nostre paure.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Qui sta la custodia dei nostri cuori e delle nostre menti: preghiera, pace e ringraziamento.

Come un abilissimo artigiano dobbiamo tessere con cura questi due passi delle Scritture insieme sul telaio della vita, perché sembra esserci una correlazione diretta tra il fruttuoso — potere, amore e mente sana — e le "radici" — preghiera, pace e gratitudine. Non vi sarà conquista delle nostre paure senza queste cose, e ogni società che è anemica a questi ingredienti sarà certamente handicappata.

La preghiera genera potere

Nella nostra condizione indebolita non possiamo comprendere la preghiera come dovremmo. È allora che dobbiamo affidarci a coloro che possono o forse allo Spirito, che makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Comunicare con il Capo Onnipotente dell'universo è un compito tremendamente audace. Molti amministrano la preghiera come un mero compito formale, cercando di essere perfettamente reverenti in essa. Questa non è comunione come con un amico, né è audace. È più adatto a rientrare nella descrizione della paura. La terapia rimediale per la paura è nello riversare tutte le nostre ansie, amarezza e lamentele sul nostro Dio. I santi di un tempo erano noti per versare veementemente le loro accuse e l'amarezza della loro anima davanti a Dio.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

Tutti questi riversarono audaci accuse e lamentele contro Dio in fervente preghiera e nessuno di loro lo offese. Al contrario, Dio non aveva dato loro lo spirito di paura ma di potere, e servono da nostri esempi. Fu il senza-fede Ahab a cui fu detto di chiedere a Dio un segno nei cieli o sulla terra. Nella sua pia risposta rifiutò di "tentare" Dio. Questa mancanza di audacia e abbondanza di paura è più tentante per Dio dell'abbondanza di amarezza nella nostra lamentela, perché “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

La pace genera amore

Siamo tutti a riposo con le cose che amiamo. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) Un fanciullo raggiante e sereno che è in pace con suo padre adora l'uomo e si sforza di imitarlo. Agli occhi teneri del ragazzo, il carattere del padre è senza difetti. La sua abilità è insuperabile. Anche la marca di veicolo che guida è la migliore, e lui imita ogni suo gesto. Anche se ogni padre conosce i limiti delle aspettative del figlio, tutti noi ci crogioliamo nella lealtà stagionale. È la conoscenza e la paura a minare questo amore leale. Un padre violento distruggerà tale stima infantile e la paura ne sarà il sostituto. Fu attraverso la paura meschina che il cattivo servo seppellì il suo talento e non commercio con esso. Ai suoi occhi il padrone era austero e da temere. Ma Dio non ci ha dato lo spirito di paura ma di amore.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) L'anima che è toccata da questo amore non può che imitarlo. È in grande pace con l'amore del Padre e gli occhi attraverso i quali egli vede il carattere del Padre possono soltanto richiedere replicazione. Per quanto terribili possano essere le circostanze in cui ci troviamo, questo spirito di amore e pace ci porterà attraverso qualunque opposizione possiamo incontrare sul sentiero della vita. Giacobbe non considerò nulla del duro servizio che doveva sopportare per Rachele; lo spirito d'amore verso Dio ci porrà al di sopra della paura dell'uomo e di tutto il male che un uomo può farci.

La riconoscenza genera una mente sana

Non dobbiamo studiare a lungo le anime felici per trovare sepolto nella base rocciosa di ciascuna una fondazione di gratitudine. Lo spirito di una mente sana, o tranquillità della mente, è un godimento pacifico della vita. Molto spesso siamo scoraggiati lungo il cammino quando i tratti del nostro ambiente non corrispondono al nostro gusto e alla nostra immaginazione. Una mente sobria, solida e riflessiva potrebbe evitare e smorzare tali nozioni sterili, eppure siamo tutti tentati di coltivare ingrata abbondanza. Non serve potenza cerebrale per esporre le cose che disprezziamo, poiché Satana è certo di ingigantire e delineare ogni dettaglio insoddisfacente che incontriamo. Ognuno di noi può pensarsi in una profonda caverna, ma dobbiamo ringraziarci fuori.

La paura di perdere salute, ricchezza, reputazione e felicità è il più grande ostacolo al suo conseguimento. Concentrarsi sul nostro dolore è invitare altro dolore. Analizzare costantemente la nostra vita per vedere se siamo soddisfatti è una strada sicura verso l'ingratitudine. Il mondo chiede continuamente: "Are we having fun yet?" La risposta è: "No". Per queste anime, la vita non sarà mai adeguata e dovranno andare in cerca di una soddisfazione maggiore che l'ultima non ha assicurato. È la paura di non ricevere la nostra giusta porzione nella vita che genera malcontento. Il malcontento produce più paura e la spirale discendente progredisce. Tale era la costernazione dell'anima che chiese a Cristo di parlare a suo fratello perché dividesse l'eredità con lui. Questo può essere un pensiero logico, ma non è favorevole a una mente sana e pacifica. Quest'anima offesa non ha radice in sé e sarà per sempre danneggiata in qualche modo e passerà i suoi giorni alla ricerca di un salvatore che venga e sistemi l'altra parte. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

Non esiste un livello terreno di raggiungimento o un ambiente perfetto che promuova una mente sana. Essa può essere assicurata solo attraverso preghiera, pace e riconoscenza. Questo può richiedere una certa riprogrammazione delle nostre menti per raggiungere le rientranze subconscie, ma dobbiamo seriosamente cingere i lombi della nostra mente ed esercitarla se mai speriamo di ottenere “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8
