Moral handler om rett og galt atferd. Renhet er å være fri for moralsk feil eller skyld, kjennetegnet av kyskhet, som er personlig integritet. Renhet inneholder ingenting som ikke hører hjemme der. Som tittelen antyder, skal denne artikkelen handle om å gjøre det som er rett og å være fri for moralsk feil og skyld, leve et liv i integritet og holde våre indre og ytre sider fri for alt som ikke riktig hører hjemme der.

Legg merke til hva Skriften sier om å være ren. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Å være moralsk ren skjer ikke uten sterk besluttsomhet og disiplin. Det har alltid vært slik, men enda mer i dag med teknologiens fremvekst og ondskap lett tilgjengelig ved fingertuppene våre.

Seksuelle synder er ikke fremmede for kirken. Faktisk er de ikke fremmede for noe folk eller noen rase. Vi kan ikke slappe av og senke garden og anta at barna våre vil være trygge mot samfunnets ondskap og vår menneskelighet. Vi må vise ved eksempel og lære barna og ungdommen vår hvis vi forventer at de skal holde seg rene i dette korrupte samfunnet. Vi kan ikke anta at dersom en person kler seg på en viss måte, så er alt i orden på innsiden. Historien fortelles ikke fullt ut av utsiden. Fariseerne fikk utsiden til å se bra ut, mens innsiden var full av fordervelse. Jesus sa, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Vi bør også gi hovedoppmerksomheten til hjertesaker. Når hjertet er rent, kan også utsiden bli renset.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Intern mørke vil alltid ødelegge fellesskap og drepe relasjoner—hver gang.

Dette er ment å være et budskap om håp, ikke motløshet. Hvis du har et skjult mørkt punkt, tilstå det og bli kvitt det. Du kan bli fri! Det er mulig å bli fri fra Satans klør og leve et åpent, gjennomsiktig liv med glede i din sjel. Du trenger ikke å gå gjennom livet og prøve å skjule ondskapens mørke. Jesus vil tilgi og helbrede.

Satan er grusom. I John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. Hans interesse er å bryte opp hjemmet ditt, ødelegge din respekt og sende deg til helvete. Hele tiden lokker han deg gjennom kjødet ditt sine lyster, med sitt sverd trukket for å binde og drepe deg.

Moralsk synd er så skammelig og vanskelig å innrømme. Det naturlige er å prøve å gjemme seg når vi gjør galt. Barn som lærer å skjule det de har gjort tidlig i livet, utvikler seg naturlig til ungdommer som skjuler ting for foreldre, lærere og forstandere. Denne personen vil måtte lære å være åpen og gjennomsiktig, ellers vil tiden komme da de skjuler ting for sin livsledsager. Å skjule fører til et dobbeltliv og leder til mer trelldom og ødelagte relasjoner. Mennesker som har lukkede dører i noen hjørner av livet sitt vil være besittende overfor telefonene sine og uvillige til å dele passordene med en betrodd partner. Det virker som vi lett glemmer hvor nytteløst det er å skjule fra Gud. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Hvordan kan vi være så naive og dumme å tro at vi kan skjule noe for Gud? Eller ta det et skritt videre: Hvorfor skulle vi ønske å skjule noe for Ham? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Gud elsker deg for mye til å la deg fortsette å skjule det som må bringes fram og bli tilgitt.

Seksuelle synder er også ekstremt villedende. Det skjer vanligvis slik James beskrev det i kapittel én. Vi blir fristet, bortdratt, dratt som en magnet av sentrum, føler en bølge av begjær, sørger for at ingen ser på, dekker sporene våre, tar et skritt nærmere det forbudte, føler mer begjær, og begynner veldig raskt å miste fornuft og sunn tenkning, ute av stand til å regne ut konsekvenser omtrent som en beruset person, så skjer James 1:15: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James ville sagt at vi ikke skal lengte etter det som ikke er vårt, ikke så mye som et hint. Bibelen sier at vi skal flykte fra tre ting. En av disse er hor, som kan utvides til alle seksuelle synder. Ikke leke med det; ikke gi det et ekstra blikk; kom deg bort fra det! Erstatt de tankene med oppbyggelige tanker om Gud og Hans vei. Syng en gammeldags salme; takk og pris kan vi ikke tenke på to ting samtidig. Hva enn som skal til, flykt fra det lystfulle begjæret. Det vil føre deg lenger enn du ønsker å gå og koste mer enn du vil betale. Spill filmen helt til slutten og spør deg selv, hvis jeg følger det jeg blir fristet til, får jeg det jeg ønsker? Satan lover alltid nytelse, men leverer smerte. Husk at Satan aldri har funnet opp en nytelse; han tar bare det Gud skapte som rent og godt, forvrenger det og tilbyr det tilbake i sin forvrengte form. Husk at Satans sverd er trukket for å drepe i dette øyeblikket. Flykt fra onde lyster!

Ikke følg din lyst. Pornografi er ekstremt avhengighetsskapende og har fanget mange. Promise Keepers sa at 65% av mennene i deres undersøkelse var avhengige. Pornofengsel er som alkohol eller narkotika. De sier at hjernen krever at endorfiner skal strømme inn, enten fra avhengighet til alkohol, narkotika eller porno. Jeg understreker igjen at menn og kvinner som når seier vil være de som, som Daniel i gamle dager, bestemmer i sitt hjerte å ikke gjøre seg urene.

Denne saken gjelder også våre søstre, og noen få spørsmål virker passende. Hva inne i livet ditt er pent gjemt bort og skjult? Har livets skuffelser forårsaket en tomhet som gjør at å ta en «emosjonell Tylenol» får deg til å føle deg bedre for en kort stund? Er din følelsesmessige forbindelse sikker der Gud har planlagt den å være?

Yngre jenter bør læres å utvikle en sunn reserve i forhold til menn. Ikke med en hovmodig holdning og aldri et smil, men heller ikke for frigjort i forholdet til unge menn. Samfunnet vårt er nøyaktig det motsatte, og fra barnehagen av blir gutter og jenter ertet for spesielle vennskap. Som et resultat vokser barn opp med liten eller ingen reserve. Sosialisering via meldinger mellom kjønn bør unngås utenfor familierelasjoner. Dette vil utvikle en vane hos ungdom som en dag må brytes hvis de forventer å leve et åpent, gjennomsiktig liv med en ektefelle. Tenk på det slik: ville du ønsket at din ektefelle sosialiserte med det motsatte kjønn på sosiale medier?

Søstre, vær forsiktige med hvilke bøker dere leser. Romantiske romaner bedøver lysten på Guds Ord og gir urealistiske forventninger til ekteskapet. Disse bøkene gir tanken om at den rette mannen et eller annet sted ville være nøkkelen til oppfyllelse og lykke i livet. Bare Jesus kan fylle hullet som synd har brakt til hvert menneske i dag. Ingen mann eller kvinne vil noen gang kunne gi den tryggheten og sjelens ro som vi alle ønsker så sterkt. Denne smerten i hjertet kan aldri slukkes med plaster eller smertestillende. De hjelper bare et øyeblikk, og når de går av, er hjertets rop enda høyere. Usunne bøker bedøver smaken for Guds ting, og skaper i stedet et begjær etter søppelmat og smertestillende.

En annen bekymring for søstre er hvor mye tid dere bruker på nettet. Det finnes ingen ende på å nære lengselen etter prakt, særegenhet, sjarm og skjønnhet. Ikke la disse tingene være drivkraften i livet ditt, for de vil aldri rope ut «nok» og vil ingenting gjøre for å tilfredsstille sjelen eller peke barna dine i riktig retning. Tenk over hvor mye tid du bruker på å være vertinne for selskap. I årenes løp har jeg sett navn komme og gå på forretningsmuligheter og produkter man må ha. Men akk, etter noen år kan vi ikke engang huske de navnene og barna vokste opp og er nå voksne. Vurder de virkelige behovene i livet ditt og ansvaret ditt, og bestem så hva som vil gi evige investeringer. Kvinner med barn må begrense hobbyene de liker så godt fordi de i dette øyeblikk er velsignet med barn som har udødelige sjeler, og tid med dem er en evig investering. Husk at din mann og dine barn er langt mer verdige din tid enn å bruke timer på enda en fest.

Den ene jeg elsker, den ene jeg hater.

Jo ærligere jeg navngir

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

Divine Redeemer, Thee I bless;
I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

But O these wonders of Thy grace,
These nobler works of Thine,
These marvels sweeter far to trace,
These new births more divine:

This new-born glow of faith so strong,
This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

Spring is my favorite time of the year. Everything is new. Hyacinths are trying their noble best to poke their buds through the cold constraint of the winter-bound earth. Migrating waterfowl bring new sounds as they honk and quack their way to their final nesting places. This year the spring peepers in our area were “winter peepers” as they feebly squeaked their greetings to the arriving spring in mid-February. Tree buds are swelling, waiting to burst forth in full glory.

Oh, the magnificence of God’s nature joining forces to proclaim the glory of new life. Surely it must have been during this exuberant time of the year when the Psalmist wrote, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). This display of new life springing from the earth is a beautiful representation of new life found in Christ Jesus. The wonders of the newness of life springing from the deadness of sin cannot be fully displayed by even the best show of God’s creation. It can only be experienced within the soul.

As I write this, I am flying 35,000 feet over the sub-Saharan desert land of Chad and Niger. The stark contrast between the landscape described in the previous paragraphs and the parched desert land hurrying by six miles below me is nearly beyond my comprehension. The dry earth begs for rain as livestock scrounge for anything green to fulfill their appetite. The vast dryness loudly proclaims a reminder of the millions of parched souls who have never heard of the “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Millions who never experienced Christ the fountain as described in the Hymn History article in this issue:

Oh! Christ He is the foutain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above:
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

At times a yearning stirs in my heart to live the relaxed, relational lifestyle experienced in these impoverished tribal communities. Family and friends are more important than calendars and commitments. As we read in the Sister to Sister article, commitments and busyness can bring us to the overload point when we feel we cannot handle anything more. Read more to learn how to take practical steps to avoid that breaking point.

Most people in this area are Muslims. As I write this, Muslims are in the middle of Ramadan, a month-long season of fasting. They fast from food and water every day from dawn to dusk, even though daytime temperatures exceed 110 degrees. Their rigorous fasting, along with stopping their work to pray many times a day, is driven by a fervent desire to seek forgiveness of sins and obtain enough merit to enter heaven. If they only knew that true grace and mercy comes from God through the salvation of his Son, Jesus Christ. Our works can never bring us into right standing with God. The writer of the article “How to Increase Your Faith” clearly points this out “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

As we plant our gardens and watch the trees burst forth in bloom, let us be reminded of the words of the prophet Isaiah, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Lente is my gunsteling tyd van die jaar. Alles is nuut. Hiensia's probeer hul edele bes om hul knoppe deur die koue, wintergebonde grond te stoot. Trekkende watervoëls bring nuwe geluide terwyl hulle gekwaak en geklak na hul laaste nesplekke beweeg. Hierdie jaar was die lente-peepers in ons omgewing “winter-peepers” toe hulle flou hul groete aan die aankomende lente in die middel van Februarie piep het. Boomknoppies swel en wag om in volle heerlikheid uit te bars.

O, die prag van God se natuur wat saamwerk om die heerlikheid van nuwe lewe te verkondig. Dit moet sekerlik in hierdie uitbundige tyd van die jaar gewees het toe die Psalmdigter geskryf het, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). Hierdie vertoning van nuwe lewe wat uit die aarde spruit is ’n pragtige voorstelling van die nuwe lewe wat in Christus Jesus gevind word. Die wonders van die nuutheid van lewe wat uit die dooies van sonde spruit, kan nie eers deur die beste skouspel van God se skepping ten volle uitgebeeld word nie. Dit kan net in die siel ervaar word.

Terwyl ek dit skryf, vlieg ek op 35 000 voet bo die sub-Sahara woestynland van Tsjad en Niger. Die skerpe kontras tussen die landskap wat in die vorige paragrawe beskryf is en die uitgedroogde woestynland wat ses myl onder my verbygly, is byna buite my begrip. Die droë aarde smeek vir reën terwyl vee enige iets groen uitkrap om hul ete te vervul. Die uitgestrekte droogte verklaar hardop ’n herinnering aan die miljoene dorstige siele wat nog nooit van die “well of water springing up into everlasting life” gehoor het nie (John 4:14). Miljoene wat Christus, die fontein, nog nooit ervaar het soos in die Liedgeskiedenis-artikel in hierdie uitgawe beskryf nie:

O! Christus Hy is die fontein,
Die diep soet put van Liefde!
Die strome op aarde wat ek geproe het,
Dieper sal ek bo drink:
Daar, tot ’n oseaan van volheid,
Strek sy barmhartigheid uit,
En heerlikheid—heerlikheid woon
In Immanuel se land.

Partykeer roer ’n verlange in my hart om die ontspanne, relationele lewenstyl te leef wat in hierdie verarmde stamgemeenskappe ervaar word. Familie en vriende is belangriker as kalenders en verpligtinge. Soos ons in die Sister to Sister-artikel lees, kan verpligtinge en besigheid ons tot die oorlaaipunt bring wanneer ons voel ons kan niks meer hanteer nie. Lees verder om te leer hoe om praktiese stappe te neem om daardie breekpunt te vermy.

Die meeste mense in hierdie gebied is Moslems. Terwyl ek dit skryf, is Moslems in die middel van Ramadan, ’n maandlange seisoen van vas. Hulle vas elke dag van dageraad tot skemer van voedsel en water, alhoewel dagtemperatures 110 grade oorskry. Hul streng vas, saam met die stilstaan van hul werk om baie kere per dag te bid, word gedryf deur ’n ywerige begeerte om vergifnis vir sondes te soek en genoeg verdienste te verkry om die hemel te betree. As hulle net geweet het dat ware genade en barmhartigheid van God deur die verlossing van sy Seun, Jesus Christus, kom. Ons werke kan ons nooit in regstelling met God bring nie. Die skrywer van die artikel “How to Increase Your Faith” wys dit duidelik uit: “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

Terwyl ons ons tuine plant en die bome sien uitbars in bloei, laat ons herinner word aan die woorde van die profeet Jesaja, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Seëninge aan almal,

Edward Martin

The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

1882년 겨울은 앨라배마 주의 작은 남부 도시 터스컴비아에서 찾아왔습니다. 행복하고 평범한 두 살배기 소녀가 이상한 열병으로 몹시 위중해졌습니다. 열은 왔다가 가고, 왔다가 가고, 다시 찾아왔습니다. 집안의 의사는 병의 부담으로 아이가 죽을까 두려워했지만 아이는 강인했고 마침내 어느 날 열은 완전히 사라졌습니다. 다음 날 어머니가 딸의 얼굴 앞에서 손을 휘저었지만 아이는 눈을 깜빡이지 않았습니다. 이후의 시도도 소용이 없었고 가족은 앞날이 결코 이전과 같지 않을 것이라는 사실을 냉혹하게 깨달았습니다.

헬렌 켈러의 가족이 겪은 비참한 처지와 같은 상황을 대부분의 우리는 결코 맞닥뜨리지 않을지 모릅니다. 그러나 우리 각자는 분명 우리 하나님께서 특별히 마련하신 고난을 견뎌야 할 것입니다.

인간의 마음은 놀랍고도 복잡한 피조물입니다. 많은 이들이 그것을 이해하려 애썼지만, 그 작동 능력은 인류에게 여전히 불가해합니다. 마음의 건강에 대한 가장 예리한 통찰 중 일부가 하나님의 말씀에 드러나 있다는 것은 결코 작은 경이가 아닙니다. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

두려움은 건전한 마음의 불길한 적수입니다. 그것은 영혼 위에 우뚝 서서 신자를 위협하며 조롱합니다. 두려움은 화창한 초원을 외로운 황야로 바꿀 수 있습니다. 웅장한 결혼 축하를 동굴처럼 어둡게 만들 수 있고, 왕에게 어울릴 연회를 구역질 나는 자리로 바꿀 수 있습니다. 그것은 마귀가 쓰는 가장 강력하고 파괴적인 도구입니다. 많은 대담한 주장에도 불구하고 그 권세로부터 면제된 자는 없습니다. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) 영혼의 모든 번영을 공격하고 소멸시키려 서 있는 자가 바로 두려움입니다. 우리가 이 시대에 그것을 저항하려면, 모든 부지런함으로 반항의 전쟁을 일으켜야 합니다.

인간 마음의 무장 해제와 약화를 보기 위해 멀리 볼 필요가 없습니다. 마음을 위한 약물 처방은 오늘날 미국에서 소비되는 주요 처방 중 하나입니다. 이는 자신의 마음을 통제하기 위해 의학적 도움을 받아야 하는 개인들에 대한 공격이 아닙니다. 그러나 비만을 보고 식단을 떠올리고, 반항하는 십대들을 보며 가정의 구조와 연결 지으며, 사람들의 마음이 무너지는 것을 보고 그 뿌리에 두려움이 있음을 믿는 데는 학자가 필요 없습니다. 어떤 이들은 식단을 완전히 통제할지 모르지만, 몇이나 훌륭한 부모라 자처할 수 있겠습니까. 더욱 적은 이들이 때때로 두려움에 시달리지 않는다고 말할 수 있습니다. 자만과 체면이 겉사람을 억제하고 완전히 침착하게 유지할지 모르나, 적어도 잠재의식 속에서 속사람은 그 긴장에 대처해야 합니다. 미국인들은 흔히 모토로 "겁 없어!"라고 주장하기 좋아하지만, 우리의 약물 소비는 다른 이야기를 들려줍니다. 바울도 예외가 아니었으니 그는 “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

우리는 무엇을 두려워합니까? 상실, 고통, 그리고 굴욕입니다. 누구도 얻기 위해 싸운 것을 잃는 것을 좋아하지 않습니다. 누구도 고통을 즐기지 않습니다. 누구도 굴욕을 사랑하지 않습니다. 그럼에도 성경을 조금만 읽어도 이러한 것들이 종종 하나님께서 그의 종들을 더 닮게 하시기 위해 사용하는 통로임을 깨닫게 됩니다. 세상에는 젊음의 활기, 가족의 사랑, 친구의 존경을 보장하는 보험이 없습니다. 우리에게 가장 큰 전위(前衛)를 제공하는 것들은 모두 상실의 위험에 취약합니다. 그러므로 우리는 두려워합니다. 우리가 새벽까지 잠자리에 누워 있어도 우리가 하나님께서 우리 삶에 두신 손실을 증가시키거나 덜어줄 수는 없습니다. 이러한 불안은 우리의 슬픔을 더할 뿐이며 두려움에 기름을 붓습니다.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) 여기에서 우리의 마음과 생각을 지키는 것은 기도, 평안, 그리고 감사입니다.

숙련된 장인이 직조틀 위에서 이 두 구절을 신중히 엮어야 하듯, 열매 있는 것들 — 능력, 사랑, 건전한 마음 — 과 뿌리 있는 것들 — 기도, 평안, 감사 — 사이에는 직접적인 상관관계가 있는 듯합니다. 이러한 것들이 없이는 우리의 두려움을 정복할 수 없으며, 이 요소들에 빈혈 증상을 보이는 모든 사회는 분명히 제약을 받을 것입니다.

기도는 능력을 낳는다

약해진 우리의 조건에서는 기도를 있어야 할 만큼 이해하지 못할 수 있습니다. 그럴 때 우리는 기도할 수 있는 이들이나 아마도 성령에 의지해야 합니다. 성령은 말로 형언할 수 없는 탄식으로 우리를 위하여 간구하신다고 했습니다. 우주 만유의 전능하신 머리와 교제하는 일은 엄청나게 담대한 과업입니다. 많은 이들이 기도를 단지 형식적인 임무로 집행하며 그 안에서 완전히 경건하려 애씁니다. 이것은 친구와의 교제가 아니며 담대함도 아닙니다. 오히려 두려움의 범주에 속하기 쉽습니다. 두려움에 대한 치료법은 우리의 모든 불안, 쓰라림, 불평을 하나님께 쏟아붓는 데 있습니다. 예전의 성도들은 자기들의 비난과 영혼의 쓰라림을 하나님께 격렬히 토로한 것으로 알려져 있습니다.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

이들 모두는 하나님께 대하여 담대하게 비난과 불평을 쏟아냈고 그 중 누구도 하나님을 범죄케 하지 않았습니다. 그 반대로 하나님은 그들에게 두려움의 영이 아니라 능력의 영을 주셨고 그들은 우리의 본이 됩니다. 표징을 하늘이나 땅에서 구하라고 들은 이는 불신앙의 아합이었습니다. 그는 경건한 답변에서 하나님을 "시험"하지 않겠다고 거절했습니다. 이러한 담대함의 결여와 두려움의 풍성함은 우리의 불평 속 쓰라림의 풍성함보다 하나님을 더 시험하는 것입니다. “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

평안은 사랑을 낳는다

우리는 사랑하는 것들과 함께 있을 때 모두 안식합니다. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) 아버지와 화목한 한 아이는 그 남자를 숭배하며 그를 본받으려 애씁니다. 소년의 부드러운 눈을 통해 아버지의 성품은 결점이 없어 보입니다. 그의 기술은 견줄 데 없고, 그가 운전하는 차의 브랜드조차 최고로 보이며 그의 모든 행동을 본받습니다. 모든 아버지가 아들의 기대의 한계를 알지만, 우리는 계절적인 충성심을 누립니다. 지식과 두려움이 이 충성된 사랑을 약화시킵니다. 학대하는 아버지는 그러한 어린 시절의 존경심을 파괴하고 그 자리를 두려움으로 대체할 것입니다. 악한 종이 달란트를 땅에 묻고 장사하지 않은 것도 바로 비굴한 두려움 때문이었습니다. 그의 눈에는 주인이 엄격하고 두려워할 존재였습니다. 그러나 하나님은 우리에게 두려움의 영을 주신 것이 아니라 사랑의 영을 주셨습니다.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) 이 사랑에 사로잡힌 영혼은 그것을 본받을 수밖에 없습니다. 그는 아버지의 사랑과 큰 평안 가운데 있고, 아버지의 성품을 보는 눈은 단지 모방을 불러일으킬 뿐입니다. 우리가 처한 상황이 아무리 절박하더라도 이 사랑과 평안의 영은 인생의 길에서 우리가 마주치는 어떠한 반대도 이겨내게 해 줄 것입니다. 야곱은 라헬을 위해 견뎌야 할 고된 봉사를 아무것도 아닌 것으로 여겼습니다; 하나님에 대한 사랑의 영은 우리를 사람의 두려움 위에 세우고 사람이 우리에게 가할 수 있는 모든 상처 위에 세울 것입니다.

감사는 건전한 정신을 낳는다

행복한 영혼들을 오래 관찰할 필요도 없이, 각 영혼의 기반 암반 속에 감사의 기초가 묻혀 있음을 알 수 있습니다. 건전한 마음의 영, 또는 마음의 고요함은 인생을 평화롭게 즐기는 것입니다. 우리의 환경의 형편이 우리의 기호와 상상에 부합하지 않을 때 우리는 자주 길을 잃습니다. 단지 온건하고 건실하며 사려 깊은 마음만으로도 이런 무익한 관념들을 제거하고 무력화할 수 있으나, 우리는 모두 끔찍한 감사하지 못함을 품도록 유혹받습니다. 우리가 경멸하는 것들을 드러내는 데는 두뇌가 필요치 않습니다. 사탄은 우리가 만나는 모든 불만족스러운 세부를 확대하고 윤곽을 그릴 것이기 때문입니다. 우리는 각자 스스로를 깊은 동굴로 몰아넣을 수 있지만, 우리는 스스로 감사함으로 빠져나와야 합니다.

건강, 부, 평판, 행복을 잃을지 모른다는 두려움이 그것을 확보하는 데 가장 큰 장애입니다. 고통에 집중하는 것은 더 많은 고통을 초대하는 것입니다. 우리가 채워지고 있는지 끊임없이 분석하는 것은 확실한 길이 ingratitude(감사 없음)로 이어집니다. 세상은 끊임없이 묻습니다, "우리는 이제 즐기고 있나?" 대답은 "아니오"입니다. 이러한 영혼들에게 인생은 결코 충분치 않을 것이고, 그들은 지난번에 얻지 못한 더 큰 충족을 찾아 방황해야 합니다. 우리가 삶에서 정당한 몫을 얻지 못하고 있다는 두려움이 불만을 낳습니다. 불만은 더 많은 두려움을 만들어내고, 하강하는 소용돌이가 진행됩니다. 이와 같은 자가 그리스도께 형제에게 말해 상속을 나누게 해 달라고 부탁한 영혼의 당혹이었습니다. 이것은 논리적 사고일 수 있으나 건전하고 평화로운 마음에 도움이 되지 않습니다. 이 불쾌한 영혼은 자기에게 뿌리가 없고 어떤 식으로든 영원히 부당함을 당할 것이며 다른 당사자를 고쳐줄 구세주를 찾아 평생을 보낼 것입니다. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

건전한 마음을 촉진할 지상의 어떤 수준의 성취나 완벽한 환경도 없습니다. 그것은 오직 기도, 평안, 감사로만 확보될 수 있습니다. 이것은 우리의 마음을 재프로그램하여 잠재의식의 심연까지 도달하게 할 필요가 있을지 모릅니다. 그러나 우리는 마음의 허리띠를 근신하게 동이고 그것들을 연습해야 하며 그래야만 “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)을 얻을 희망이라도 가질 수 있습니다.

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Moralisches Verhalten betrifft richtiges und falsches Handeln. Reinheit bedeutet frei von moralischem Fehler oder Schuld zu sein, gekennzeichnet durch Keuschheit, was persönliche Integrität ist. Reinheit enthält nichts, was dort nicht hingehört. Wie der Titel andeutet, wird es in diesem Artikel um richtiges Handeln und das Frei-Sein von moralischem Fehler und Schuld gehen, ein Leben in Integrität zu führen und unser Inneres und Äußeres frei von allem zu halten, was dort nicht hingehört.

Beachte, was die Schrift über Reinheit sagt. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Moralisch rein zu sein wird nicht ohne starken Willen und Disziplin geschehen. Es war schon immer so, doch heute noch mehr mit dem Aufstieg der Technologie und der Verfügbarkeit des Bösen in unseren Fingerspitzen.

Sexuelle Sünden sind der Kirche nicht fremd. Tatsächlich sind sie keinem Volk irgendwelcher Rasse fremd. Wir können uns nicht entspannen und unsere Wachsamkeit verlieren und annehmen, dass unsere Kinder vor den Übeln der Gesellschaft und unserer Menschlichkeit sicher sein werden. Wir müssen durch Beispiel vorangehen und unsere Kinder und Jugendlichen lehren, wenn wir erwarten, dass sie in dieser verdorbenen Gesellschaft rein bleiben. Wir dürfen nicht davon ausgehen, dass, wenn sich jemand auf eine bestimmte Weise kleidet, auch alles innerlich in Ordnung ist. Die Geschichte wird nicht vollständig durch das Äußere erzählt. Die Pharisäer ließen das Äußere gut aussehen, während das Innere voller Verderbnis war. Jesus sagte: “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Auch wir sollten primär Herzangelegenheiten Aufmerksamkeit schenken. Wenn das Herz rein ist, dann kann auch das Äußere gereinigt werden.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Innerliche Dunkelheit wird immer die Gemeinschaft zerstören und Beziehungen töten—jedes Mal.

Dies soll eine Botschaft der Hoffnung sein, nicht der Entmutigung. Wenn du einen versteckten dunklen Punkt hast, bekenne ihn und entferne ihn. Du kannst frei sein! Es ist möglich, frei von Satans Klauen zu sein und ein offenes, transparentes Leben mit Freude in deiner Seele zu führen. Du musst dein Leben nicht damit verbringen, die Dunkelheit des Bösen zu verbergen. Jesus will vergeben und heilen.

Satan ist grausam. In John 10:10 sagte Jesus: “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” alle gottesfürchtigen Beziehungen. Sein Interesse ist es, dein Heim auseinanderzubringen, deinen Respekt zu zerstören und dich zur Hölle zu schicken. Unterdessen lockt er dich durch die Begierde deines Fleisches, mit seinem gezückten Schwert, um dich zu binden und zu töten.

Moralische Sünde ist so beschämend und schwer zuzugeben. Das Natürliche ist zu versuchen, sich zu verstecken, wenn wir Unrecht tun. Kinder, die früh im Leben lernen, Fehlverhalten zu verbergen, entwickeln sich natürlicherweise zu Jugendlichen, die Dinge vor Eltern, Lehrern und Predigern verbergen. Diese Person wird lernen müssen, offen und transparent zu sein, sonst wird die Zeit kommen, in der sie Dinge vor ihrem Lebensgefährten verbergen wird. Verbergen führt zu einem Doppelleben und führt zu mehr Knechtschaft und zerbrochenen Beziehungen. Menschen, die in manchen Bereichen ihres Lebens geschlossene Türen haben, werden besitzergreifend mit ihren Handys sein und nicht bereit, ihre Passwörter mit einem vertrauten Partner zu teilen. Es scheint, wir vergessen leicht, wie aussichtslos es ist, sich vor Gott zu verbergen. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Wie können wir so naiv und töricht sein zu denken, wir könnten Gott etwas verbergen? Oder noch weiter: Warum sollten wir überhaupt etwas vor Ihm verbergen wollen? Numbers 32:23 ist weiterhin sehr wahr und sagt: “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Gott liebt dich zu sehr, um dir zu erlauben, weiterhin zu verbergen, was hervorgebracht und vergeben werden muss.

Sexuelle Sünden sind außerdem extrem täuschend. Meist geschieht es so, wie James es in Kapitel eins beschrieb. Wir werden verlockt, weggezogen, wie ein Magnet aus der Mitte gezogen, fühlen einen Ansturm der Begierde, stellen sicher, dass niemand zusieht, decken unsere Spuren, treten näher an das Verbotene, fühlen mehr Verlangen und beginnen sehr schnell, die Vernunft und gesundes Denken zu verlieren, unfähig, die Konsequenzen zu berechnen, ähnlich einem Betrunkenen, dann tritt James 1:15 ein: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Vers 16 sagt: “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James würde uns sagen, nicht nach dem zu begehren, was nicht unser ist, nicht einmal eine Andeutung davon. Die Bibel sagt uns, vor drei Dingen zu fliehen. Eines davon ist Unzucht, was auf alle sexuellen Sünden erweitert werden kann. Spiel nicht damit; wirf ihm keinen zweiten Blick zu; geh weg davon! Ersetze diese Gedanken durch aufbauende Gedanken über Gott und seinen Weg. Sing ein altes Lied; glücklicherweise können wir nicht an zwei Dinge gleichzeitig denken. Was immer nötig ist, fliehe vor dieser lüsternen Begierde. Sie wird dich weiter bringen, als du gehen willst, und mehr kosten, als du bezahlen willst. Spiele das Band bis zum Ende ab und frage dich, wenn ich der Versuchung folge, werde ich bekommen, was ich will? Satan verspricht immer Vergnügen, liefert dann aber Schmerz. Denk daran, Satan hat noch nie ein Vergnügen erfunden; er nimmt nur, was Gott rein und gut geschaffen hat, pervertiert es und bietet es in seiner pervertierten Form an. Denk daran, Satans Schwert ist in diesem Moment gezückt, um zu töten. Fliehe böse Begierden!

Folge nicht deiner Lust. Pornografie ist extrem süchtig machend und hat viele Menschen gefangen. Promise Keepers sagten, 65% der Männer in ihrer Umfrage seien abhängig. Pornosucht ist wie Alkohol- oder Drogenabhängigkeit. Man sagt uns, dass das Gehirn Endorphine fordert, ob durch Sucht nach Alkohol, Drogen oder Pornos. Ich betone erneut, dass die Männer und Frauen, die den Sieg erreichen, diejenigen sein werden, die, wie Daniel früher, in ihrem Herzen Vorsatz fassen, sich nicht zu verunreinigen.

Dieses Thema richtet sich auch an unsere Schwestern, und einige Fragen scheinen angebracht. Was in deinem Leben ist ordentlich verstaut und verborgen? Haben Enttäuschungen des Lebens eine Leere verursacht, die dich dazu bringt, ein „emotionales Tylenol“ zu nehmen, das dich für kurze Zeit besser fühlen lässt? Ist deine emotionale Bindung dort gesichert, wo Gott sie vorgesehen hat?

Junge Mädchen sollten gelehrt werden, mit Männern eine gesunde Zurückhaltung zu entwickeln. Nicht mit einer hochmütigen Haltung und nie einem Lächeln, aber auch nicht zu frei im Umgang mit jungen Männern. Unsere Gesellschaft ist genau gegensätzlich ausgerichtet, und vom Kindergarten an werden Jungen und Mädchen wegen besonderer Freundschaften gehänselt. Infolgedessen wachsen Kinder mit wenig bis keiner Zurückhaltung auf. Soziales Kontaktieren per Nachrichten zwischen den Geschlechtern sollte außerhalb familiärer Beziehungen vermieden werden. Dies wird bei Jugendlichen eine Gewohnheit entwickeln, die eines Tages gebrochen werden muss, wenn sie erwarten, ein offenes, transparentes Leben mit einem Ehepartner zu führen. Denk so: Würdest du wollen, dass dein Ehepartner auf sozialen Medien mit dem anderen Geschlecht sozialisiert?

Schwestern, seid vorsichtig, welche Bücher ihr lest. Liebesromane betäuben das Verlangen nach dem Wort Gottes und geben unrealistische Erwartungen an das Eheleben. Diese Bücher vermitteln die Idee, dass der richtige Mann irgendwo der Schlüssel zu Erfüllung und Glück im Leben wäre. Nur Jesus kann das Loch füllen, das die Sünde heute jedem Menschen gebracht hat. Kein Mann und keine Frau wird jemals die Sicherheit und die Seelenruhe geben können, die wir uns so sehr wünschen. Dieser Schmerz im Herzen wird niemals durch Pflaster oder Schmerzmittel gelöscht. Sie helfen nur einen Moment, und wenn sie nachlassen, ist der Ruf des Herzens noch lauter. Unheilsame Bücher betäuben den Geschmack für die Dinge Gottes und schaffen stattdessen ein Verlangen nach Junkfood und Schmerzmitteln.

Eine weitere Sorge für die Schwestern ist die Zeit, die ihr online verbringt. Es gibt kein Ende, die Gier nach Zierlichkeit, Einzigartigkeit, Charm und Schönheit zu füttern. Lass diese Dinge nicht der Antrieb deines Lebens sein, denn sie werden niemals „genug“ rufen und nichts tun, um die Seele zu befriedigen oder deine Kinder in die richtige Richtung zu weisen. Überlege, wie viel Zeit du für das Ausrichten von Partys aufwendest. Im Laufe der Jahre habe ich Namen gesehen kommen und gehen von Geschäftsmöglichkeiten und Produkten, die man unbedingt haben musste. Aber leider können wir in ein paar Jahren diese Namen nicht einmal mehr erinnern, und währenddessen wuchsen die Kinder und sind inzwischen Erwachsene. Überlege die wirklichen Bedürfnisse in deinem Leben und deine Verantwortlichkeiten und entscheide dann, welches ewige Investitionen bringen wird. Frauen mit Kindern müssen die Hobbys, die sie so sehr genießen, einschränken, weil sie in diesem Moment gesegnet sind mit Kindern, die unsterbliche Seelen haben, und Zeit mit ihnen ist eine ewige Investition. Denk daran, dass dein Mann und deine Kinder weit mehr würdig sind deiner Zeit als Stunden auf einer weiteren Party zu verbringen.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” Es erfordert Demut und Zerbrochenheit, unsere Bedürfnisse anzuerkennen, aber Zerbrochenheit ist der Schlüssel zum Sieg. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. Eine der umfassendsten Definitionen von Gnade ist unverdiente göttliche Hilfe, die Menschen zur Wiedergeburt und Heiligung gegeben wird. Wiedergeburt ist 'erlösende Gnade' und Heiligung ist 'verwandelnde Gnade.' Die Wahrheit ist, dass Gott den Demütigen 'verwandelnde Gnade' gibt. Diese Gnade verändert uns von innen nach außen und macht uns heilig. Dieser Aspekt der Gnade muss ebenso begehrt und gesucht werden wie die erlösende Gnade, als Gott uns rettete. Dies ist wahrscheinlich der einzelne wichtigste Schritt, um Süchte jeder Art zu überwinden. Sei demütig genug, es zu einem täglichen Gebet an Gott um seine verwandelnde Gnade zu machen. Jesus lehrte in Matthew 23:26, wo Er sagte: "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Prüfe deine Gedanken, Handlungen, Versuchungen, die Dinge, mit denen du kämpfst, Zorn, Lust, Stolz, Bitterkeit usw. Bist du so geistlich, wie du dich äußerlich darstellst? Entferne die Fassade und gib die Notwendigkeit von Hilfe zu.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. Wir sind so töricht zu denken, wir könnten das Böse verbergen. Wir können eine Weile verbergen, aber eines Tages werden unsere Taten nackt vor einem allwissenden Gott stehen. Warum sollten wir jetzt versuchen, etwas zu verbergen? Diese verborgenen Dinge können vor Gericht gebracht werden, und ein schuldfreies Leben kann heute Wirklichkeit werden. Sei transparent; es muss ein praktisches Ziel sein.

Tell yourself the truth. Wenn du versucht wirst, bedenke das Ende deiner lüsternen Begierde. Wirst du bekommen, was du willst? Wird dieses Verlangen befriedigt, oder wird es nur nach mehr verlangen? Wenn du deinen Bruder so sähe, wie er das tut, wonach du gehst, wie würde es aussehen? Wie wird es in dreißig Jahren aussehen, wenn du deiner bösen Begierde folgst? Wird es Freude oder Leid bringen? Wird es jemandem helfen, oder wird jemand anders verängstigt sein? Sag dir die Wahrheit, bevor du betrunken wirst und nicht mehr rational urteilen kannst.

Teach your eyes to bounce. Du kannst nicht kontrollieren, was du beim ersten Blick ansiehst, aber du kannst kontrollieren, was du ein zweites Mal ansiehst. Mach es zur Gewohnheit, bis es eine Routine wird, deine Augen in eine andere Richtung zu wenden, wann immer du etwas siehst, das zu unreinen Gedanken führt.

Teaching our children. Dies sollte uns von frühester Kindheit an sehr am Herzen liegen. Wenn wir unseren Kindern nicht beibringen, dass Gott uns nach seinem Ebenbild geschaffen hat, das rein gehalten werden muss, wird es jemand anderes sie lehren, geheimnisvoll zu sein und sie sich unrein fühlen zu lassen. Bleib nah bei deinen Kindern und lehre sie, während sie reifen.

Keep your emotions. Dies ist ein Schutz in unserer verdorbenen Gesellschaft. Je weiter du dich davon entfernst, desto verwundbarer wirst du für Verderbnis. Halte deinen Ehepartner an erster Stelle im Leben, denjenigen, mit dem du teilst und an den du emotional gebunden bist.

Flee lust and fornication. Lauf davon! Diese Begierden sind Süchte, die gebrochen werden müssen. Denk daran, was du nährst, wächst, und was du verhungerst, stirbt. Diese Süchte können gebrochen werden, aber du wirst die Beziehungen nähren müssen, die Gott dir gegeben hat, und die schädlichen verhungern lassen.

Gott hat uns so geschaffen, dass, wenn wir die Dinge lieben, die Er liebt, unser Herz noch Raum hat, mehr zu lieben. Egal wie viele Kinder, Enkelkinder oder gottesfürchtige Freunde wir haben, unsere Herzen haben noch Raum, mehr zu lieben. Aber in dem Moment, in dem wir anfangen, das zu lieben, was Gott verboten hat, beginnt es, alle andere Liebe zu ersetzen und zu zerstören, füllt unser Herz mit Leere, Schmerz und Einsamkeit, was zu einem bitteren Ende führt.

Mancher Mann ist zur Vernunft gekommen und hat die ungeheure Torheit des Weges gesehen, den er eingeschlagen hat. Einige versuchten, unreines Verhalten zu verbergen und hatten bis ins hohe Alter damit Erfolg. Andere hielten es versteckt, bis sie tot waren. Eine Frage zum Nachdenken: War es das wert? Natürlich ist die Antwort ein lautes NEIN!

Wie wunderbar ist es, ein offenes Leben frei von Schuld zu führen und Frieden mit Gott und die Gewissheit der vergebenen Sünden zu haben, sodass eines Tages wir aus dieser bösen Welt herausgenommen und in die Gegenwart unseres heiligen Gottes eingeführt werden.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Our spiritual forefathers had much to say on the many issues facing the American Mennonite church in their time, and we can still learn from the collected writings of these church leaders and brethren. We will look first at the hermeneutics of the early American Mennonite church, endeavoring to draw examples from which we, as 21st-century Christians, can learn.

First, the correct interpretation of Scripture was a matter of great importance to these earlier Christians. They had only recently emigrated away from a largely hostile area, where they had been constantly tested to the point of death on matters of faith and now faced a different set of challenges when confronted with peace and religious freedom. We will look at how they navigated these challenges by studying several of their doctrines and practices.

The Doctrine of Nonresistance

One matter that was well interpreted and applied by many of the early Mennonite writers is the principle and doctrine of the nonresistant Christian. Although many of their Anabaptist descendants of today still hold, to varying degrees, this doctrine, it is oftentimes not done with the clarity and solemnity of their forefathers. The early American Mennonites understood nonresistance as a foundational aspect of the Christian life, as it should be, and taught extensively on the practical application and appearance of nonresistance in the life of a believer. Their primary motivation for living peaceably and without malice toward one’s fellow man was the given example of Jesus. Christ typified the acceptable response to violence and ill-will: gentleness, meekness, as befitted one who is called a Lamb.

The Emphasis of Biblical Foundations

There was also a firm focus amongst early Mennonite writers against building doctrine on the writings of men. This emphasis comes through strongly in their works, as they quote Scripture extensively. They made their point by bringing in an example of Christ or by way of an applicable Scripture verse, rather than building on the sandy soil of a man’s opinions. One of the areas in which they did so was the matter of salvation.

Importance of Practical Salvation

We can learn much from the early Mennonites about the practical working out of salvation. First, salvation is portrayed as both an inward and an outward change. The inward is affected first through the working of the Holy Spirit in the willful sinner’s life. It is an important distinction that the sinner is willful. This position was contrary to most of the greater established churches of the time. If a sinner must be willful, then it implies that all men can willfully accept salvation, an idea that is fundamental in nature, if not always verbalized, to the church of today.

In the early Mennonites’ time, predestination as taught by Calvinism seems to have necessitated this emphasis on man’s ability to choose freely, which is still true today. There is also another flavoring of the “unwillingly saved” interpretation, and that comes from the aftereffects of the charismatic movement and the effect it has had on Mennonite and Amish circles. This “unwilling salvation” is not a matter of predestination, but rather is described as almost a coercive calling by the Spirit. It has been observed in several salvation testimonies where the testifiers recalled how they were completely comfortable in their lives of sin and debauchery when suddenly they would be struck down in the manner of Saul and could not help themselves but follow after God and give their lives to Him. There are numerous pitfalls with this dramatic understanding of conversion, namely that it absolves responsibility from the one converted for his decision to convert. This leads to a lack of counting the cost of Christianity, which is a death of oneself, a death of pride, and a death of favor with man. If the believer hops headfirst into Christianity, not reckoning that he must give up all these self-pleasing traits, how will he be able to grow spiritually if he cannot let go of his former vices? While this form of conversion may be genuine at the beginning, it does not often progress beyond the milk of the Word to the meat of which a mature Christian must partake. This maturing of a Christian is emphasized in writings ranging from those of Menno Simons up to Abraham Goshalk. It is also important for the sake of the church that the believer be firmly committed and engaged in the steady growth of his faith.

The Seriousness of a Pure Church

The idea of church to the early American Mennonite seems to have been a more serious thought, less individualistic than our current state. It is the pitiable state of nominal Christianity that the church has become a social organization with room for all sin and depravity.

It behooves us to consider closely the character of the church that Christ established and to note as well the character of the true churches, unspotted by apostasy and laxness. This character is, like Christ himself, simple and yet incredibly full of meaning and spiritual vitality.

The first aspect of the church to recognize is its pure state as the bride of Christ. Here again, we should consider the character of Christ. Did He ever give Himself space for sin? Do we find Him occasionally indulging in a brief enjoyment of a “guilty pleasure”? The understanding reader will agree that Christ was pure in His entirety, and so how else should the bride be with which He is to be intimately and eternally joined? To aid our minds in answering such a question, let us consider the earthly symbol of this heavenly union: that of a man and a woman joined together for life. This earthly union is recognized even by non-Christians as something set aside purely for the two individuals involved, a relationship and a sharing of each other that is not and never to be partaken of by anyone outside of the intimate union. This paints clearly for our earth-bound minds the mind of Christ, insomuch as that marriage is a symbol of Christ and His bride. The bride and Christ are for each other and give themselves to nothing and no one other.

Now that we can see the purity of the church, let us examine its practical working out amongst fallen man. If it is to be pure, then how are we to be a part of it? Here enters the need for a clear understanding of regeneration, a doctrine held in high regard by these Mennonite forefathers. They taught that the Spirit affects the spiritual washing and cleansing that will be made apparent in a changed state of thought and action in the believer. This change is still at variance with our fallen nature, but through continued surrender and a deep humility, the Spirit will fill the believer until the nature of sin becomes the dominated instead of the dominant. It is important to realize, however, that this victory over sin is brought into effect by the believer yielding his will and allowing the Spirit complete control.

Thus, a pure church is a surrendered, Spirit-filled group of believers who recognize in true humility that their power is not in any way linked to their own merit. The absence of pride, achieved only by the constant aid of the Spirit, gives further room for purification of the willing believer. In this way, we can see the Christian life in shoe leather.

The Teachings of Practical Christianity

The practicality of the early American Mennonite’s faith was continually on display. In his book, “Pride and Humility,” John M. Brenneman maintains that the outward appearance of a person is directly related to his inward heart, a view which extends as well to the actions of the individual. It is necessary to build on the beliefs of willful salvation, regeneration, and a pure church previously examined to frame the mindset of a Mennonite’s interactions in daily living.

To these serious-minded Christians, there was no difference in importance between the religious belief expressed on Sundays and the mundane actions of the rest of the week. This is evidenced by their general abstinence from political matters and other elements of a worldly nature that would infringe upon the beliefs they held. This put them in direct opposition to many of the churches of their day, where thrived two schools of thought: either that one’s earthly duties in a political manner were carried out completely separate from one’s faith, or that the accomplishment of these civic duties were incorporated in the will of God and so permissible for the Christian to engage in freely.

To the early American Mennonite, these types of stances betrayed the very meaning of his Christianity: he was a new person, alive only in the power of Christ that flowed through him. This influenced and directed every aspect of his life, from his business dealings, which were carried out in a way so as not to take advantage of any party involved, to his dress and manner of deportment, which was to be based on humility and plainness, to his method of conversing with his fellow man, which was to show a genuine concern for the spiritual well-being and eternal destiny.

Conclusion

The sum of all these colonial Mennonite beliefs was the doctrine of how to grow into a mature, humble, repentant, but spiritually powerful servant of God. He denied the allures of the world around him in favor of an eternal reward promised upon the purity of his faith and willing renunciation of the sin in which he had formerly lived. This example, lived out by believers like us, should inspire us to further press into the Kingdom of God, working out our faith in humility and repentance.
