A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

Salah satu hal yang indah menjadi seorang Kristen adalah menantikan hari ketika kita akan memandang dengan mata kepala sendiri keindahan agung Allah kita. Besar kemungkinan, kita semua pernah membayangkan secara mental seperti apa rupa Tuhan menurut kita, meskipun kita tahu bahwa khayalan paling liar sekalipun akan dilampaui. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). Alkitab penuh dengan gambaran deskriptif yang berusaha memberi kita sekilas pandang ke dalam kerajaan sorgawi. Lanskap di bukit-bukit kemuliaan, makhluk-makhluk yang menakjubkan yang tinggal di sana, dan yang terutama, Sang Pribadi Tertinggi di atas takhta, semua menantang usaha manusia untuk memahami dan meraih keindahan serta kemuliaan Allah kita.

Kadang-kadang kita mengagumi keindahan dalam sebuah lagu, sebuah karya seni, sebuah cerita, atau bahkan orang lain, tetapi Daud menggambarkan sukacita saat menatap keindahan Allah. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). Allah itu indah karena keunggulan-Nya menarik hati— karakter-Nya tanpa cela. Daud mengalami kesenangan yang datang dari mengenal dan mengalami Allah dalam segala kepenuhan-Nya. Bagaimana Allah mengungkapkan Keindahan-Nya?

Melalui Injil

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). Dalam kengerian Sengsara Kristus, kita menemukan sebuah keindahan yang mendalam dan khidmat— keindahan sebuah korban yang dipersembahkan oleh Juruselamat yang tak bercela bagi umat manusia yang tidak layak. Kadang-kadang jenis keindahan yang paling menggugah ditemukan dalam hal-hal yang tidak dapat kita pahami sepenuhnya.

Ada keindahan dalam tangisan Maria dan para murid di sekitar salib yang menahan tubuh tanpa nyawa dari Guru yang mereka kasihi. Namun ketika fajar terbit pada pagi kebangkitan, putus asa berubah menjadi pengharapan dan dukacita menjadi sukacita.

Kita melihat adegan yang indah di Bukit Zaitun empat puluh hari kemudian ketika para murid yang sama menatap rindu ke langit, menyaksikan Tuan mereka yang bangkit menghilang ke dalam sorga. Dengan sukacita besar, mereka kembali ke Yerusalem, dengan janji akan kedatangan-Nya menyala dalam hati mereka, untuk menantikan turunnya Roh Kudus.

Hari ini kita menantikan dengan penuh harap kedatangan Anak Allah dari sorga dengan kuasa dan kemuliaan besar untuk menyelesaikan karya keselamatan. Saat itulah kita akan memandang-Nya dalam segala kemegahan dan keindahan-Nya. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

Bagaimana kita, sebagai pembawa gambar Allah, memantulkan keindahan-Nya melalui Injil? Allah adalah Pribadi yang tidak diciptakan dan kekal, dan manusia diciptakan menurut gambar-Nya untuk memantulkan kemuliaan dan keindahan-Nya. Namun, keindahan ini ternoda oleh dosa dan tidak lagi menjadi perwakilan yang layak dari karakter Allah. Tetapi, ada penebusan! Sedikit sekali yang melampaui keindahan sebuah hidup yang pernah terluka dan hancur oleh dosa tetapi kini dipulihkan, ditebus, dan dibuat utuh oleh Injil. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Orang-orang atheis menantang keberadaan Allah, para ilmuwan memperdebatkan penciptaan menurut Alkitab, para sarjana mempertanyakan ketidakbersalahan Kitab Suci, tetapi tidak seorang pun dapat membantah kesaksian tentang sebuah hidup yang ditebus.

Melalui Penciptaan

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). Semua keindahan di dunia ciptaan berasal dari Allah. Sebuah matahari terbenam yang indah, sebuah mawar yang menawan, sebuah pohon redwood yang menjulang, sebuah puncak gunung yang agung, semuanya menjadi saksi keindahan Allah yang tergambar dalam ciptaan. Seperti rambu-rambu di sepanjang jalan yang menuntun kita ke tujuan, demikian pula ciptaan mengarahkan manusia kepada Allah sendiri. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). Pemberian ciptaan ini diberikan untuk memberi kita sekilas pandang tentang Sang Pencipta mereka.

Bagaimana kita, sebagai bagian dari ciptaan Allah, memantulkan keindahan kreatif-Nya? Meskipun kita tidak dapat mencipta sesuatu dari ketiadaan, Allah telah merancang kita untuk bersifat kreatif, menggunakan sumber daya ciptaan-Nya dan kemampuan intelektual kita untuk menjadikan hidup praktis. Rasa terpenuhi atas pekerjaan yang dilakukan dengan baik berasal dari ciptaan, di mana Allah memandang pekerjaan-Nya dan menyatakannya baik. Dalam upaya kita hidup tanpa berlebih-lebihan, terkadang kita gagal mengambil sukacita dalam hal-hal indah dalam hidup. Adalah benar dan baik serta selaras dengan bagaimana kita diciptakan untuk menemukan kesenangan dalam hal-hal yang indah. Orang-orang yang tidak takut Allah telah menggunakan anugerah kreativitas ini berkali-kali untuk tujuan jahat. Karena itu, terlebih lagi, marilah kita memuliakan Allah dengan menggunakan ciptaan-Nya dengan cara yang mencerminkan karakter-Nya.

Sebuah peringatan bagi semua yang mengasihi alam dan ciptaan (alami maupun buatan manusia): marilah kita berhati-hati agar tidak mengangkat keindahan duniawi di atas Sang Pencipta, yang mengarah pada penyembahan berhala. Senja pudar, pohon redwood tumbang, mawar layu, tubuh manusia kembali menjadi debu lagi, tetapi Allah tetap ada. Hidup dan segala keindahannya bermula dan berakhir pada Allah.

Melalui Musik dan Bunyi

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) Menurut kitab Wahyu, takhta Allah dikelilingi oleh bunyi: guntur dan kilat; pujian yang mengalir dari malaikat-malaikat, keempat makhluk dan dua puluh empat tua-tua, serta kerumunan besar yang tak terhitung; dan nyanyian baru oleh seratus empat puluh empat ribu.

Allah menciptakan keindahan bunyi untuk memuliakan diri-Nya dengan cara-cara yang tidak dapat dicapai oleh kata-kata semata. Kerumitan kreativitas-Nya tergambar dengan kuat dalam cara frekuensi bunyi yang berbeda-beda bergabung untuk menciptakan harmoni yang indah dan surgawi. Adalah menghormati Allah apabila manusia mengambil kesenangan dalam keindahan bunyi yang Ia ciptakan untuk kemuliaan-Nya. Orang yang mengasihi Allah akan tertarik kepada-Nya saat disenandungkan oleh bunyi-bunyi yang menyenangkan: umat Allah menyanyikan lagu-lagu Sion, doa-doa orang kudus, angin yang berbisik melalui puncak pohon, burung penyanyi memuji Penciptanya, gemuruh guntur, atau ketukan hujan yang sederhana di atas atap.

Bagaimana kita, sebagai alat-alat bunyi, memantulkan keindahan Allah melalui bunyi? Kita harus selalu berusaha mendengarkan dan menyerupai bunyi-bunyi serta harmoni sorga. Meskipun kita tidak akan pernah sepenuhnya mampu mencapai ini di bumi, hal itu harus menjadi usaha seumur hidup. Pertanyaan-pertanyaan telah diajukan, “Haruskah kita selalu berusaha meningkatkan kualitas bermusik kita?” dan “kapan kita mencapai ‘cukup baik’?” Kita tidak akan pernah mencapai kesempurnaan sorgawi, sehingga pertanyaannya sebaiknya, “Apakah kita memberikan yang terbaik bagi Allah?” Beberapa orang memiliki kemampuan bernyanyi lebih daripada orang lain, tetapi pertanyaannya tetap. “Apakah kita memberikan yang terbaik atau puas dengan korban yang rendah?” Marilah kita menjadi penghasil bunyi yang memuliakan Allah yang membawa sukacita ke hati Sang Pencipta!

Melalui Jemaat:

Alkitab berbicara secara luas tentang keindahan umat Allah. “Sion,” “Bait Suci,” “Gunung Allah,” “Yerusalem,” dan “Gereja” adalah ungkapan-ungkapan sinonim yang terjalin di seluruh Kitab Suci yang merujuk kepada tempat berdiamnya umat Allah di bumi. Adalah kehendak Allah bahwa keindahan-Nya tercermin dalam kehidupan umat-Nya. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Tidak ada yang lebih dekat di hati Allah daripada jemaat-Nya. Ketika anak-anak Israel melakukan perjalanan di padang gurun, mereka mendirikan tabernakel sebagai tempat bagi Allah untuk berdiam di tengah-tengah mereka. Ketika Salomo mendedikasikan bait Allah sebagai tempat kediaman Allah, Allah sangat berkenan dan 2 Chronicles 7:1 mengatakan kemuliaan TUHAN memenuhi bait itu. Bait itu dianggap Rumah TUHAN—Yesus sendiri merujuk kepadanya beberapa kali sebagai rumah Allah dan sangat bersemangat agar itu dijaga kudus.

Saat ini, baik kemah tabernakel maupun bait tidak lagi menjadi tempat kediaman Allah tetapi semangat ilahi-Nya terkonsentrasi pada jemaat Yesus Kristus. Di sinilah orang-orang yang benar-benar mengasihi-Nya dan rela menyerahkan nyawa bagi-Nya. Di sinilah orang-orang yang rela melepaskan hak-hak mereka sebagai individu dan menyerahkan diri pada sebuah tujuan yang lebih besar. Di sinilah banyak orang kudus telah menumpahkan darahnya demi Injil. Dan di sinilah suatu hari Sang Juruselamat akan datang kembali seperti yang Ia janjikan, dan akan membawa mempelai-Nya, jemaat, ke tempat kediaman kekal-Nya. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

Bagaimana kita, sebagai umat Allah, memantulkan keindahan-Nya dalam jemaat? Dengan diam bersama dalam kesatuan dan harmoni dengan kasih untuk semua orang, terutama seisi rumah Allah. Jemaat harus menjadi tempat di mana dunia dapat melihat sekilas apa yang berlangsung di sorga. Jemaat harus menjadi tempat di mana Kristus selalu ditinggikan sebagai Sang Penakluk yang menang atas dosa, maut, dan neraka.

Sayangnya, banyak orang menjadi bingung oleh kegagalan jemaat dan telah menjauh dari iman rasuli yang sejati. Terlepas dari kekecewaan kita, marilah kita “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) dan marilah kita terus maju. Kita tidak akan pernah memiliki panggilan yang lebih tinggi, dan tidak pernah peperangan yang lebih mulia untuk diperjuangkan.

Terakhir, bagaimana kita memantulkan keindahan-Nya dalam hidup kita? Dengan bersukacita di dalam Dia. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). Kepuasan terbesar dalam hidup datang dari menemukan kesenangan dalam membawa sukacita kepada hati Allah dengan bersukacita dalam apa yang Ia sukai dan mengasihi apa yang Ia kasihi. Janganlah kita pernah kehilangan rasa takjub akan keindahan Keselamatan kita!

It's incredible to me to see how God uses His people throughout history to bring glory to His name. He uses the weak things to confound the wise; the base things to bring to nothing the wisdom of earthly wise men. God uses physical weakness, hardship, loss, grief, toil, and pain to increase our spiritual treasures and build His Kingdom here on the earth!

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

Mi sembra incredibile vedere come Dio usi il Suo popolo nel corso della storia per rendere gloria al Suo nome. Egli usa le cose deboli per confondere i saggi; le cose umili per ridurre a nulla la sapienza degli uomini mondani. Dio usa la debolezza fisica, le sofferenze, la perdita, il dolore, il lavoro e il patimento per aumentare i nostri tesori spirituali e edificare il Suo Regno qui sulla terra!

Questo inno divenne prezioso per la mia famiglia e per me diversi anni fa, mentre attendevamo la nascita della nostra quarta bambina con difficoltà genetiche. Sapevamo che non sarebbe rimasta con noi a lungo. Morì quando aveva appena tre giorni. Dopo aver ricercato la storia di questo inno, rimasi stupito nello scoprire che l’uomo la cui vita aveva ispirato questo canto aveva perso otto dei suoi nove figli.

La storia di quest’uomo è notevole. I suoi 61 anni su questa terra furono segnati da dolore e perdita, persecuzione e prigionia. Eppure, la sua dedizione a Cristo fu straordinaria, e il suo zelo per Dio e per la predicazione del vangelo non venne meno fino all’ultimo giorno.

Samuel Rutherford, figlio di un contadino benestante, nacque nell’anno 1600. La sua vita ebbe inizio nel piccolo villaggio di Nisbet, in Scozia. Facendo uno sguardo sulla sua vita, notiamo la mano di Dio all’opera negli anni dell’infanzia di Samuel. A soli tre anni stava giocando con i suoi amici quando cadde nel pozzo del paese. Sua sorella e gli amici corsero a chiedere aiuto. Quando ritornarono, trovarono un Samuel molto fradicio seduto sull’erba accanto al pozzo. Gli chiesero come fosse uscito, e lui rispose: "Un bel uomo vestito di bianco venne e mi tirò fuori dal pozzo." La sua famiglia credette che Dio avesse mandato un angelo a salvarlo quel giorno.

Da quanto sappiamo di Samuel Rutherford, aveva due fratelli e una sorella. Fu mandato a scuola da piccolo e divenne uno studente molto diligente. Imparò così bene il latino e il greco che divenne in seguito professore. Sposò Eupham Hamilton intorno al 1624, poco dopo aver iniziato a insegnare all’Università di Edimburgo. A quel tempo Samuel non era ancora convertito e si preoccupava soltanto di perseguire i suoi obiettivi accademici.

Nel 1626, all’età di 26 anni, Samuel giunse a una fede chiara e salvifica nel Signore Gesù Cristo. Egli disse: "O ma Cristo ha un occhio salvifico. Quando Egli per la prima volta posò lo sguardo su di me, fui salvato. Gli costò soltanto uno sguardo per rendere l’inferno inutile per me." Da quel momento fu pieno di passione per predicare e parlare del suo Salvatore. Questo cambiamento di vita causò tale scalpore nell’università che Rutherford finì per dimettersi dalla cattedra.

Nel 1627 Samuel portò sua moglie e i due figli piccoli a Galloway, in Scozia, dove iniziò a pastoreggiare la piccola chiesa di Anwoth. Nel cominciare il suo ministero disse: "Ho ricevuto la commissione dal Reale e Principesco Maestro, il mio Signore Gesù, di predicare Cristo al popolo." La sua passione era la conversione della gente, e si dice che sembrasse sempre pregare, sempre predicare, sempre visitare gli ammalati, sempre insegnare e istruire, sempre scrivere o studiare. Il zelo con cui predicava e la sua cura per il benessere della sua congregazione ebbero grande effetto su di loro. Non solo loro: persone venivano dai paesi e villaggi circostanti per ascoltare la sua predicazione. Un amico riferì una volta: "Molte volte ho pensato che sarebbe volato fuori dal pulpito quando veniva a parlare di Gesù Cristo."

Samuel non fu estraneo al dolore e al cordoglio. Nel 1631, soltanto quattro anni dopo aver iniziato il suo lavoro come pastore, sua moglie morì. Anche i suoi due figli si ammalarono e uscirono da questo mondo. Nel 1636, dopo nove anni di predicazione, fu esiliato ad Aberdeen, dove gli fu proibito di predicare il vangelo. Questo fu un periodo molto difficile per lui, poiché gli mancavano profondamente la moglie, i figli e la sua congregazione, la Chiesa di Anwoth. Questo periodo della sua vita è infatti uno dei motivi per cui è così ricordato, perché iniziò a scrivere lettere alla sua gente di chiesa e agli amici. Delle 365 lettere che scrisse, 220 furono redatte durante questi 22 mesi di esilio.

Il governo alla fine cambiò, il che diede maggiore libertà ai dissenzienti Covenanter. Di conseguenza Rutherford tornò rapidamente al suo amato gregge di Anwoth. Circa un anno dopo, nell’autunno del 1639, lasciò di nuovo Anwoth di malavoglia, ma questa volta per assumere l’incarico di Professore di Divinità al St Mary's College di St. Andrews. Questo cambiamento fu difficile per lui, poiché di nuovo sentiva moltissimo la mancanza della sua congregazione. Scrive: "Il mio allontanamento dal mio gregge è per me così grave, che rende la mia vita un peso; non ebbi mai tanto desiderio di morire. Il Signore aiuti e sostenga questa triste argilla."

Dopo cinque mesi nella sua nuova posizione e dopo essere stato quasi dieci anni da solo, il quarantenne Samuel sposò Jean McMath. Insieme ebbero sette figli. Purtroppo, sei di loro morirono in tenera età e nell’infanzia. Solo una figlia di nome Agnes sopravvisse fino all’età adulta.

Rutherford continuò a essere un leader influente nel movimento nonconformista in Scozia per i successivi 20 anni fino al 1660. Con la morte di Cromwell, il governo del Commonwealth ebbe fine e Carlo II fu restaurato al potere. Ancora una volta, l’ira della monarchia si abbatté su Samuel. Fu convocato davanti al giudice e accusato di alto tradimento contro il governo per aver predicato la verità. Fu messo in prigione in attesa di esecuzione. Tuttavia, prima che il re potesse condannarlo a morte, Samuel si ammalò gravemente. Egli disse: "Ho già una citazione da un Giudice superiore, e devo rispondere alla mia prima citazione e quando verrà il vostro giorno io sarò dove pochi re e persone grandi vengono."

Tardi nel pomeriggio dell’ultimo giorno della sua vita, in risposta alla domanda: "Che pensate ora di Cristo?" rispose così: "Oh, che tutti i miei fratelli nella terra possano sapere che Maestro ho servito, e quale pace ho oggi! Dormirò in Cristo, e quando mi risveglierò sarò soddisfatto della Sua somiglianza. Questa notte chiuderà la porta, e poserà la mia ancora entro il velo, e me ne andrò in un sonno verso le cinque del mattino. Gloria! gloria al mio Creatore e mio Redentore in eterno! Vivrò e Lo adorerò. Oh, per braccia che Lo abbraccino! Oh, per un'arpa ben accordata! Gloria! la gloria dimora nella terra di Immanuel!" Queste parole furono udite da sua moglie, dalla figlia e dagli amici, e egli fu davvero con il suo Signore alle cinque del mattino.

Quasi due secoli dopo, Annie Ross Cousin, poetessa e autrice di inni scozzese e moglie di un ministro, fu ispirata dalla vita e dagli scritti di Samuel Rutherford. Riassunse la sua vita in un inno biografico, "The Sands of Time are Sinking". Questo inno fu pubblicato per la prima volta nel 1857 nel Christian Treasury. Delle diciannove strofe originali, soltanto quattro sono utilizzate nei nostri libri di inni. (in copia in grassetto)

Le sabbie del tempo stanno affondando,
L’alba del cielo si spezza,
Il mattino estivo che ho sospirato,
Il bel, dolce mattino si desta:
Buia, buia è stata la mezzanotte,
Ma l’aurora è a portata di mano,
E gloria—gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

2. Oh! bene è per sempre,
Oh! bene per sempre ancora
Il mio nido appeso in nessuna foresta
Di tutta questa sponda destinata alla morte!
Sì, lasciate che il vano mondo svanisca,
Come dal ponte della nave,
Mentre gloria—gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

3. Lì la Rosa Rossa di Sharon
Schiude il suo cuore più profondo.
E riempie l’aria del Cielo
Con un profumo inebriante;
Oh, poter contemplare il suo fiore,
Mentre dalla sua fragranza ventilato
Dove gloria—gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

4. Il Re là nella Sua bellezza,
Senza velo è visto:
Sarebbe un viaggio ben speso
Anche se sette morti stessero tra mezzo:
L’Agnello con il Suo bello esercito,
Sta sul Monte Sion;
E gloria—gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

5. Oh! Cristo Egli è la fonte,
Il profondo dolce pozzo d’Amore!
I ruscelli sulla terra che ho gustato,
Più profondamente berrò sopra;
Là, fino alla pienezza oceanica,
La Sua misericordia si espande,
E gloria—gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

6. Perfino Anwoth non era il cielo—
Perfino la predicazione non era Cristo;
E nella mia prigione battuta dal mare
Il mio Signore e io avemmo un appuntamento:
E sempre la mia nube di tempesta più oscura
Fu da un arcobaleno distesa,
Catturata dalla gloria che dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

7. Ma che Egli costruì un cielo
Del Suo amore eccedente,
Una piccola Nuova Gerusalemme,
Simile a quella lassù,—
“Signore, portami oltre l’acqua,”
Sarebbe stata la mia alta richiesta,
“Portami nel paese dell’amore,
Verso la terra di Immanuel.”

8. Ma i fiori hanno bisogno del fresco buio della notte,
Della luce della luna e della rugiada;
Così Cristo, da chi lo amava,
Il Suo splendore spesso ritirò;
E allora, a cagione dell’assenza,
Esaminavo la mia anima turbata—
Ma la gloria, senza ombra, risplende
Nella terra di Immanuel.

9. I piccoli uccelli di Anwoth,
si diceva fossero benedetti,—
Ora, accanto ad altari più felici,
vanno a costruire il mio nido:
Su questi non aleggia silenzio,
Non ci sono tombe intorno a loro,
Perché gloria, immortale, dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

10. Bella Anwoth sul Solway,
Per me tu resti cara!
Perfino dal ciglio del Cielo
Io verso di te lascio una lacrima.
Oh! se un’anima di Anwoth
Mi incontrasse alla destra di Dio,
Il mio Cielo sarà due Cieli,
Nella terra di Immanuel!

11. Ho lottato verso il Cielo,
Contro tempesta, vento e marea;—
Ora, come un viaggiatore stanco,
Che si appoggia alla sua guida,
Tra le ombre della sera,
Mentre affonda la sabbia che indugia la vita,
Saluto l’apparire della gloria
Dalla terra di Immanuel.

12. Acque profonde hanno attraversato il sentiero della vita,
La siepe di spine era acuta;
Ora queste sono tutte dietro di me,—
Oh, per un’arpa ben accordata!
Oh, unirsi all’Aleluia
Con quella banda trionfante,
Che cantano dove la gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel!

13. Con misericordia e con giudizio
La mia tela del tempo Egli tessé,
E sempre le rugiade del dolore
Furono illuminate dal Suo amore!
Benedico la mano che guidò,
Benedico il cuore che progettò,
Quando assetato dove la gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

14. Presto la coppa della gloria
Laverà i più amari affanni della terra,
Presto la spina del deserto
Fiorirà nella rosa dell’Eden:
La maledizione muterà in benedizione–
Il nome sulla terra che è bandito,
Sarà inciso sulla pietra bianca
Nella terra di Immanuel.

15. Oh! Io sono della mia Diletta,
E la mia Diletta è mia!
Porta un povero miserabile peccatore
Nella Sua “casa del vino”:
Io sto sul Suo merito,
Non conosco altra base,
Neppure dove la gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

16. Dormirò profondamente in Gesù,
Ricolmo della Sua somiglianza sorgerò,
Per vivere e per adorarLo,
Per vederLo con questi occhi:
Tra me e la risurrezione
Ma il Paradiso sta;
Allora—allora per dimorare nella gloria
Nella terra di Immanuel!

17. La sposa non guarda il suo vestito,
Ma il volto del suo caro Sposo;
Io non contemplerò la gloria,
Ma il mio Re di Grazia—
Non alla corona che Egli dona,
Ma alla Sua mano trafitta:
L’Agnello è tutta la gloria
Della terra di Immanuel.

18. Ho sopportato disprezzo e odio,
Ho sopportato torto e vergogna,
I superbi della terra mi hanno rimproverato,
Per il triplice benedetto nome di Cristo:
Dove Dio pose il Suo sigillo più bello
Loro hanno impresso il loro marchio più infame;
Ma il giudizio splende come mezzogiorno
Nella terra di Immanuel.

19. Mi hanno convocato davanti a loro,
Ma là io non posso venire,—
Il mio Signore dice, "Salite quassù",
Il mio Signore dice, "Benvenuto a casa!
Il mio Re ora al Suo trono bianco,
Comanda la mia presenza,
Dove gloria—gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

La bella melodia complementare per questo testo fu composta nei primi anni del 1800 da un musicista francese, Chretien D`Urhan. Si adatta bene alle parole dell’inno—il suo tempo solenne corrisponde alla solennità delle parole. La linea melodica ascendente dell’ultima frase si accorda perfettamente con la gioia attesa espressa dal ritornello—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

Concludendo questa storia dell’inno, continuiamo a stupirci della provvidenza di Dio nelle vite di coloro che ci hanno preceduto. Seguiamo Cristo con tutto il cuore ed essere vasi pronti all’uso del Maestro! Un’ultima citazione di Samuel Rutherford da portarci dietro. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

Le informazioni per questo articolo sono state tratte da 101 Hymn Stories, A Treasury of Hymns, Crichbaptist.org.

Spring is my favorite time of the year. Everything is new. Hyacinths are trying their noble best to poke their buds through the cold constraint of the winter-bound earth. Migrating waterfowl bring new sounds as they honk and quack their way to their final nesting places. This year the spring peepers in our area were “winter peepers” as they feebly squeaked their greetings to the arriving spring in mid-February. Tree buds are swelling, waiting to burst forth in full glory.

Oh, the magnificence of God’s nature joining forces to proclaim the glory of new life. Surely it must have been during this exuberant time of the year when the Psalmist wrote, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). This display of new life springing from the earth is a beautiful representation of new life found in Christ Jesus. The wonders of the newness of life springing from the deadness of sin cannot be fully displayed by even the best show of God’s creation. It can only be experienced within the soul.

As I write this, I am flying 35,000 feet over the sub-Saharan desert land of Chad and Niger. The stark contrast between the landscape described in the previous paragraphs and the parched desert land hurrying by six miles below me is nearly beyond my comprehension. The dry earth begs for rain as livestock scrounge for anything green to fulfill their appetite. The vast dryness loudly proclaims a reminder of the millions of parched souls who have never heard of the “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Millions who never experienced Christ the fountain as described in the Hymn History article in this issue:

Oh! Christ He is the foutain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above:
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

At times a yearning stirs in my heart to live the relaxed, relational lifestyle experienced in these impoverished tribal communities. Family and friends are more important than calendars and commitments. As we read in the Sister to Sister article, commitments and busyness can bring us to the overload point when we feel we cannot handle anything more. Read more to learn how to take practical steps to avoid that breaking point.

Most people in this area are Muslims. As I write this, Muslims are in the middle of Ramadan, a month-long season of fasting. They fast from food and water every day from dawn to dusk, even though daytime temperatures exceed 110 degrees. Their rigorous fasting, along with stopping their work to pray many times a day, is driven by a fervent desire to seek forgiveness of sins and obtain enough merit to enter heaven. If they only knew that true grace and mercy comes from God through the salvation of his Son, Jesus Christ. Our works can never bring us into right standing with God. The writer of the article “How to Increase Your Faith” clearly points this out “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

As we plant our gardens and watch the trees burst forth in bloom, let us be reminded of the words of the prophet Isaiah, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

Musim semi adalah waktu favorit saya dalam setahun. Segalanya terasa baru. Bunga hiacint berusaha sekuat tenaga menusukkan tunasnya melalui kekakuan tanah yang terikat musim dingin. Burung air migran membawa suara-suara baru saat mereka membunyikan honk dan krek mereka menuju tempat bersarang terakhir. Tahun ini, katak-katak peeper musim semi di daerah kami menjadi “peeper musim dingin” saat mereka dengan lemah menggerutu salam mereka kepada datangnya musim semi pada pertengahan Februari. Tunas-tunas pohon membengkak, menunggu untuk meletuskan diri dalam kemegahan penuh.

Oh, kemegahan ciptaan Tuhan yang bersatu untuk menyatakan kemuliaan kehidupan baru. Pasti pada waktu musim yang penuh semarak inilah Sang Pujangga menulis, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). Pertunjukan kehidupan baru yang muncul dari bumi ini adalah gambaran indah dari kehidupan baru yang ditemukan dalam Kristus Yesus. Keajaiban kebaruan hidup yang tumbuh dari kefanaan dosa tidak dapat sepenuhnya ditampilkan bahkan oleh pameran terbaik ciptaan Tuhan. Itu hanya dapat dialami dalam jiwa.

Saat saya menulis ini, saya sedang terbang pada ketinggian 35.000 kaki di atas tanah gurun sub-Sahara Chad dan Niger. Kontras yang tajam antara lanskap yang saya gambarkan pada paragraf sebelumnya dan tanah gurun yang kering yang terbentang di bawah saya sejauh enam mil hampir di luar kemampuan nalar saya. Tanah kering itu merintih untuk hujan sementara ternak mencari apa pun yang hijau untuk memenuhi selera mereka. Kekeringan yang luas itu dengan lantang mengingatkan jutaan jiwa yang kering yang tidak pernah mendengar tentang “the well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Jutaan yang tidak pernah mengalami Kristus sebagai sumber seperti yang digambarkan dalam artikel Sejarah Hymne di edisi ini:

Oh! Kristus Dia adalah mata air,
Sumur manis kasih yang dalam!
Aliran di bumi yang pernah kucicipi,
Lebih dalam kusyukuri di atas sana:
Di sana, menuju kelimpahan samudra,
Kasih karunia-Nya meluas,
Dan kemuliaan—kemuliaan berdiam
Di negeri Immanuel.

Terkadang terbit kerinduan dalam hati saya untuk menjalani gaya hidup santai yang relasional seperti yang dialami dalam komunitas suku yang miskin ini. Keluarga dan teman lebih penting daripada kalender dan kewajiban. Seperti yang kita baca dalam artikel Sister to Sister, komitmen dan kesibukan dapat membawa kita ke titik kelebihan muatan ketika kita merasa tidak dapat menangani apapun lagi. Bacalah lebih lanjut untuk mempelajari langkah-langkah praktis menghindari titik patah itu.

Kebanyakan orang di daerah ini beragama Islam. Saat saya menulis ini, umat Muslim sedang menjalani bulan Ramadan, musim puasa sebulan penuh. Mereka berpuasa dari makanan dan air setiap hari dari fajar hingga senja, meskipun suhu siang hari melampaui 110 derajat. Puasa mereka yang ketat, beserta berhentinya mereka dari bekerja untuk berdoa beberapa kali sehari, didorong oleh keinginan yang bersemangat untuk mencari pengampunan dosa dan memperoleh cukup pahala untuk masuk surga. Andai mereka tahu bahwa kasih karunia dan belas kasihan sejati berasal dari Allah melalui keselamatan oleh Anak-Nya, Yesus Kristus. Perbuatan kita tidak pernah dapat menempatkan kita dalam kondisi benar di hadapan Allah. Penulis artikel “How to Increase Your Faith” jelas menunjukkan hal ini: “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

Saat kita menanam kebun kita dan menyaksikan pohon-pohon meletuskan bunga, marilah kita diingatkan oleh kata-kata nabi Yesaya, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Berkat untuk semua,

Edward Martin

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

“Adrianna, joto nje ni kiasi gani?” aliuliza Asher. Yeye na Adrianna walikuwa wamekaa mezani wakifanya shule pamoja na ndugu zao Emily na Kianna.

“Pengine takriban 50.” Adrianna alitazama kwa uvivu kwenye thermometa. “Hey, ni 65 nyuzi! Mama, tunaweza kula mchana nje?”

Mama alitazama kutoka kwenye sinki. “Ikiwa mfanya kazi nzuri na shule zenu hadi wakati huo, mnaweza,” aliwaambia. “Na ikiwa mtamaliza shule kabla ya mchana, mnaweza kucheza nje kwa muda kidogo jioni hii.”

Asher aliruka kwa mfuriko na akaanza kuandika kwa kasi. Wasichana wakanagana kwa tabasamu na wakachukua penseli zao.

Kila mmoja alifanya kazi kwa bidii hadi wakati wa mchana. Kisha Adrianna alitengeneza sandwitchi wakati Asher alibweka biskuti kwenye mifuko, Emily alikusanya mifuko ya chipsi, na Kianna akaruka hadi basement kuchukua matunda machache. Kila mmoja aliweka chakula chao kwenye mfuko wa kununulia na wakaenda mahali pao pa picnic, jiwe kubwa, tambarare kwenye uwazi msituni.

Walila kwa haraka, kisha Adrianna alipendekeza, “Twende tukayaki kwenye bwawa!”

“Nadhani tunaweza,” alisema Asher polepole. “Lakini mama hakusema kuwa Emily na Kianna ni wadogo mno kushughulikia majaki?”

“Ah, ndiyo, nadhani alisema hivyo. Vizuri, zinaweza kucheza kwenye swingi au kitu kama hicho,” alibusha mabega.

“Nadhani tunapaswa kucheza kitu ambacho kila mtu anaweza kushiriki,” alisema Asher. Akamgeukia Emily na Kianna. “Mnataka kufanya nini?”

“Tujengeneze nyumba ya kuchezea!” alipendekeza Kianna.

“Ndiyo, tufanye!” Emily alikubali. “Wewe unaweza kutuwaangalia,” alisema kwa Asher.

“Na Adrianna anaweza kuwa mama!” alisema Kianna.

Adrianna alisimama akiwa na uso wa kukasirika. Nyumba ya kuchezea kweli! Yeye alikuwa mzee mno kwa hilo! “Ninakwenda kukayaki,” alitangaza. “Mnaweza kuwa na nyumba yenu ya kuchezea.” Alinasa mfuko wake wa kununulia na kuweka sandwitchi na mifuko ya biskuti ndani yake. Alitupa kidonda cha tofaa kwa mbwa na kuanza kuelekea nyumba.

“Adrianna, unaweza tafadhali kuchukua zake pia?” aliomba Emily. “Unakwenda nyumbani hata hivyo.”

“Mnaweza kuangalia vitu vyenu wenyewe,” Adrianna aliwajibu kwa hasira. Alitupa mfuko wake wa kununulia juu ya kaunteri, akitumaini kutoka nyumba kabla Mama hawamuone.

Alisikia sauti ya mama yake. “Subiri, Adrianna, kuna nini? Uso wako unaonekana kama dhoruba ya radi!”

Adrianna alitokwa na pumzi. Hakua haraka vya kutosha. “Nilitaka kwenda kukayaki, lakini Asher hataki,” alicherwa.

“Vizuri,” alisema Mama polepole, “nadhani Asher anakumbuka kuwa wasichana wengine hawawezi kushughulikia majaki bado. Wanafanya nini?”

“Wanakujenga nyumba ya kuchezea. Mimi ni mzee mno kwa hilo!” Adrianna alitoka kwa ghadhabu.

Mama alitabasamu, “Nini kinachokufanya ufikiri hivyo?”

“Nina hakika hakuna wasichana wa umri wangu wanafanya vitu kama hivyo na ndugu zao wadogo.”

“Una uhakika hujijali?” Mama aliuliza. “Wakati mwingine, tunahitaji kuacha kile tunachotaka ili wengine wawe na furaha.”

Adrianna alibusha mabega na kwenda kwenye gereji kuchukua kajaki. Alipandisha kajaki yake ya buluu kutoka kwenye rafu na kuileta chini hadi bwawani. Alipiga mkoko na kukaa kwenye kiti, akikandamiza kajaki kwenye uso laini wa maji. Alitikisa kwa furaha. Hii ilikuwa bora mno kuliko kujenga nyumba ya kuchezea msituni! Alizunguka mara kadhaa kwenye bwawa kabla mkoko wake kuanza kupungua. Kwa namna fulani haikuwa ya kufurahisha kama kawaida. Alisikia vicheko na matusi ya Asher na wasichana wanapocheza. Labda Mama alikuwa sawa, alifikiria. Labda ningeweza kufurahi zaidi nikiuza ninachotaka ili tuweze kucheza pamoja. Polepole alipiga mkoko hadi ukingoni mwa bwawa. Alistorosha nje ya kajaki, kuiita kutoka kwenye maji, na kuizungusha ili ikauke. Kwa azimio, alitoka kwenye maeneo ya malisho kutafuta Asher na wasichana.

“Hey! Hapa anakuja Adrianna!” Emily alipigia simu kwa furaha wakati Adrianna alipotembea hadi hapo.

Adrianna alitabasamu, “Inaonekana mnashikwa karibu na nyumba yenu tayari,” alisema kwa kuwahimiza. “Mnahitaji nini kukamilisha?”

“Bado tunahitaji jiko, na kitu cha kutumika kama kaunta,” alisema Kianna.

“Ninaweza kuwasaidia kupata kitu,” Adrianna aliwaambia. Pamoja walitafuta msituni na gereji mbao na magunia ya kuni kumalizia nyumba. Wakati saa ya chakula cha jioni ilipofika na walikwenda ndani kwa chakula cha jioni, Adrianna alikuwa mwenye furaha sana. Mama alikuwa sahihi, alifikiria. Ni kufurahisha zaidi kuacha njia yangu na kufanya kile kila mtu anataka.

Our spiritual forefathers had much to say on the many issues facing the American Mennonite church in their time, and we can still learn from the collected writings of these church leaders and brethren. We will look first at the hermeneutics of the early American Mennonite church, endeavoring to draw examples from which we, as 21st-century Christians, can learn.

First, the correct interpretation of Scripture was a matter of great importance to these earlier Christians. They had only recently emigrated away from a largely hostile area, where they had been constantly tested to the point of death on matters of faith and now faced a different set of challenges when confronted with peace and religious freedom. We will look at how they navigated these challenges by studying several of their doctrines and practices.

The Doctrine of Nonresistance

One matter that was well interpreted and applied by many of the early Mennonite writers is the principle and doctrine of the nonresistant Christian. Although many of their Anabaptist descendants of today still hold, to varying degrees, this doctrine, it is oftentimes not done with the clarity and solemnity of their forefathers. The early American Mennonites understood nonresistance as a foundational aspect of the Christian life, as it should be, and taught extensively on the practical application and appearance of nonresistance in the life of a believer. Their primary motivation for living peaceably and without malice toward one’s fellow man was the given example of Jesus. Christ typified the acceptable response to violence and ill-will: gentleness, meekness, as befitted one who is called a Lamb.

The Emphasis of Biblical Foundations

There was also a firm focus amongst early Mennonite writers against building doctrine on the writings of men. This emphasis comes through strongly in their works, as they quote Scripture extensively. They made their point by bringing in an example of Christ or by way of an applicable Scripture verse, rather than building on the sandy soil of a man’s opinions. One of the areas in which they did so was the matter of salvation.

Importance of Practical Salvation

We can learn much from the early Mennonites about the practical working out of salvation. First, salvation is portrayed as both an inward and an outward change. The inward is affected first through the working of the Holy Spirit in the willful sinner’s life. It is an important distinction that the sinner is willful. This position was contrary to most of the greater established churches of the time. If a sinner must be willful, then it implies that all men can willfully accept salvation, an idea that is fundamental in nature, if not always verbalized, to the church of today.

In the early Mennonites’ time, predestination as taught by Calvinism seems to have necessitated this emphasis on man’s ability to choose freely, which is still true today. There is also another flavoring of the “unwillingly saved” interpretation, and that comes from the aftereffects of the charismatic movement and the effect it has had on Mennonite and Amish circles. This “unwilling salvation” is not a matter of predestination, but rather is described as almost a coercive calling by the Spirit. It has been observed in several salvation testimonies where the testifiers recalled how they were completely comfortable in their lives of sin and debauchery when suddenly they would be struck down in the manner of Saul and could not help themselves but follow after God and give their lives to Him. There are numerous pitfalls with this dramatic understanding of conversion, namely that it absolves responsibility from the one converted for his decision to convert. This leads to a lack of counting the cost of Christianity, which is a death of oneself, a death of pride, and a death of favor with man. If the believer hops headfirst into Christianity, not reckoning that he must give up all these self-pleasing traits, how will he be able to grow spiritually if he cannot let go of his former vices? While this form of conversion may be genuine at the beginning, it does not often progress beyond the milk of the Word to the meat of which a mature Christian must partake. This maturing of a Christian is emphasized in writings ranging from those of Menno Simons up to Abraham Goshalk. It is also important for the sake of the church that the believer be firmly committed and engaged in the steady growth of his faith.

The Seriousness of a Pure Church

The idea of church to the early American Mennonite seems to have been a more serious thought, less individualistic than our current state. It is the pitiable state of nominal Christianity that the church has become a social organization with room for all sin and depravity.

It behooves us to consider closely the character of the church that Christ established and to note as well the character of the true churches, unspotted by apostasy and laxness. This character is, like Christ himself, simple and yet incredibly full of meaning and spiritual vitality.

The first aspect of the church to recognize is its pure state as the bride of Christ. Here again, we should consider the character of Christ. Did He ever give Himself space for sin? Do we find Him occasionally indulging in a brief enjoyment of a “guilty pleasure”? The understanding reader will agree that Christ was pure in His entirety, and so how else should the bride be with which He is to be intimately and eternally joined? To aid our minds in answering such a question, let us consider the earthly symbol of this heavenly union: that of a man and a woman joined together for life. This earthly union is recognized even by non-Christians as something set aside purely for the two individuals involved, a relationship and a sharing of each other that is not and never to be partaken of by anyone outside of the intimate union. This paints clearly for our earth-bound minds the mind of Christ, insomuch as that marriage is a symbol of Christ and His bride. The bride and Christ are for each other and give themselves to nothing and no one other.

Now that we can see the purity of the church, let us examine its practical working out amongst fallen man. If it is to be pure, then how are we to be a part of it? Here enters the need for a clear understanding of regeneration, a doctrine held in high regard by these Mennonite forefathers. They taught that the Spirit affects the spiritual washing and cleansing that will be made apparent in a changed state of thought and action in the believer. This change is still at variance with our fallen nature, but through continued surrender and a deep humility, the Spirit will fill the believer until the nature of sin becomes the dominated instead of the dominant. It is important to realize, however, that this victory over sin is brought into effect by the believer yielding his will and allowing the Spirit complete control.

Thus, a pure church is a surrendered, Spirit-filled group of believers who recognize in true humility that their power is not in any way linked to their own merit. The absence of pride, achieved only by the constant aid of the Spirit, gives further room for purification of the willing believer. In this way, we can see the Christian life in shoe leather.

The Teachings of Practical Christianity

The practicality of the early American Mennonite’s faith was continually on display. In his book, “Pride and Humility,” John M. Brenneman maintains that the outward appearance of a person is directly related to his inward heart, a view which extends as well to the actions of the individual. It is necessary to build on the beliefs of willful salvation, regeneration, and a pure church previously examined to frame the mindset of a Mennonite’s interactions in daily living.

To these serious-minded Christians, there was no difference in importance between the religious belief expressed on Sundays and the mundane actions of the rest of the week. This is evidenced by their general abstinence from political matters and other elements of a worldly nature that would infringe upon the beliefs they held. This put them in direct opposition to many of the churches of their day, where thrived two schools of thought: either that one’s earthly duties in a political manner were carried out completely separate from one’s faith, or that the accomplishment of these civic duties were incorporated in the will of God and so permissible for the Christian to engage in freely.

To the early American Mennonite, these types of stances betrayed the very meaning of his Christianity: he was a new person, alive only in the power of Christ that flowed through him. This influenced and directed every aspect of his life, from his business dealings, which were carried out in a way so as not to take advantage of any party involved, to his dress and manner of deportment, which was to be based on humility and plainness, to his method of conversing with his fellow man, which was to show a genuine concern for the spiritual well-being and eternal destiny.

Conclusion

The sum of all these colonial Mennonite beliefs was the doctrine of how to grow into a mature, humble, repentant, but spiritually powerful servant of God. He denied the allures of the world around him in favor of an eternal reward promised upon the purity of his faith and willing renunciation of the sin in which he had formerly lived. This example, lived out by believers like us, should inspire us to further press into the Kingdom of God, working out our faith in humility and repentance.
