Moralidade tem a ver com comportamento certo e errado. Pureza é estar livre de culpa ou falha moral, marcada pela castidade, que é integridade pessoal. Pureza não contém nada que não pertença propriamente ali. Como o título sugere, este artigo tratará de fazer o que é certo e estar livre de falha e culpa moral, viver uma vida de integridade e manter nosso interior e exterior livres de qualquer coisa que não pertença propriamente.

Repare no que as Escrituras dizem sobre ser puro. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” Em outras palavras, são as pessoas limpas por dentro e por fora que verão a Deus e entrarão em Sua presença.

Ser moralmente puro não acontecerá sem forte determinação e disciplina. Sempre foi assim, mas ainda mais hoje com o crescimento da tecnologia e a disponibilidade do mal na ponta dos nossos dedos.

Os pecados sexuais não são estranhos à igreja. De fato, não são estranhos a nenhum povo de qualquer raça. Não podemos relaxar e baixar a guarda supondo que nossos filhos estarão seguros dos males da sociedade e da nossa humanidade. Devemos mostrar pelo exemplo e ensinar nossos filhos e jovens se esperarmos que eles permaneçam limpos nesta sociedade corrupta. Não podemos presumir que se uma pessoa se veste de determinada maneira, tudo está bem por dentro. A história não é totalmente contada pelo exterior. Os fariseus faziam o exterior parecer bom, enquanto o interior estava cheio de corrupção. Jesus disse, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Nós também devemos dar atenção primária às questões do coração. Quando o coração está limpo, então o exterior também poderá ser limpo.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” A escuridão interna sempre destruirá a comunhão e matará relacionamentos—todas as vezes.

Isto pretende ser uma mensagem de esperança, não de desânimo. Se você tem um ponto escuro escondido, confesse-o e livre-se dele. Você pode ser livre! É possível ser liberto das garras de Satanás e viver uma vida aberta e transparente com alegria na alma. Você não precisa passar a vida tentando esconder a escuridão do mal. Jesus quer perdoar e curar.

Satanás é cruel. Em John 10:10, Jesus disse, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. O interesse dele é desestruturar seu lar, destruir seu respeito e te enviar ao inferno. Enquanto isso, ele está te atraindo pelo desejo da carne, com sua espada desembainhada para prender e matar você.

O pecado moral é tão vergonhoso e difícil de admitir. O natural é tentar esconder quando erramos. Crianças que aprendem a esconder o erro cedo na vida naturalmente se desenvolvem em jovens que escondem coisas dos pais, professores e ministros. Essa pessoa precisará aprender a ser aberta e transparente, ou chegará o momento em que ela estará escondendo coisas de seu cônjuge. Esconder resulta em uma vida dupla e conduz a mais escravidão e relacionamentos quebrados. Pessoas que têm portas fechadas em alguns cantos de suas vidas serão possessivas com seus telefones e relutarão em compartilhar suas senhas com uma parceira de confiança. Parece que facilmente esquecemos quão fútil é esconder-se de Deus. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Como podemos ser tão ingênuos e tolos em pensar que podemos esconder qualquer coisa de Deus? Ou levar um passo adiante: por que quereríamos esconder algo Dele? Numbers 32:23 continua muito verdadeiro, dizendo, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Deus te ama demais para deixar você continuar escondendo o que precisa ser trazido à luz e perdoado.

Os pecados sexuais também são extremamente enganosos. Geralmente acontecem como Tiago descreveu no capítulo um. Somos seduzidos, desviados, puxados como um ímã para fora do centro, sentimos uma onda de desejo, certificamo-nos de que ninguém está olhando, cobrimos nossos rastros, damos um passo mais perto do proibido, sentimos mais desejo, e começamos muito rápido a perder o raciocínio e o pensamento sadio, incapazes de calcular consequências semelhantemente a uma pessoa embriagada, então Tiago 1:15 acontece: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

Tiago nos diria para não cobiçar o que não é nosso, nem mesmo um indício. A Bíblia nos diz para fugir de três coisas. Uma delas é fornicação, que pode ser ampliada para todos os pecados sexuais. Não brinque com isso; não olhe de novo; afaste-se! Substitua esses pensamentos por pensamentos edificantes sobre Deus e Seu caminho. Cante um hino antigo; felizmente não conseguimos pensar em duas coisas ao mesmo tempo. Seja o que for preciso, fuja desse desejo lascivo. Ele te levará mais longe do que você deseja ir e custará mais do que você quer pagar. Veja a fita até o fim e pergunte a si mesmo: se eu seguir o que estou sendo tentado, terei o que quero? Satanás sempre promete prazer, mas então entrega dor. Lembre-se, Satanás nunca inventou um prazer; ele apenas toma o que Deus fez para ser puro e bom, perverte e oferece de volta em sua forma pervertida. Lembre-se, a espada de Satanás está desembainhada para matar neste ponto. Fuja dos desejos maus!

Não siga sua concupiscência. Pornografia é extremamente viciante e tem enredado muitas pessoas. Promise Keepers disse que 65% dos homens em sua pesquisa eram viciados. O vício em pornografia é como álcool ou drogas. Dizem-nos que o cérebro está pedindo endorfinas a serem despejadas nele, seja por vício em álcool, drogas ou pornografia. Enfatizo novamente que os homens e mulheres que alcançarem a vitória serão aqueles que, como Daniel dos antigos, propuseram em seus corações não se contaminarem.

Este assunto também é para nossas irmãs, e algumas perguntas parecem apropriadas. O que no seu interior está cuidadosamente guardado e escondido? As decepções da vida causaram um vazio que faz tomar um 'Tylenol emocional' te fazer sentir melhor por um curto período? Sua conexão emocional está segura onde Deus a planejou?

Jovens devem ser ensinadas a desenvolver uma reserva saudável com os homens. Não com uma atitude altiva e nunca sorrindo, mas também não se relacionando de forma excessivamente livre com rapazes. Nossa sociedade está voltada exatamente para o oposto, e desde o jardim de infância meninos e meninas são provocados sobre amizades especiais. Como resultado, as crianças crescem com pouca ou nenhuma reserva. Socializar por mensagens entre gêneros deve ser evitado fora das relações familiares. Isso desenvolverá um hábito nos jovens que um dia precisará ser quebrado se esperam viver uma vida aberta e transparente com um cônjuge. Pense desta forma: você gostaria que seu cônjuge socializasse com o gênero oposto nas redes sociais?

Irmãs, cuidado com os livros que vocês leem. Romances de amor embotam o desejo pela Palavra de Deus e dão expectativas irreais da vida conjugal. Esses livros passam a ideia de que o homem certo em algum lugar seria a chave para a realização e felicidade na vida. Só Jesus pode preencher o vazio que o pecado trouxe a todo ser humano hoje. Nenhum homem ou mulher jamais poderá dar a segurança e a tranquilidade da alma que todos desejamos tão ardentemente. Essa dor no coração nunca será saciada por curativos ou analgésicos. Eles ajudam apenas por um momento, e quando passam, o clamor do coração é ainda mais alto. Livros indigestos embotam o gosto pelas coisas de Deus e, em vez disso, criam um desejo por comida de baixa qualidade e analgésicos.

Outra preocupação para as irmãs é a quantidade de tempo que vocês passam online. Não há fim em alimentar o desejo por requinte, singularidade, charme e beleza. Não deixem que essas coisas sejam o motor da sua vida, pois nunca dirão 'basta' e nada farão para satisfazer a alma ou apontar seus filhos na direção certa. Considere a quantidade de tempo que você dedica a receber visitas e festas. Ao longo dos anos, vi nomes surgirem e desaparecerem de oportunidades de negócios e produtos que era preciso ter. Mas, em alguns anos, não conseguimos nem lembrar esses nomes e, enquanto isso, as crianças cresciam e agora são adultos. Considere as reais necessidades na sua vida e suas responsabilidades, e então decida o que trará investimentos eternos. Mulheres com filhos precisam limitar hobbies que tanto apreciam porque, neste momento, são abençoadas com filhos que têm almas eternas e o tempo com eles é um investimento para a eternidade. Lembre-se que seu marido e filhos são muito mais dignos do seu tempo do que passar horas em mais uma festa.

Como podemos viver uma vida moralmente pura?

Seja Humilde. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” É preciso humildade e quebrantamento para reconhecer nossas necessidades, mas o quebrantamento é a chave para a vitória. I Peter 5:5 nos diz que Deus dá graça aos humildes. Uma das definições mais abrangentes de graça é a assistência divina imerecida dada aos humanos para regeneração e santificação. Regeneração é 'graça redentora', e santificação é 'graça transformadora'. A verdade é que Deus dá 'graça transformadora' aos humildes. Essa graça nos transforma de dentro para fora, tornando-nos santos. Este aspecto da graça deve ser desejado e buscado tanto quanto a graça redentora foi quando Deus nos salvou. Este é provavelmente o passo mais importante para vencer vícios de qualquer tipo. Seja humilde o suficiente para torná-lo uma oração diária a Deus por Sua graça transformadora. Jesus ensinou em Matthew 23:26, onde disse, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Seja Honesto. Examine seus pensamentos, ações, tentações, as coisas com que você luta, raiva, luxúria, orgulho, amargura, etc. Você é tão espiritual quanto se mostra por fora? Tire o verniz e admita a necessidade de ajuda.

Seja transparente. Romans 2:16 fala do dia em que Deus julgará os segredos dos homens. Somos tão tolos em pensar que podemos esconder o mal. Podemos nos esconder por um tempo, mas algum dia nossas ações ficarão nuas diante de um Deus que tudo sabe. Por que tentar esconder algo agora? Essas coisas escondidas podem ser trazidas antes do julgamento, e uma vida sem culpa pode ser uma realidade hoje. Seja transparente; deve ser uma meta em funcionamento.

Diga a si mesmo a verdade. Quando você é tentado, considere o fim do seu desejo lascivo. Você conseguirá o que quer? Esse desejo será satisfeito, ou só desejará mais? Se você visse seu irmão fazendo o que está buscando, como pareceria? Como parecerá trinta anos adiante se você seguir seu desejo maligno? Trazerá alegria ou tristeza? Será útil para alguém, ou assustará outra pessoa? Diga a si mesmo a verdade antes de ficar intoxicado e incapaz de fazer julgamentos racionais.

Ensine seus olhos a pular. Você não pode controlar o que vê na primeira vez, mas pode controlar o que olha pela segunda vez. Faça disso uma prática até virar hábito: desvie os olhos sempre que vir algo que leva a pensamentos impuros.

Ensinando nossos filhos. Isso deve pesar em nossos corações desde a infância. Se não ensinarmos nossos filhos que Deus nos fez à Sua imagem, que precisa ser mantida pura, outra pessoa os ensinará a ser secretos e a se sentirem impuros. Fique perto de seus filhos e ensine-os conforme amadurecem.

Mantenha suas emoções. Isso é uma proteção em nossa sociedade corrompida. Quanto mais você se afastar disso, mais vulnerável estará à corrupção. Mantenha seu cônjuge em primeiro lugar na vida, aquele com quem você compartilha e por quem está ligado emocionalmente.

Fuja da luxúria e da fornicação. Fuja! Esses desejos são vícios que precisam ser quebrados. Lembre-se, o que você alimenta cresce, e o que você deixa morrerá de fome. Esses vícios podem ser quebrados, mas você precisará alimentar os relacionamentos que Deus lhe deu e privar os prejudiciais.

Deus nos fez de tal maneira que quando amamos as coisas que Ele ama, nosso coração ainda tem espaço para amar mais. Não importa quantos filhos, netos ou amigos piedosos tenhamos, nossos corações ainda têm espaço para amar mais. Mas no momento em que começamos a amar o que Deus proibiu, isso começa a substituir e destruir todo outro amor, preenchendo nossos corações com vazio, dor e solidão, que leva a um fim amargo.

Muitos homens recobraram a sensatez e viram a total tolice do caminho que escolheram. Alguns tentaram esconder conduta impura e foram bem-sucedidos até a velhice. Outros a mantiveram escondida até depois de terem partido. Uma pergunta para refletir: vale a pena? Claro que a resposta é um retumbante NÃO!

Quão maravilhoso é viver uma vida aberta livre de culpa e ter paz com Deus e a certeza dos pecados perdoados, para que um dia sejamos retirados deste mundo mau e conduzidos à presença do nosso Santo Deus.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

کبھی ہم کسی گانے، فن کا کام، کہانی، یا کسی اور شخص میں حسن کی تعریف کرتے ہیں، لیکن داؤد خدا کی خوبصورتی کو دیکھ کر خوشی کی کیفیت بیان کرتا ہے۔ “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). خدا خوبصورت ہے کیونکہ اُس کی برتری دلکش ہے—اُس کا کردار بے عیب ہے۔ داؤد نے جان بھرا ہوا لطف محسوس کیا جو خدا کو اس کی پوری حقیقت میں جاننے اور تجربہ کرنے سے آتا ہے۔ خدا اپنی خوبصورتی کیسے ظاہر کرتا ہے؟

مخلُوقات کے ذریعے

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). مخلوق کی دنیا کی تمام خوبصورتی خدا سے آئی ہے۔ ایک خوبصورت غروبِ آفتاب، ایک حسین گلاب، ایک بلند سرخ لکڑی کا درخت، ایک شاندار پہاڑی چوٹی—یہ سب مخلوقات میں خدا کی خوبصورتی کی مثال ہیں۔ جیسا کہ شاہراہ پر لگے نشان ہمیں ہماری منزل تک رہنمائی کرتے ہیں، اسی طرح مخلوق انسانیت کو خود خدا کی طرف رہنمائی کرتی ہے۔ “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). مخلوق کے یہ تحفے ہمیں اُن خالق کی مختصر جھلک دکھانے کے لئے دیے گئے ہیں جنہوں نے انہیں پیدا کیا۔

ہم، خدا کی مخلوق کے حصے کے طور پر، اُس کی تخلیقی خوبصورتی کو کیسے منعکس کریں؟ اگرچہ ہم کچھ بھی نہیں سے کچھ نہیں بنا سکتے، خدا نے ہمیں تخلیقی بننے کے لیے بنایا ہے، تاکہ ہم اپنی فکری صلاحیتوں اور مخلوق کے وسائل کو استعمال کر کے زندگی کو عملی بنائیں۔ کسی اچھے کام کے موثر انجام سے ملنے والا اطمینان تخلیق میں اس کی بنیاد رکھتا ہے، جہاں خدا نے اپنے کام کو دیکھا اور اسے اچھا قرار دیا۔ سادہ اور میانہ رو زندگی گزارنے کی کوشش میں ہم بعض اوقات زندگی کی خوبصورت چیزوں میں خوشی لینا بھول جاتے ہیں۔ یہ درست اور اچھا ہے اور ہماری تخلیق کے مطابق ہے کہ ہم خوبصورتی والی چیزوں میں خوشی محسوس کریں۔ بے خدا لوگوں نے اس تخلیقی تحفے کو بہت بار برے مقصد کے لیے استعمال کیا ہے۔ اس لیے زیادہ از زیادہ، آئیں ہم خدا کی مخلوق کو ایسے طریقوں سے استعمال کر کے خدا کی جلال کریں جو اُس کے کردار کی عکاسی کریں۔

قدرت اور مخلوق (قدرتی اور انسان ساختہ) سے محبت کرنے والوں کے لیے ایک انتباہ: ہمیں محتاط رہنا چاہیے کہ ہم زمینی خوبصورتی کو خالق سے بالا نہ کریں، کیونکہ یہ بت پرستی کی جانب لاتا ہے۔ غروبِ آفتاب مدھم پڑ جاتے ہیں، سرخ لکڑیاں گر پڑتی ہیں، گلاب مرجھا جاتے ہیں، انسانی جسم پھر دوبارہ مٹی بن جاتا ہے، مگر خدا برقرار رہتا ہے۔ زندگی اور اس کی تمام خوبصورتی خدا کے ساتھ شروع ہوتی ہے اور خدا پر ختم ہوتی ہے۔

موسیقی اور آواز کے ذریعے

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) مکاشفہ کی کتاب کے مطابق، خدا کے تخت کے گرد آواز ہے: گرج اور بجلی؛ فرشتوں، چار حیوانوں اور بیس بزرگوں سے بہنے والی ستائشیں، اور ایک بہت بڑا ہجوم جسے کوئی گنتی نہیں کر سکتا؛ اور وہ نوے چار ہزار کا نیا گانا۔

خدا نے آواز کی خوبصورتی پیدا کی تاکہ الفاظ جو کہ حد رکھتے ہیں اُن سے بڑھ کر اپنے آپ کو جلال بخشے۔ اُس کی تخلیق کی باریکی اس طرح ظاہر ہوتی ہے کہ مختلف صوتی فریکوئنسیز کس طرح مل کر ایک خوبصورت اور آسمانی ہم آہنگی بناتی ہیں۔ انسانیت کے لیے صحیح ہے کہ وہ اُن آوازوں کی خوبصورتی میں لطف اٹھا کر خدا کو جلال دے جو اُس نے اپنی جلال کے لیے پیدا کیں۔ جو شخص خدا سے محبت رکھتا ہے، جب بھی خوشگوار آوازوں سے سہلایا جاتا ہے تو خدا کی طرف کھنچا جاتا ہے: قومِ خدا زِیون کے گیت گا رہی ہے، مقدسین کی دعائیں، درختوں کی چوٹیوں میں سرسراہٹ کرتی ہوا، گانے والا پرندہ اپنے خالق کی ستائش کر رہا ہے، بادلوں کی گڑگڑاہٹ، یا چھت پر بارش کے سادہ ٹپ ٹپ۔

ہم، آواز کے ساز کے طور پر، خدا کی خوبصورتی کو آواز کے ذریعے کیسے منعکس کریں؟ ہمیں ہمیشہ سُنتے رہنے اور آسمان کی آوازوں اور ہم آہنگیوں کی مانند بننے کی کوشش کرنی چاہیے۔ اگرچہ ہم زمین پر اسے مکمل طور پر حاصل نہیں کر سکیں گے، یہ عمر بھر کا عزم ہونا چاہیے۔ یہ سوالات پوچھے گئے ہیں، “کیا ہمیں ہمیشہ اپنی موسیقی سازی کو بہتر بنانے کی کوشش کرنی چاہیے؟” اور “ہم نے کب ‘کافی اچھا’ کو حاصل کر لیا؟” ہم آسمانی کمال تک کبھی پہنچ نہیں سکیں گے، اس لیے سوال یہ ہونا چاہیے، “کیا ہم خدا کو اپنی بہترین چیز دے رہے ہیں؟” بعض لوگوں میں دوسروں کے مقابلے میں زیادہ گانے کی صلاحیت ہوتی ہے، مگر سوال وہی رہتا ہے۔ “کیا ہم اپنی بہترین چیز دے رہے ہیں یا کیا ہم ایک نا موزوں قربانی پر راضی ہیں؟” آئیں ہم ایسے خدا کی خوشنودی کے آوازیں پیدا کریں جو خالق کے دل کو خوشی پہنچائیں!

چرچ کے ذریعے:

بائبل خدا کے لوگوں کی خوبصورتی کے بارے میں بہت کچھ کہتی ہے۔ “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” اور “The Church” بائبل میں باہم مترادف اظہار ہیں جو زمین پر خدا کے لوگوں کے ٹھکانے کو ظاہر کرتے ہیں۔ یہ خدا کی خواہش ہے کہ اس کی خوبصورتی اس کے لوگوں کی زندگیوں میں ظاہر ہو۔ “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

خدا کے دل کے لیے اس کی کلیسا سے زیادہ عزیز کوئی چیز نہیں۔ جب بنی اسرائیل صحرا میں سفر کر رہے تھے تو انہوں نے خدا کے درمیان رہنے کے لئے خیمہ بنوایا۔ جب سلیمان نے مندر کو خدا کا گھر طور پر وقف کیا تو خدا بہت خوش ہوا اور 2 Chronicles 7:1 کہتا ہے کہ خدا کی جلالت نے مندر کو بھر دیا۔ مندر کو خدا کے گھر کے طور پر سمجھا جاتا تھا—یسوع نے خود اسے متعدد بار خدا کے گھر کے طور پر ذکر کیا اور یہ بہت جذبہ رکھتا تھا کہ اسے پاک رکھا جائے۔

آج نہ تو خیمہ اور نہ ہی مندر خدا کی موجودگی کی میزبانی کرتے ہیں بلکہ اس کی الوہی جذبہ یسوع مسیح کی کلیسا پر مرتکز ہے۔ یہاں وہ لوگ ہیں جو واقعی اسے محبت کرتے ہیں اور اس کے لیے اپنی زندگیاں دینے کو تیار ہیں۔ یہاں وہ لوگ ہیں جو اپنی انفرادی حقوق سے دست بردار ہونے اور ایک بڑے مقصد کے لیے خود کو سونپنے کو تیار ہیں۔ یہاں بہت سے مقدسین نے انجیل کے لیے اپنا خونی قطرہ دیا ہے۔ اور یہاں وہ جگہ ہے جہاں ایک دن ہمارا نجات دہندہ جیسا کہ اُس نے وعدہ کیا ہے واپسی کرے گا، اور اپنی دلہن، کلیسا، کو اُس کے ابدی ٹھکانے پر لے جائے گا۔ “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

ہم، خدا کے لوگ، کلیسا میں اُس کی خوبصورتی کو کیسے منعکس کریں؟ ایک ساتھ رہ کر، اتحاد اور ہم آہنگی میں، خاص طور پر خدا کے گھر والوں کے لیے محبت رکھ کر۔ کلیسا وہ جگہ ہونی چاہیے جہاں دنیا آسمان میں ہونے والی چیزوں کی جھلک پائے۔ یہ وہ جگہ ہونی چاہیے جہاں مسیح ہمیشہ گناہ، موت اور ہولاک کے فاتح کے طور پر بلندی پر ہو۔

افسوس کی بات ہے کہ بہت سے لوگ کلیسا کی ناکامیوں سے مایوس ہو کر اصلی رسولی ایمان سے دور ہو گئے ہیں۔ ہماری مایوسیوں کے باوجود، آئیں ہم “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) اور آگے بڑھیں۔ ہمیں کبھی بھی کوئی اعلیٰ تر بلندی نہیں ملے گی، اور نہ ہی کوئی زیادہ عظیم جنگ جو لڑنی ہو۔

آخر میں، ہم اپنی زندگیوں میں اُس کی خوبصورتی کیسے منعکس کریں؟ اُس میں خوشی منا کر۔ “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). زندگی میں سب سے بڑی تکمیل اسی چیز سے ملتی ہے کہ خدا کے دل کو خوشی پہنچانے میں خوشی ملے—اُس میں خوش ہونا جو وہ خوش ہوتا ہے اور اُس سے محبت کرنا جو وہ محبت کرتا ہے۔ آئیں ہم اپنی نجات کی خوبصورتی کا حیرت کبھی نہ کھوئیں!

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet

Of Thy renewed earth.

These nobler works of Thine,

This bloom of love so fair,

And fragrancy of prayer!

These wonders sweet of Thine;

Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

“אדריאנה, מה הטמפרטורה בחוץ?” שאל אשר. הוא ואדריאנה ישבו על השולחן ועשו שיעורים יחד עם אחיותיהם אמילי וקיאנה.

“כנראה בערך 50.” אדריאנה הביטה ברשלנות במד־החום. “היי, זה 65 מעלות! אמא, אפשר לאכול ארוחת צהריים בחוץ?”

אמא הרימה מבט מהכיור. “אם תעבדו טוב על השיעורים עד אז, תוכלו,” אמרה להם. “ואם תסיימו את השיעורים לפני ארוחת הצהריים, תוכלו לשחק בחוץ קצת אחרי הצהריים.”

אשר צרח משמחה והתחיל לכתוב מהר. הבנות חייכו זו לזו והחלו להרים את העפרונות.

כולם עבדו בהתמדה עד ארוחת הצהריים. אז אדריאנה הכינה כריכים בעוד אשר שמר עוגיות בשקיות, אמילי אספה שקיות חטיפים, וקיאנה ירדה למרתף לתפוס כמה תפוחים. כל אחד חיבר את ארוחתו בשקית קניות ויצא לנקודת הפיקניק שלהם — סלע גדול ושטוח בפתח יער.

הם אכלו מהר, ואז אדריאנה הציעה, “בואו נלך בקאייק לאגם!”

“נראה לי שנוכל,” אמר אשר באיטיות. “אבל האמא לא אמרה שאמילי וקיאנה קטנות מדי לטפל בקאייקים?”

“או, כן, כנראה שהיא אמרה. ובכן, הן יכולות לשחק על המנדפות או משהו,” היא משכה בכתפיה.

“אני חושב שנוח לשחק משהו שכולם יכולים לעזור בו,” אמר אשר. הוא פנה לאמילי ולקיאנה. “מה תרצו לעשות?”

“בואו נכין בית משחק!” הציעה קיאנה.

“כן, בואו!” הסכימה אמילי. “אתה יכול לצוד בשבילנו,” אמרה לאשר.

“ואדריאנה יכולה להיות אמא!” אמרה קיאנה.

אדריאנה עמדה עם פרצוף מקומט. בית משחק! היא כבר גדולה מדי לזה! “אני הולכת בקאייק,” הכריזה. “אתן יכולות לשמור על בית המשחק שלכן.” היא הרימה את שקית הקניות והכניסה לתוכה את הכריך ושקיות העוגיות שלה. היא זרקה את גלעין התפוח לכלבים והחלה לצעוד לכיוון הבית.

“אדריאנה, תוכלי בבקשה לקחת גם את שלנו?” התחננה אמילי. “את anyway הולכת לבית.”

“אתן תדאגו לדברים שלכן,” קראה אדריאנה בחוצפה. היא הטילה את שקית הקניות על הדלפק, בתקווה לצאת מהבית לפני שאמא תראה אותה.

שמעו את קול אמא. “חכי, אדריאנה, מה קרה? הפנים שלך נראות כמו סערה!”

אדריאנה נשפה. היא לא הספיקה מהר מספיק. “רציתי ללכת בקאייק, אבל אשר לא רוצה,” היא מלמלה.

“ובכן,” אמרה אמא לאט, “אני חושבת שאשר זוכר שהבנות האחרות עדיין לא יכולות לטפל בקאייקים. מה הן עושות?”

“הן בונות בית משחק. אני כבר גדולה מדי לזה!” פרצה אדריאנה.

אמא חייכה, “מה גורם לך לחשוב כך?”

“אני בטוחה שאף אחת מהבנות בגיל שלי לא עושה דברים כאלה עם אחיותיהן הקטנות.”

“את בטוחה שאת לא אגואיסטית?” שאלה אמא. “לפעמים צריך לוותר על מה שאנחנו רוצים כדי שאחרים יהיו מאושרים.”

אדריאנה משכה בכתפיה ויצאה למחסן להשיג קאייק. היא הורידה את הקאייק הכחול מהמדף והסיעה אותו אל האגם. היא הרכיבה את המשוט, קפצה למושב ודחפה את הקאייק אל פני המים החלקים. היא נשפה בהנאה. זה הרבה יותר טוב מבניית בית משחק ביער! היא עשתה כמה הקפות סביב האגם לפני שהמשוט התחיל להאט. איכשהו זה לא היה כל כך כיף הפעם. היא שמעה את אשר והבנות צוחקים וצופרים בזמן ששיחקו. אולי אמא צודקת, חשבה. אולי אהיה מאושרת יותר אם אוותר על מה שאני רוצה כדי שכולנו נשחק יחד. לאט לאט היא שפכה אל שפת האגם. היא יצאה מהקאייק, משכה אותו אל החוף והפכה אותו כדי ליבש. בהחלטיות היא הלכה מעבר למגרש למצוא את אשר והבנות.

“היי! הנה באה אדריאנה!” קראה אמילי בשמחה כשהיא חולפת אליה.

אדריאנה חייכה, “נראה שביתכן כמעט מוכן,” היא אמרה בעידוד. “מה חסר לכן כדי לסיים אותו?”

“עדיין צריך כיריים, ומשהו לשמש לדלפק,” сказала קיאנה.

“אני יכולה לעזור לכן למצוא משהו,” אדריאנה אמרה להן. יחד הן חיפשו ביער ובמחסן קרשים ולוגים כדי להשלים את הבית. כשבאה זמן ארוחת הערב והן נכנסו לאכול, אדריאנה הייתה מאוד שמחה. אמא צדקה, חשבה. זה יותר כיף לוותר על הדרך שלי ולעשות מה שכולם רוצים.

Our spiritual forefathers had much to say on the many issues facing the American Mennonite church in their time, and we can still learn from the collected writings of these church leaders and brethren. We will look first at the hermeneutics of the early American Mennonite church, endeavoring to draw examples from which we, as 21st-century Christians, can learn.

First, the correct interpretation of Scripture was a matter of great importance to these earlier Christians. They had only recently emigrated away from a largely hostile area, where they had been constantly tested to the point of death on matters of faith and now faced a different set of challenges when confronted with peace and religious freedom. We will look at how they navigated these challenges by studying several of their doctrines and practices.

The Doctrine of Nonresistance

One matter that was well interpreted and applied by many of the early Mennonite writers is the principle and doctrine of the nonresistant Christian. Although many of their Anabaptist descendants of today still hold, to varying degrees, this doctrine, it is oftentimes not done with the clarity and solemnity of their forefathers. The early American Mennonites understood nonresistance as a foundational aspect of the Christian life, as it should be, and taught extensively on the practical application and appearance of nonresistance in the life of a believer. Their primary motivation for living peaceably and without malice toward one’s fellow man was the given example of Jesus. Christ typified the acceptable response to violence and ill-will: gentleness, meekness, as befitted one who is called a Lamb.

The Emphasis of Biblical Foundations

There was also a firm focus amongst early Mennonite writers against building doctrine on the writings of men. This emphasis comes through strongly in their works, as they quote Scripture extensively. They made their point by bringing in an example of Christ or by way of an applicable Scripture verse, rather than building on the sandy soil of a man’s opinions. One of the areas in which they did so was the matter of salvation.

Importance of Practical Salvation

We can learn much from the early Mennonites about the practical working out of salvation. First, salvation is portrayed as both an inward and an outward change. The inward is affected first through the working of the Holy Spirit in the willful sinner’s life. It is an important distinction that the sinner is willful. This position was contrary to most of the greater established churches of the time. If a sinner must be willful, then it implies that all men can willfully accept salvation, an idea that is fundamental in nature, if not always verbalized, to the church of today.

In the early Mennonites’ time, predestination as taught by Calvinism seems to have necessitated this emphasis on man’s ability to choose freely, which is still true today. There is also another flavoring of the “unwillingly saved” interpretation, and that comes from the aftereffects of the charismatic movement and the effect it has had on Mennonite and Amish circles. This “unwilling salvation” is not a matter of predestination, but rather is described as almost a coercive calling by the Spirit. It has been observed in several salvation testimonies where the testifiers recalled how they were completely comfortable in their lives of sin and debauchery when suddenly they would be struck down in the manner of Saul and could not help themselves but follow after God and give their lives to Him. There are numerous pitfalls with this dramatic understanding of conversion, namely that it absolves responsibility from the one converted for his decision to convert. This leads to a lack of counting the cost of Christianity, which is a death of oneself, a death of pride, and a death of favor with man. If the believer hops headfirst into Christianity, not reckoning that he must give up all these self-pleasing traits, how will he be able to grow spiritually if he cannot let go of his former vices? While this form of conversion may be genuine at the beginning, it does not often progress beyond the milk of the Word to the meat of which a mature Christian must partake. This maturing of a Christian is emphasized in writings ranging from those of Menno Simons up to Abraham Goshalk. It is also important for the sake of the church that the believer be firmly committed and engaged in the steady growth of his faith.

The Seriousness of a Pure Church

The idea of church to the early American Mennonite seems to have been a more serious thought, less individualistic than our current state. It is the pitiable state of nominal Christianity that the church has become a social organization with room for all sin and depravity.

It behooves us to consider closely the character of the church that Christ established and to note as well the character of the true churches, unspotted by apostasy and laxness. This character is, like Christ himself, simple and yet incredibly full of meaning and spiritual vitality.

The first aspect of the church to recognize is its pure state as the bride of Christ. Here again, we should consider the character of Christ. Did He ever give Himself space for sin? Do we find Him occasionally indulging in a brief enjoyment of a “guilty pleasure”? The understanding reader will agree that Christ was pure in His entirety, and so how else should the bride be with which He is to be intimately and eternally joined? To aid our minds in answering such a question, let us consider the earthly symbol of this heavenly union: that of a man and a woman joined together for life. This earthly union is recognized even by non-Christians as something set aside purely for the two individuals involved, a relationship and a sharing of each other that is not and never to be partaken of by anyone outside of the intimate union. This paints clearly for our earth-bound minds the mind of Christ, insomuch as that marriage is a symbol of Christ and His bride. The bride and Christ are for each other and give themselves to nothing and no one other.

Now that we can see the purity of the church, let us examine its practical working out amongst fallen man. If it is to be pure, then how are we to be a part of it? Here enters the need for a clear understanding of regeneration, a doctrine held in high regard by these Mennonite forefathers. They taught that the Spirit affects the spiritual washing and cleansing that will be made apparent in a changed state of thought and action in the believer. This change is still at variance with our fallen nature, but through continued surrender and a deep humility, the Spirit will fill the believer until the nature of sin becomes the dominated instead of the dominant. It is important to realize, however, that this victory over sin is brought into effect by the believer yielding his will and allowing the Spirit complete control.

Thus, a pure church is a surrendered, Spirit-filled group of believers who recognize in true humility that their power is not in any way linked to their own merit. The absence of pride, achieved only by the constant aid of the Spirit, gives further room for purification of the willing believer. In this way, we can see the Christian life in shoe leather.

The Teachings of Practical Christianity

The practicality of the early American Mennonite’s faith was continually on display. In his book, “Pride and Humility,” John M. Brenneman maintains that the outward appearance of a person is directly related to his inward heart, a view which extends as well to the actions of the individual. It is necessary to build on the beliefs of willful salvation, regeneration, and a pure church previously examined to frame the mindset of a Mennonite’s interactions in daily living.

To these serious-minded Christians, there was no difference in importance between the religious belief expressed on Sundays and the mundane actions of the rest of the week. This is evidenced by their general abstinence from political matters and other elements of a worldly nature that would infringe upon the beliefs they held. This put them in direct opposition to many of the churches of their day, where thrived two schools of thought: either that one’s earthly duties in a political manner were carried out completely separate from one’s faith, or that the accomplishment of these civic duties were incorporated in the will of God and so permissible for the Christian to engage in freely.

To the early American Mennonite, these types of stances betrayed the very meaning of his Christianity: he was a new person, alive only in the power of Christ that flowed through him. This influenced and directed every aspect of his life, from his business dealings, which were carried out in a way so as not to take advantage of any party involved, to his dress and manner of deportment, which was to be based on humility and plainness, to his method of conversing with his fellow man, which was to show a genuine concern for the spiritual well-being and eternal destiny.

Conclusion

The sum of all these colonial Mennonite beliefs was the doctrine of how to grow into a mature, humble, repentant, but spiritually powerful servant of God. He denied the allures of the world around him in favor of an eternal reward promised upon the purity of his faith and willing renunciation of the sin in which he had formerly lived. This example, lived out by believers like us, should inspire us to further press into the Kingdom of God, working out our faith in humility and repentance.

ہمارے روحانی بزرگوں نے ان امور پر بہت کچھ کہا جو ان کے وقت میں امریکن مینو نائٹ چرچ کو درپیش تھے، اور ہم ان چرچ رہنماؤں اور بھائیوں کی جمع شدہ تحریروں سے ابھی بھی بہت کچھ سیکھ سکتے ہیں۔ ہم پہلے ابتدائی امریکن مینو نائٹسچرچ کی تفسیرِ کتابِ مقدس پر نظر ڈالیں گے، اور ان مثالوں کو اخذ کرنے کی کوشش کریں گے جن سے ہم، بطور اکیسویں صدی کے عیسائی، سبق حاصل کر سکتے ہیں۔

سب سے پہلے، کلامِ مقدس کی صحیح تشریح ان قدیم مسیحیوں کے لیے انتہائی اہم بات تھی۔ وہ حال ہی میں ایک نسبتاً خصمانہ علاقے سے ہجرت کر کے آئے تھے، جہاں ایمان کے معاملات میں انہیں موت تک آزمائشوں کا سامنا کرنا پڑا تھا، اور اب جب انہیں امن اور مذہبی آزادی کا سامنا تھا تو ایک مختلف سیٹ کے چیلنجز درپیش تھے۔ ہم چند اُن کے عقائد اور عملی طریقوں کا مطالعہ کر کے دیکھیں گے کہ انہوں نے ان چیلنجز کو کس طرح عبور کیا۔

غیر مزاحمت کے عقیدے

ایک ایسا معاملہ جس کی کئی ابتدائی مینو نائٹ مؤلفین نے واضح طور پر تشریح اور اطلاق کیا وہ غیر مزاحم عیسائی کے اصول اور عقیدہ تھا۔ اگرچہ ان کے انا بیتھسٹ نسل سے تعلق رکھنے والے آج کے بہت سے لوگ مختلف درجوں میں یہ عقیدہ برقرار رکھتے ہیں، مگر اکثر اوقات یہ اتنی واضحیت اور سنجیدگی کے ساتھ نہیں دیکھا جاتا جتنی ان کے بزرگوں نے دکھائی۔ ابتدائی امریکن مینو نائٹس غیر مزاحمت کو مسیحی زندگی کا بنیادی پہلو سمجھتے تھے، جیسا کہ ہونا چاہیے، اور مومن کی زندگی میں غیر مزاحمت کے عملی اطلاق اور ظاہر ہونے پر وسیع پیمانے پر تعلیم دیتے تھے۔ ایک انسان کے ساتھ پرامن اور بغض کے بغیر رہنے کی ان کی بنیادی تحریک یسوع کا دیا ہوا نمونہ تھا۔ مسیح نے تشدد اور برائی کے لیے جو قبول شدہ ردعمل دکھایا وہ نرمی، عاجزی تھی، جیسا کہ اس کے لائق تھا جو ایک برّہ کہلانے والا ہے۔

کتابی بنیادوں کی اہمیت

ابتدائی مینو نائٹ مؤلفین کے درمیان یہ بھی ایک مضبوط توجہ تھی کہ عقائد کو مردوں کی تحریروں پر استوار نہ کیا جائے۔ یہ زور ان کے کاموں میں واضح طور پر آتا ہے، کیونکہ وہ کلامِ مقدس کا کثرت سے حوالہ دیتے ہیں۔ وہ اپنا نقطہ اس طرح بیان کرتے کہ کسی واقعے یا مسیح کے مثال یا قابل اطلاق آیت کے ذریعے پیش کرتے، بجائے کہ کسی آدمی کی رائے کے ریتیلے زمین پر تعمیر کریں۔ جس میدان میں انہوں نے یہ طریقہ اختیار کیا، وہ نجات کا معاملہ تھا۔

عملی نجات کی اہمیت

ہم ابتدائی مینو نائٹس سے نجات کے عملی اظہار کے بارے میں بہت کچھ سیکھ سکتے ہیں۔ پہلی بات یہ کہ نجات کو اندرونی اور بیرونی دونوں تبدیلیوں کی حیثیت سے دکھایا گیا ہے۔ اندرونی تبدیلی پہلے روح القدس کے کام کے ذریعے ارادتمند گنہگار کی زندگی میں واقع ہوتی ہے۔ یہ اہم امتیاز ہے کہ گنہگار ارادتمند ہے۔ یہ موقف اس وقت کی بیشتر معروف کلیسائی روایات کے برخلاف تھا۔ اگر گنہگار کو ارادتمند ہونا ضروری ہے، تو اس کا مطلب یہ ہے کہ تمام انسان ارادتمندی سے نجات قبول کر سکتے ہیں، ایک خیال جو بنیادی لحاظ سے آج کی کلیسیا کے لیے اہم ہے، خواہ ہمیشہ لفظی طور پر بیان نہ کیا جائے۔

ابتدائی مینو نائٹس کے عہد میں، کیلون ازم کی تعلیمات کے تحت جو تقدیر (predestination) تھی، وہ انسان کی آزاد انتخاب کی صلاحیت پر اس زور کو لازم کرتی محسوس ہوتی تھی، اور یہ آج بھی سچ ہے۔ ایک اور رنگینی ‘‘ناقابلِ مرضی نجات’’ کی تعبیر سے ملتی ہے، جو کاریزماتک تحریک کے بعد کے اثرات اور اس کے مینو نائٹ اور امش حلقوں پر اثر کی وجہ سے ہے۔ یہ ‘‘ناقابلِ مرضی نجات’’ تقدیر کا معاملہ نہیں، بلکہ اسے روح کی طرف سے تقریباً جبری بلاوے کے طور پر بیان کیا جاتا ہے۔ کئی نجاتی شہادتوں میں مشاہدہ کیا گیا ہے کہ گواہان نے یاد کیا کہ وہ اپنے گناہ اور بدکاری کی زندگی میں بالکل مطمئن تھے جب اچانک انہیں شاول کی مانند گرا دیا جاتا اور وہ خود کو قابو میں نہ رکھ پاتے بلکہ خدا کے پیچھے چل پڑتے اور اپنی زندگیاں اسے دے دیتے۔ اس ڈرامائی تبدیلی کی سمجھ میں کئی خطرات ہیں، بالخصوص یہ کہ یہ تبدیل شدہ شخص کی تبدیلی کے فیصلے کی ذمہ داری سے استثنا دیتی ہے۔ اس سے مسیحیت کی قیمت گننے کا فقدان پیدا ہوتا ہے، یعنی خود کی موت، غرور کی موت، اور انسان کی حمایت کی موت۔ اگر مومن بغیر سوچے سمجھے مسیحیت میں کود پڑے، یہ نہ گن کر کہ اسے اپنے سابقہ مفادات کو ترک کرنا ہوگا، تو وہ روحانی طور پر کیسے بڑھ پائے گا اگر وہ اپنی سابقہ برائیوں کو چھوڑ نہ سکے؟ اگرچہ یہ قسم کی تبدیلی آغاز میں حقیقی ہو سکتی ہے، مگر اکثر یہ کلام کے دودھ سے آگے بڑھ کر اس گوشت تک نہیں پہنچ پاتی جسے بالغ مسیحی کھانا چاہیے۔ مسیحی کے اس پختہ ہونے پر زور سِمنز سے لیکر ابراہیم گوشالک تک کی تحریروں میں ملتا ہے۔ کلیسیا کے مفاد کے لیے بھی ضروری ہے کہ مومن مضبوطی سے وابستہ اور اپنے ایمان کی مسلسل بڑھوتری میں شامل ہو۔

ایک پاک کلیسیا کی سنجیدگی

ابتدائی امریکن مینو نائٹس کے نزدیک کلیسیا کا تصور ہمارے موجودہ حال سے زیادہ سنجیدہ اور کم فردی نوعیت کا معلوم ہوتا ہے۔ نامیاتی مسیحیت کی حالت اس قابل افسوس ہے کہ کلیسیا ایک سماجی تنظیم بن چکی ہے جس میں تمام گناہ اور بگاڑ کے لیے جگہ ہے۔

یہ ہمارے لیے مناسب ہے کہ ہم غور سے اُس کلیسیا کے کردار پر نظر کریں جو مسیح نے قائم کی اور ساتھ ہی اُن سچے کلیساؤں کے کردار کو نوٹ کریں جو بدذہبی اور سستی سے پاک ہیں۔ یہ کردار، مسیح کی مانند، سادہ ہے اور پھر بھی معنویت اور روحانی زرخیزی میں بہت بھرپور ہے۔

کلیسیا کا پہلا پہلو جو پہچانا جانا چاہیے وہ اس کی دلہنِ مسیح کے طور پر پاک حالت ہے۔ یہاں پھر ہمیں مسیح کے کردار پر غور کرنا چاہیے۔ کیا اُس نے کبھی اپنے لیے گناہ کی گنجائش رکھی؟ کیا ہمیں اسے کبھی کسی ‘‘شرمناک لطف’’ سے مختصر لطف اندوز ہوتے پایا؟ سمجھدار قاری اتفاق کرے گا کہ مسیح اپنی پوری حیثیت میں پاک تھا، اور تو پھر دلہن کیسی ہوگی جس کے ساتھ وہ دائمی اور قرِیب رشتہ میں بندھنے جا رہا ہے؟ ہمارے ذہنوں کی مدد کے لیے آئیں ہم اس آسمانی اتحاد کے زمینی علامت پر غور کریں: ایک مرد اور عورت جو زندگی بھر ایک دوسرے کے ساتھ بندھے رہتے ہیں۔ یہ زمینی اتحاد غیر مسیحیوں کے ذریعے بھی بطور ایک خصوصیت پہچانا جاتا ہے کہ یہ دونوں افراد کے لیے مخصوص ہے، ایک رشتہ اور ایک دوسرے کا باہمی اشتراک جو کسی بیرونی شخص کے لیے کبھی حصہ نہیں ہوتا۔ یہ ہمارے دنیاوی ذہنوں کے لیے مسیح اور اس کی دلہن کے ارادے کو واضح طور پر پیش کرتا ہے۔ دلہن اور مسیح ایک دوسرے کے لیے ہیں اور خود کو کسی اور کے لیے نہیں دیتے۔

اب جب ہم کلیسیا کی پاکیزگی دیکھ سکتے ہیں، تو آئیں اس کے عملی اظہار کو زوال پذیر انسان میں جانچیں۔ اگر یہ پاک رہنی ہے تو ہم اس کا حصہ کیسے بنیں؟ یہاں رجعت (regeneration) کی واضح سمجھ ضروری ہوتی ہے، ایک ایسا عقیدہ جسے ان مینو نائٹ بزرگوں نے بلند مقام دیا تھا۔ انہوں نے سکھایا کہ روح القدس وہ روحانی دھلائی اور صفائی کرتا ہے جو مومن کے سوچ اور اعمال میں ایک بدلتی ہوئی حالت کے طور پر واضح ہو جاتی ہے۔ یہ تبدیلی پھر بھی ہماری زوال پذیر فطرت کے ساتھ متصادم ہے، مگر مسلسل تسلیم اور گہری عاجزی کے ذریعے، روح مومن کو بھر دے گا یہاں تک کہ گناہ کی فطرت غالب کے بجائے مغلوب ہو جائے گی۔ یہ جاننا ضروری ہے کہ گناہ پر یہ فتح مومن کے اپنے ارادے کو سرنگوں کر کے اور روح کو مکمل کنٹرول دینے کے ذریعے لائی جاتی ہے۔

یوں ایک پاک کلیسیا وہ مومنوں کا گروہ ہے جو سر تسلیم خم کیے ہوئے اور روح سے بھرا ہوا ہے اور حقیقی عاجزی میں پہچانتا ہے کہ ان کی قوت کسی بھی طرح ان کی اپنی شایستگی سے وابستہ نہیں ہے۔ غرور کی غیر موجودگی، جو صرف روح کی مسلسل مدد سے حاصل ہو سکتی ہے، راضی مومن کے مزید پاک ہونے کے لیے مزید گنجائش فراہم کرتی ہے۔ اس طرح ہم مسیحی زندگی کو عملی طور پر سمجھ سکتے ہیں۔

عملی عیسائیت کی تعلیمات

ابتدائی امریکن مینو نائٹس کے ایمان کی عملی نوعیت مسلسل عیاں رہی۔ اپنی کتاب "Pride and Humility" میں، جان ایم۔ برینمین یہ مؤقف رکھتے ہیں کہ ایک شخص کا ظاہری اظہار براہِ راست اس کے دل کے اندر سے متعلق ہوتا ہے، ایک نقطۂ نظر جو فرد کے اعمال تک بھی پھیلا ہوا ہے۔ ارادتمند نجات، رجعت، اور ایک پاک کلیسیا کے ان عقائد پر تعمیر کرنا ضروری ہے جو پہلے جا کر جائزہ لیے گئے، تاکہ مینو نائٹ کے روزمرہ روابط کے ذہنیت کا فریم فراہم کیا جا سکے۔

ان سنجیدہ مزاج مسیحیوں کے لیے، اتوار کو اظہار پانے والا مذہبی عقیدہ اور ہفتے کے باقی دنوں کے عام اعمال میں کوئی اہم فرق نہیں تھا۔ یہ اُن کے سیاسی معاملات اور دنیاوی نوعیت کے دیگر عناصر سے عمومی پرہیز سے ثابت ہوتا ہے جو اُن کے رکھے ہوئے عقائد پر اثر انداز ہوتے۔ اس نے انہیں اپنی روز کی کلیساؤں کے مقابلے میں براہِ راست مخالفت میں رکھا، جہاں دو مکتبِ فکر پروان چلے: یا تو انسان کے زمینی فرائض سیاسی طور پر اس کے ایمان سے مکمل طور پر جدا انجام پائے جاتے تھے، یا یہ کہ ان شہری فرائض کا انجام خدا کی مرضی میں شامل سمجھا جاتا اور لہٰذا مسیحی کے لیے آزادانہ طور پر شامل ہونا جائز تھا۔

ابتدائی امریکن مینو نائٹ کے نزدیک، ایسے موقف اس کے مسیحیت کے اصل معنی کی خیانت کرتے تھے: وہ ایک نیا شخص تھا، صرف اُس مسیح کی قوت میں زندہ جو اُس میں بہتی تھی۔ اس نے اس کی زندگی کے ہر پہلو کو متاثر اور ہدایت کیا، اس کے کاروباری معاملات سے جو اس طرح انجام پاتے کہ کسی فریق کا فائدہ نہ لیا جائے، اس کے لباس اور اطوار تک جو عاجزی اور سادگی پر مبنی ہونے چاہئیں، اس کے اپنے ہم نوع کے ساتھ گفتگو کے طریقے تک جو روحانی خیر خواہی اور ابدی مقدّر کے بارے میں حقیقی فکر دکھائیں۔

نتیجہ

ان تمام نوآبائشی مینو نائٹ عقائد کا خلاصہ یہ تھا کہ بالغ، عاجز، توبہ کار، مگر روحانی طور پر قوت یافتہ خدا کے خادم میں کیسے بڑھا جائے۔ اس نے اپنے گرد کی دنیا کے لالچوں کو انکار کیا اور اپنے ایمان کی پاکیزگی اور سابقہ گناہوں کے ارادی ترک کے بدلے میں وعدہ کی گئی ابدی جزا کو پسند کیا۔ ہمیں جیسی مومنوں نے یہ مثال زندہ کر کے دکھائی، وہ ہمیں مملکتِ خدا کی طرف مزید دباؤ ڈالنے، عاجزی اور توبہ میں اپنے ایمان کو عملی طور پر نبھانے کی ترغیب دینی چاہیے۔

Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Maadili yanahusiana na tabia za haki na ujinga. Usafi ni kuwa huru kutokana na kosa la kimaadili au hatia, ukionekana kwa uzingatiaji wa uzembe, ambao ni uadilifu wa kibinafsi. Usafi haujumuishi chochote ambacho haki yake siyo sehemu yake. Kama ilivyoonyeshwa na kichwa, makala haya yatakuwa kuhusu kufanya mema na kuwa huru kutokana na kosa la kimaadili na hatia, kuishi maisha ya uadilifu, na kuweka ndani na nje mwetu huru ya chochote ambacho haki yake siyo sehemu yake.

Angalia kile Biblia inasema kuhusu kuwa mweupe. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” Kwa maneno mengine, ni watu ambao wapo safi ndani na nje watakaoona Mungu na kuingia katika uwepo Wake.

Kuishi kwa usafi wa kimaadili haitatokea bila azimio kali na nidhamu. Daima imekuwa hivyo, lakini hata zaidi leo kwa kuongezeka kwa teknolojia na upatikanaji wa uovu kwa urahisi mikononi mwetu.

Mavunjo ya ngono si mambo ya kigeni kwa kanisa. Kwa kweli, hayakuwa kigeni kwa watu wa rangi yoyote. Hatuwezi kupumzika na kuacha ulinzi wetu tukidhani watoto wetu watakuwa salama dhidi ya mabaya ya jamii na ubinadamu wetu. Lazima tuwaonyeshe kwa mfano na kuwafundisha watoto na vijana wetu ikiwa tunatarajia wawe watsafi katika jamii hii iliyo uchafu. Hatuwezi kudhani kwamba mtu akivaa kwa namna fulani, kila kitu ndani ni sawa. Hadithi haiambiwi kwa ukamilifu na muonekano wa nje. Mafarisayo walifanya muonekano wa nje uonekane mzuri, wakati ndani kulikuwa na uharibifu. Yesu alisema, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Hata sisi tunapaswa kutoa kipaumbele kwa matatizo ya moyo. Moyo ukiwa safi, basi nje pia itaweza kusafishwa.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Giza la ndani daima litaangamiza ushirikiano na kuua mahusiano—kila wakati.

Hii inakusudiwa kuwa ujumbe wa matumaini, sio kukata tamaa. Ikiwa una sehemu ya giza iliyofichika, itikie na uiondoe. Unaweza kuwa huru! Inawezekana kuwa huru kutokana na wavu wa Shetani na kuishi maisha ya uwazi, wazi na furaha ndani ya roho yako. Huna haja ya kuishi njia ya kujaribu kuficha giza la uovu. Yesu anataka kusamehe na kuponya.

Shetani ni mnyanyasaji. In John 10:10, Yesu alisema, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” mahusiano yote ya kimungu. Maslahi yake ni kuvunja nyumba yako, kuharibu heshima yako, na kukutuma kuzimu. Wakati wote, anakurudisha kupitia tamaa za mwili wako, na upanga wake umechomolewa kukufunga na kukuua.

Dhambi za kimaadili ni aibu sana na ngumu kutamka. Jambo la kawaida ni kujaribu kuficha tunapofanya vibaya. Watoto wanaojifunza kuficha maovu mapema maishani kawaida hukua na kuwa vijana wanaoficha vitu kutoka kwa wazazi, walimu shuleni, na makasisi. Mtu huyu atahitaji kujifunza kuwa wazi na waziwazi, au wakati utafika atakapoanza kuficha vitu hata kwa mwenzi wake. Kuficha kunaofanya maisha ya pacha na kusababisha utegemezi zaidi na mahusiano yaliyovunjika. Watu walio na milango iliyofungwa katika pembe fulani za maisha yao watakuwa wenye kumiliki simu zao na wasiotaka kushiriki nywila zao za siri na mwenzi wa kuaminika. Inaonekana tunasahau kwa urahisi jinsi ilivyo bure kuficha kutoka kwa Mungu. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Je, tunaweza kuwa wavivu na wajinga kiasi gani kufikiri tunaweza kuficha lolote kwa Mungu? Au kuchukua hatua zaidi: Kwa nini tungependelea kuficha kitu kwake? Numbers 32:23 bado ni kweli sana, ikisema, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Mungu anakupenda mno kiasi kwamba hatakuacha utiwa wa kuficha kile kinachohitaji kuletwa nje na kusamehewa.

Mavunjo ya ngono pia ni ya udanganyifu mkubwa. Kwa kawaida hutokea jinsi James alivyoiweka kwenye sura ya kwanza. Tunavutwa, tunavutwa mbali, tunavutwa kama sumaku kutoka katikati, tunahisi msukumo wa tamaa, tukihakikisha hakuna mtu anayeangalia, na alama zetu zimefunikwa, hatua zinakaribia marufuku, tamaa inazidi, na kuanza kwa haraka kupoteza uwezo wa kufikiri na kukisia matokeo kama mtu aliyekonywa hadhi, kisha James 1:15 inatokea: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James angesema tusitamani kile ambacho si chetu, hata ishara moja. Biblia inatuambia kukimbia vitu vitatu. Moja yao ni ubabaishaji, ambao unaweza kupanuliwa hadi dhambi zote za ngono. Usicheze nayo; usitazame mara ya pili; kimbia! Badilisha mawazo hayo na mawazo yanayojenga ya Mungu na njia Yake. Imba wimbo wa kale; kwa bahati nzuri hatuwezi kufikiri vitu viwili kwa wakati mmoja. Ni chochote itakayochukua, kimbia tamaa hiyo ya tendo la kimahaba. Itakupeleka mbali zaidi ya unavyotaka kwenda na itagharimu zaidi ya unavyotaka kulipa. Endesha filamu hadi mwisho na jiulize, ikiwa nitafuata kilichoniangusha, nitapata kile ninachotaka? Shetani daima ahalalisha raha, lakini kisha analeta maumivu. Kumbuka, Shetani hajawahi kubuni raha; yeye tu huchukua kile Mungu alichotengeneza kuwa safi na kizuri, anakichafua, na kukirudisha kwa sura yake iliyoharibika. Kumbuka, upanga wa Shetani umechomolewa kuua kwa wakati huu. Kimbia tamaa za uovu!

Usifuate tamaa yako. Utiririshaji wa picha na video za ngono ni wa kutegemeza sana na umewashikwa wengi. Promise Keepers alisema asilimia 65 ya wanaume katika utafiti wao walikuwa wamegandamizwa. Uenezaji wa picha za ngono unafananishwa na pombe au madawa. Wanatuambia kwamba ubongo unataka endorphins zitolewe ndani yake, iwe kutokana na uraibu wa pombe, madawa, au picha za ngono. Ninaeleza tena kwamba wanaume na wanawake wanaofika kuwa wa kushinda watakuwa wale ambao, kama Daniel wa zamani, watakubali moyoni mwao, wasajisababishaji uchafu.

Mada hii pia ni kwa dada zetu, na maswali machache yanayofaa. Kuna nini ndani ya maisha yako kilichofungwa vizuri na kufichwa? Je, kukatishwa tamaa kwa maisha kumesababisha utupu unaofanya kuchukua 'Tylenol ya hisia' kukufanya uhisi vizuri kwa muda mfupi? Je, uhusiano wako wa kihisia uko salama mahali Mungu alikusudia kuweka?

Wasichana wadogo wanapaswa kufundishwa kuendeleza hifadhi yenye afya kwa wanaume. Sio kwa mtazamo wa kiburi na kamwe bila tabasamu, lakini pia sio kuwa huru kupita kiasi katika kuhusiana na wavulana. Jamii yetu imepangwa kinyume kabisa, na kuanzia chekechea, wavulana na wasichana wanatajwa kuhusu urafiki maalum. Kwa matokeo, watoto hukua wakiwa na uhifadhi mdogo au bila kabisa. Kujumuika kwa ujumbe kati ya jinsia tofauti kunapaswa kuepukwa nje ya uhusiano wa kifamilia. Hii itakuza tabia kwa vijana ambayo siku moja itabidi ivunjwe ikiwa wanatarajia kuishi maisha ya uwazi na mke/mume. Fikiria hivi: ungependa mwenzi wako kujumuika na jinsia ya kinyume kwenye mitandao ya kijamii?

Dada, kuwa makini na vitabu unavyosoma. Riwaya za kimapenzi hupunguza hamu ya Neno la Mungu na kutoa matarajio yasiyo halisi ya maisha ya ndoa. Vitabu hivi vinatoa wazo kwamba mwanaume sahihi mahali fulani atakuwa ufunguo wako wa kutimizwa na furaha maishani. Ni Yesu pekee ndiye anaweza kujaza shimo ambalo dhambi imeleta kwa kila binadamu leo. Hakuna mwanaume au mwanamke atakayewahi kuweza kutoa usalama na utulivu wa nafsi tunayotaka sana. Maumivu haya moyoni hayataguzwa na kile kinachofungwa kwa banda au vidonge vya maumivu. Husaidia kwa muda tu, na vinapotoweka, kilio cha moyo kinakuwa kwa sauti kubwa zaidi. Vitabu zisizofaa hupunguza tamu ya vitu vya Mungu, na badala yake huunda hamu ya vyakula vya taka na vidonge vya maumivu.

Tatizo jingine kwa dada ni kiasi cha muda unaotumia mtandaoni. Hakuna mwisho wa kutosheleza tamaa ya umaridadi, kipekee, mvuto, na uzuri. Usiruhusu mambo haya kuwa nguvu inayoendesha maisha yako kwa kuwa hayatatafuta kamwe 'sawa' na hayatatoa chochote kukidhi nafsi au kumwelekeza watoto wako kwa njia sahihi. Fikiria kiasi cha wakati unaotumia kuandaa sherehe. Kwa miaka, nimeona majina yanakuja na kupita ya fursa za biashara na bidhaa zinazopaswa kuwa nazo. Lakini kwa huzuni, katika miaka michache, hatuwezi hata kukumbuka yale majina wakati watoto walikuwa wakikua na sasa ni watu wazima. Fikiria mahitaji halisi katika maisha yako na wajibu wako, kisha uamue ni yapi yatakayoweka uwekezaji wa milele. Wanawake wenye watoto wanahitaji kupunguza vishawishi vinavyowafurahisha mno kwa sababu, kwa sasa, wamebarikiwa na watoto wenye roho zisizo za kifo na muda pamoja nao ni uwekezaji wa milele. Kumbuka kwamba mumeo na watoto wako wanastahili zaidi wakati wako kuliko kutumia masaa kwenye sherehe nyingine.
