A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

En vidunderlig ting ved å være kristen er å se fram til den dag vi får skue vår Guds praktfulle skjønnhet. Sannsynligvis har vi alle laget mentale bilder av hvordan vi tror Gud kan se ut, selv om vi vet at selv våre villeste forestillinger vil bli overgått. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). Bibelen er full av beskrivende billedspråk som forsøker å gi oss et glimt inn i himmelens riker. Landskapet på herlighetens åser, de underfulle skapningene som bor der, og framfor alt, Den høyeste Vesenet på tronen, trosser alle våre menneskelige forsøk på å gripe og forstå Guds skjønnhet og herlighet.

Noen ganger beundrer vi skjønnhet i en sang, et kunstverk, en historie eller til og med et annet menneske, men David beskriver gleden ved å skue Guds skjønnhet. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). Gud er vakker fordi Hans overlegenhet er tiltrekkende—Hans karakter er feilfri. David erfarte den glede som kommer av å kjenne og erfare Gud i all Hans fylde. Hvordan uttrykker Gud Sin skjønnhet?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). I grusomheten i Kristi lidelse finner vi en dyp og alvorlig skjønnhet—skjønnheten i et offer utført av en syndfri Frelser for et ufortjent menneskeegg. Noen ganger finnes den mest gripende typen skjønnhet i ting vi ikke fullt ut kan fatte.

Det er skjønnhet i Marias og disiplene gråt rundt korset som holdt den livløse kroppen til deres elskede Mester. Men da morgenen for oppstandelsen brøt frem, ble fortvilelse til håp og sorg til glede.

Vi ser en vakker scene på Oljeberget førti dager etterpå mens de samme disiplene lengselsfullt stirret mot himmelen og så deres oppstandne Herre forsvinne opp. Med stor glede vendte de tilbake til Jerusalem, med løftet om Hans tilbakekomst brennende i hjertene, for å vente på Den Hellige Ånds komme.

I dag venter vi forventningsfullt på at Guds Sønn skal åpenbares fra himmelen med makt og stor herlighet for å fullføre frelsens verk. Da skal vi skue Ham i all Hans prakt og skjønnhet. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

Hvordan skal vi, som Guds bildebærere, reflektere Hans skjønnhet gjennom evangeliet? Gud er et u skapt evig vesen, og mennesket ble skapt i Hans bilde for å gjenspeile Hans herlighet og skjønnhet. Denne skjønnheten er imidlertid blitt skjemmet av synd og er ikke lenger en verdig framstilling av Guds karakter. Men det finnes forløsning! Lite overgår skjønnheten i et liv som en gang var såret og knust av synd, men som nå er gjenopprettet, forløst og gjort helt ved Evangeliet. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Ateister utfordrer Guds eksistens, vitenskapsmenn argumenterer mot bibelsk skapelse, lærde stiller spørsmål ved Skriftens feilfrihet, men ingen kan motstride vitnesbyrdet fra et forløst liv.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All skjønnhet i den skapte verden kommer fra Gud. En vakker solnedgang, en yndig rose, en mektig redwood, et majestetisk fjelltopp, vitner alle om Guds skjønnhet illustrert i skaperverket. Som veikart langs motorveien leder oss til målet, slik peker også skaperverket mennesket mot Gud selv. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). Disse gavene i skaperverket er gitt for å gi oss et kort glimt av Den som skapte dem.

Hvordan skal vi, som en del av Guds skapning, gjenspeile Hans kreative skjønnhet? Selv om vi ikke kan skape noe av intet, har Gud designet oss til å være skapende, bruke ressursene i Hans skapelse og våre intellektuelle evner for å gjøre livet praktisk. Den tilfredsstillende følelsen av å fullføre en god jobb har sitt utspring i skapelsen, hvor Gud så på sitt verk og erklærte det for godt. I vårt forsøk på å leve nøkterne liv mislykkes vi noen ganger med å glede oss over livets vakre ting. Det er riktig og godt og i samsvar med hvordan vi er skapt å finne glede i skjønnhetens ting. Ugudelige mennesker har ofte brukt denne gavens kreativitet til onde formål. Så la oss desto mer ære Gud ved å bruke Hans skapelse på måter som reflekterer Hans karakter.

En advarsel til alle som elsker naturen og skapelsen (både naturlig og menneskeskapt): la oss være forsiktige med å ikke opphøye jordisk skjønnhet over Skaperen, for det fører til avgudsdyrkelse. Solnedganger falmer, redwoodtrær faller, roser visner, menneskekroppen vender tilbake til støv igjen, men Gud blir. Livet og all dets skjønnhet begynner og ender med Gud.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) Ifølge Johannes' åpenbaring er Guds trone omgitt av lyd: torden og lyn; lovsanger fra englene, de fire vesenene og tjue eldste, og den store mengden som ingen kan telle; og den nye sangen fra de hundre og førti tusen.

Gud skapte lydens skjønnhet for å ære Seg selv på måter rene ord ikke kan. Hans skapende intrikate natur vises kraftfullt i hvordan ulike lydfrekvenser smelter sammen og skaper en vakker og himmelsk harmoni. Det ærer Gud at mennesket finner glede i de lydenes skjønnhet Han har skapt til Sin pris. Den som elsker Gud, vil bli trukket til Ham når Han blir serenadert av behagelige lyder: Guds folk som synger Sions sanger, de helliges bønner, vinden som hvisker gjennom tretoppene, spurven som priser Skaperen, tordens rumling eller den enkle rytmen av regn mot taket.

Hvordan skal vi, som lydenes instrumenter, reflektere Guds skjønnhet gjennom lyd? Vi bør alltid søke å lytte til og ligne himmelens lyder og harmonier. Selv om vi aldri helt kan oppnå dette på jorden, bør det være et livslangt strev. Spørsmålene har blitt stilt: ”Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” og ”when have we reached ‘good enough’?” Vi kommer aldri til å nå himmelsk perfeksjon, så spørsmålet bør heller være, ”Gir vi Gud det beste vi har?” Noen har større sanggave enn andre, men spørsmålet står igjen. ”Gir vi vårt beste eller er vi fornøyd med et dårligere offer?” La oss være skapere av Gud-ærede lyder som bringer glede i Skaperens hjerte!

Through the Church:

Bibelen taler utførlig om skjønnheten til Guds folk. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” og “The Church” er synonyme uttrykk vevd gjennom Skriften som peker til Guds folks bolig på jorden. Det er Guds ønske at Hans skjønnhet skal gjenspeiles i Hans folks liv. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Intet er kjærere for Guds hjerte enn Hans kirke. Da Israels barn vandret gjennom ørkenen, bygde de tabernaklet som et sted for Gud å bo midt blant dem. Da Salomo vigslet tempelet som Guds bolig, var Gud meget tilfreds og 2 Chronicles 7:1 sier at Herrens herlighet fylte tempelet. Tempelet ble ansett som Herrens Hus—Jesus selv refererte til det mange ganger som Guds hus og var svært lidenskapelig opptatt av at det skulle holdes hellig.

I dag er det verken tabernaklet eller tempelet som rommer Guds nærvær, men Hans guddommelige lidenskap er konsentrert om Jesu Kristi kirke. Her er de menneskene som virkelig elsker Ham og er villige til å legge ned sine liv for Ham. Her er de som er villige til å gi avkall på sine individuelle rettigheter og overgi seg til en større sak. Her har mange en hellig gitt sitt livs blod for evangeliet. Og her er stedet hvor vår Frelser en dag vil vende tilbake som Han har lovet, og skal føre Sin brud, kirken, til hennes evige bolig. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

Hvordan skal vi, som Guds folk, reflektere Hans skjønnhet i kirken? Ved å bo sammen i enhet og harmoni med kjærlighet for alle mennesker, spesielt Guds husstand. Kirken bør være et sted hvor verden kan få et glimt av hva som foregår i himmelen. Det bør være et sted hvor Kristus alltid blir opphøyd som den seierende erobrer over synd, død og helvete.

Trist nok har mange blitt desorientert av kirkens svik og har vendt seg bort fra den sanne apostoliske tro. Til tross for våre skuffelser, la oss ”lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) og la oss stride videre. Vi vil aldri ha et høyere kall, og aldri en mer edel krig å føre.

Til sist, hvordan skal vi gjenspeile Hans skjønnhet i våre liv? Ved å fryde oss i Ham. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). Den største oppfyllelse i livet kommer av å finne glede i å bringe fryd til Guds hjerte ved å fryde seg i det Han fryder seg i og elske det Han elsker. La oss aldri miste undringen over skjønnheten i vår frelse!

Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Moraal het te doen met reg en verkeerd gedrag. Suiwerheid is vry wees van morele fout of skuld, gekenmerk deur kuisheid, wat persoonlike integriteit is. Suiwerheid bevat niks wat nie behoorlik daar hoort nie. Soos die titel aandui, gaan hierdie artikel oor om reg te doen en vry te wees van morele fout en skuld, om ’n lewe van integriteit te leef, en ons binne- en buitekant vry te hou van enigiets wat nie behoorlik daar hoort nie.

Let op wat die Skrif sê oor suiwer wees. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Om moreel suiwer te wees sal nie gebeur sonder sterke vasberadenheid en dissipline nie. Dit was nog altyd so, maar selfs meer vandag met die opkoms van tegnologie en die beskikbaarheid van die boos by ons vingerpunte.

Seksuele sondes is nie vreemd aan die kerk nie. In werklikheid is hulle nie vreemd aan enige mense van enige ras nie. Ons kan nie ontspan en ons wag laat sak en veronderstel dat ons kinders veilig sal wees van die booshede van die samelewing en ons menslikheid nie. Ons moet deur voorbeeld wys en ons kinders en jeug leer as ons verwag dat hulle skoon sal bly in hierdie korrupte samelewing. Ons kan nie aanvaar dat as ’n persoon op ’n sekere manier aantrek, alles binne-in reg sal wees nie. Die storie word nie volledig deur die buitekant vertel nie. Die Fariseërs het die buitekant laat lyk goed, terwyl die binne-in vol bederf was. Jesus het gesê, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Ons behoort ook primêre aandag aan hartkwessies te gee. Wanneer die hart skoon is, kan die buitekant ook gesuiwer word.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Interne duisternis sal altyd gemeenskap vernietig en verhoudings doodmaak—elke keer.

Hierdie boodskap is bedoel om hoop te bring, nie ontmoediging nie. As jy ’n verborge donker kol het, bely dit en raak daarvan ontslae. Jy kan vry wees! Dit is moontlik om vry te wees van Satan se kloue en ’n oop, deursigtige lewe met vreugde in jou siel te leef. Jy hoef nie deur die lewe te gaan en te probeer om die duisternis van boosheid te verberg nie. Jesus wil vergewe en genees.

Satan is wreed. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Morele sonde is so skaam en moeilik om te bely. Die natuurlike ding is om te probeer wegsteek wanneer ons verkeerd doen. Kinders wat baie vroeg in die lewe leer om verkeerde dade te verberg, ontwikkel natuurlik in jongmense wat dinge wegsteek vir ouers, skoolonderwysers en ministers. Hierdie persoon sal moet leer om oop en deursigtig te wees, of die tyd sal kom wanneer hulle dinge van hul maat sal wegsteek. Wegsteek lei tot ’n dubbele lewe en lei tot meer band en gebroke verhoudings. Mense wat geslote deure in sekere hoeke van hul lewe het, sal besitterig wees oor hul fone en onwillig om hul wagwoorde met ’n betroubare maat te deel. Dit lyk of ons maklik vergeet hoe nutteloos dit is om God te probeer verberg. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Hoe kan ons so naief en dwaas wees om te dink ons kan enigiets vir God wegsteek? Of neem dit ’n stap verder: Waarom sou ons iets van Hom wou verberg? Numbers 32:23 is nog steeds baie waar en sê, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God het te veel liefde vir jou om jou toe te laat om te bly wegsteek wat uitgedra en vergewe moet word.

Seksuele sondes is ook uiters misleidend. Dit gebeur gewoonlik soos James dit in hoofstuk een beskryf het. Ons word verlei, weggetrek, soos ’n magneet uit die sentrum getrek, voel ’n oplewing van begeerte, maak seker niemand kyk nie, doek ons spore toe, skuif ’n tree nader aan die verbode, voel meer begeerte, en begin baie vinnig rede en gesonde denke verloor, nie in staat om gevolge te bereken nie, baie soos ’n dronk persoon, dan gebeur James 1:15: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James sou vir ons sê om nie te begeer na wat nie onsne is nie, nie eers ’n wenk daarvan nie. Die Bybel sê ons moet drie dinge vlug. Een van hierdie is hoererij, wat uitgebrei kan word tot alle seksuele sondes. Moenie daarmee speel nie; moenie twee keer kyk nie; kom weg daarvandaan! Vervang daardie gedagtes met opbouende gedagtes oor God en Sy weg. Sing ’n ou hymne; dankbaarlik kan ons nie aan twee dinge terselfdertyd dink nie. Wat ook al nodig is, vlug van daardie wellustige begeerte. Dit sal jou verder neem as wat jy wil gaan en meer kos as wat jy wil betaal. Dra die band tot die einde en vra jouself, as ek volg wat ek versoek word om te doen, sal ek kry wat ek wil hê? Satan beloof altyd plesier, maar lewer dan pyn. Onthou, Satan het nog nooit ’n plesier uitgevind nie; hy neem net wat God gemaak het om suiwer en goed te wees, verdraai dit, en bied dit terug in sy verdraaide vorm. Onthou, Satan se swaard is op hierdie punt getrek om te dood. Vluig boosheid!

Moenie jou lus volg nie. Pornografie is uiters verslawend en het baie mense in sy net gevang. Promise Keepers het gesê 65% van mans in hul opname was verslaaf. Pornoverslawing is soos alkohol of dwelms. Hulle sê vir ons dat die brein vra vir endorfiene om daarin uitgegooi te word, hetsy uit verslawing aan alkohol, dwelms, of porn. Ek beklemtoon weer dat die mans en vroue wat oorwin sal behaal, dié sal wees wat, soos Daniël van oud, in hul harte vasbesluit het om hulself nie te besmet nie.

Hierdie onderwerp is ook vir ons susters, en ’n paar vrae blyk gepas. Wat binne-in jou lewe is netjies weggesteek en verberg? Het die teleurstellings van die lewe ’n leegheid veroorsaak wat dit laat lyk asof ’n ‘emosionele Tylenol’ jou vir ’n kort rukkie beter laat voel? Is jou emosionele verbintenis seker waar God dit beplan het om te wees?

Jong dogters moet geleer word om ’n gesonde reservaat te ontwikkel met mans. Nie met ’n hoogmoedige houding en nooit ’n glimlag nie, maar ook nie te vrylik in hulle omgang met jong mans nie. Ons samelewing is presies die teenoorgestelde, en van kleuterskool af word seuns en dogters geteister oor spesiale vriendskappe. Gevolglik groei kinders op met min tot geen reserve nie. Sosialisering in boodskapuitruil tussen geslagte moet buite familierelaties vermy word. Dit sal ’n gewoonte ontwikkel in die jeug wat eendag gebreek sal moet word as hulle verwag om ’n oop, deursigtige lewe met ’n huweliksmaat te leef. Dink hieraan: sou jy wil hê jou maat moet met die teenoorgestelde geslag sosiaal wees op sosiale media?

Susters, wees versigtig watter boeke jy lees. Romantiese romans verdof die begeerte na die Woord van God en gee onrealistiese verwagtinge van getroude lewe. Hierdie boeke gee die idee dat die regte man iewers jou sleutel tot vervulling en geluk in die lewe sal wees. Net Jesus kan die gaatjie vul wat sonde by elke mens geskep het. Geen man of vrou sal ooit die sekerheid en rus van die siel kan gee wat ons almal so hartstogtelik begeer nie. Hierdie seer in die hart sal nooit deur pleisters of pynstillers gestil word nie. Hulle help slegs vir ’n oomblik, en wanneer hulle ophou werk, is die hart se kreet selfs harder. Onbehoorlike boeke verdof ’n smaak vir die dinge van God, en skep in plaas daarvan ’n drang na junkkos en pynstillers.

’n Ander bekommernis vir die susters is die hoeveelheid tyd wat julle aanlyn spandeer. Daar is geen einde aan die voed van die drang na netheid, uniekheid, sjarme en skoonheid nie. Moenie toelaat dat hierdie dinge die dryfkrag van jou lewe word nie, want hulle sal nooit uitroep ‘genoeg’ nie en sal niks doen om die siel tevrede te stel of jou kinders in die regte rigting te wys nie. Oorweeg die hoeveelheid tyd wat jy aan partytjies hou. Oor die jare het ek name van sakegeleenthede en produkte sien kom en gaan wat ’n mens móét hê. Maar ongelukkig kan ons na ’n paar jaar nie eens meer daardie name onthou nie en in die tussentyd het die kinders grootgeword en is nou volwassenes. Oorweeg die werklike behoeftes in jou lewe en jou verantwoordelikhede, en besluit dan wat ewigheidsbeleggings sal oplewer. Vroue met kinders moet stokperdjies waarop hulle so baie staatmaak beperk, omdat hulle op hierdie stadium geseën is met kinders wat onsterflike siele het en tyd saam met hulle ’n ewige belegging is. Onthou dat jou man en kinders baie meer die moeite werd is van jou tyd as om ure by nog ’n partytjie deur te bring.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Our spiritual forefathers had much to say on the many issues facing the American Mennonite church in their time, and we can still learn from the collected writings of these church leaders and brethren. We will look first at the hermeneutics of the early American Mennonite church, endeavoring to draw examples from which we, as 21st-century Christians, can learn.

First, the correct interpretation of Scripture was a matter of great importance to these earlier Christians. They had only recently emigrated away from a largely hostile area, where they had been constantly tested to the point of death on matters of faith and now faced a different set of challenges when confronted with peace and religious freedom. We will look at how they navigated these challenges by studying several of their doctrines and practices.

The Doctrine of Nonresistance

One matter that was well interpreted and applied by many of the early Mennonite writers is the principle and doctrine of the nonresistant Christian. Although many of their Anabaptist descendants of today still hold, to varying degrees, this doctrine, it is oftentimes not done with the clarity and solemnity of their forefathers. The early American Mennonites understood nonresistance as a foundational aspect of the Christian life, as it should be, and taught extensively on the practical application and appearance of nonresistance in the life of a believer. Their primary motivation for living peaceably and without malice toward one’s fellow man was the given example of Jesus. Christ typified the acceptable response to violence and ill-will: gentleness, meekness, as befitted one who is called a Lamb.

The Emphasis of Biblical Foundations

There was also a firm focus amongst early Mennonite writers against building doctrine on the writings of men. This emphasis comes through strongly in their works, as they quote Scripture extensively. They made their point by bringing in an example of Christ or by way of an applicable Scripture verse, rather than building on the sandy soil of a man’s opinions. One of the areas in which they did so was the matter of salvation.

Importance of Practical Salvation

We can learn much from the early Mennonites about the practical working out of salvation. First, salvation is portrayed as both an inward and an outward change. The inward is affected first through the working of the Holy Spirit in the willful sinner’s life. It is an important distinction that the sinner is willful. This position was contrary to most of the greater established churches of the time. If a sinner must be willful, then it implies that all men can willfully accept salvation, an idea that is fundamental in nature, if not always verbalized, to the church of today.

In the early Mennonites’ time, predestination as taught by Calvinism seems to have necessitated this emphasis on man’s ability to choose freely, which is still true today. There is also another flavoring of the “unwillingly saved” interpretation, and that comes from the aftereffects of the charismatic movement and the effect it has had on Mennonite and Amish circles. This “unwilling salvation” is not a matter of predestination, but rather is described as almost a coercive calling by the Spirit. It has been observed in several salvation testimonies where the testifiers recalled how they were completely comfortable in their lives of sin and debauchery when suddenly they would be struck down in the manner of Saul and could not help themselves but follow after God and give their lives to Him. There are numerous pitfalls with this dramatic understanding of conversion, namely that it absolves responsibility from the one converted for his decision to convert. This leads to a lack of counting the cost of Christianity, which is a death of oneself, a death of pride, and a death of favor with man. If the believer hops headfirst into Christianity, not reckoning that he must give up all these self-pleasing traits, how will he be able to grow spiritually if he cannot let go of his former vices? While this form of conversion may be genuine at the beginning, it does not often progress beyond the milk of the Word to the meat of which a mature Christian must partake. This maturing of a Christian is emphasized in writings ranging from those of Menno Simons up to Abraham Goshalk. It is also important for the sake of the church that the believer be firmly committed and engaged in the steady growth of his faith.

The Seriousness of a Pure Church

The idea of church to the early American Mennonite seems to have been a more serious thought, less individualistic than our current state. It is the pitiable state of nominal Christianity that the church has become a social organization with room for all sin and depravity.

It behooves us to consider closely the character of the church that Christ established and to note as well the character of the true churches, unspotted by apostasy and laxness. This character is, like Christ himself, simple and yet incredibly full of meaning and spiritual vitality.

The first aspect of the church to recognize is its pure state as the bride of Christ. Here again, we should consider the character of Christ. Did He ever give Himself space for sin? Do we find Him occasionally indulging in a brief enjoyment of a “guilty pleasure”? The understanding reader will agree that Christ was pure in His entirety, and so how else should the bride be with which He is to be intimately and eternally joined? To aid our minds in answering such a question, let us consider the earthly symbol of this heavenly union: that of a man and a woman joined together for life. This earthly union is recognized even by non-Christians as something set aside purely for the two individuals involved, a relationship and a sharing of each other that is not and never to be partaken of by anyone outside of the intimate union. This paints clearly for our earth-bound minds the mind of Christ, insomuch as that marriage is a symbol of Christ and His bride. The bride and Christ are for each other and give themselves to nothing and no one other.

Now that we can see the purity of the church, let us examine its practical working out amongst fallen man. If it is to be pure, then how are we to be a part of it? Here enters the need for a clear understanding of regeneration, a doctrine held in high regard by these Mennonite forefathers. They taught that the Spirit affects the spiritual washing and cleansing that will be made apparent in a changed state of thought and action in the believer. This change is still at variance with our fallen nature, but through continued surrender and a deep humility, the Spirit will fill the believer until the nature of sin becomes the dominated instead of the dominant. It is important to realize, however, that this victory over sin is brought into effect by the believer yielding his will and allowing the Spirit complete control.

Thus, a pure church is a surrendered, Spirit-filled group of believers who recognize in true humility that their power is not in any way linked to their own merit. The absence of pride, achieved only by the constant aid of the Spirit, gives further room for purification of the willing believer. In this way, we can see the Christian life in shoe leather.

The Teachings of Practical Christianity

The practicality of the early American Mennonite’s faith was continually on display. In his book, “Pride and Humility,” John M. Brenneman maintains that the outward appearance of a person is directly related to his inward heart, a view which extends as well to the actions of the individual. It is necessary to build on the beliefs of willful salvation, regeneration, and a pure church previously examined to frame the mindset of a Mennonite’s interactions in daily living.

To these serious-minded Christians, there was no difference in importance between the religious belief expressed on Sundays and the mundane actions of the rest of the week. This is evidenced by their general abstinence from political matters and other elements of a worldly nature that would infringe upon the beliefs they held. This put them in direct opposition to many of the churches of their day, where thrived two schools of thought: either that one’s earthly duties in a political manner were carried out completely separate from one’s faith, or that the accomplishment of these civic duties were incorporated in the will of God and so permissible for the Christian to engage in freely.

To the early American Mennonite, these types of stances betrayed the very meaning of his Christianity: he was a new person, alive only in the power of Christ that flowed through him. This influenced and directed every aspect of his life, from his business dealings, which were carried out in a way so as not to take advantage of any party involved, to his dress and manner of deportment, which was to be based on humility and plainness, to his method of conversing with his fellow man, which was to show a genuine concern for the spiritual well-being and eternal destiny.

Conclusion

The sum of all these colonial Mennonite beliefs was the doctrine of how to grow into a mature, humble, repentant, but spiritually powerful servant of God. He denied the allures of the world around him in favor of an eternal reward promised upon the purity of his faith and willing renunciation of the sin in which he had formerly lived. This example, lived out by believers like us, should inspire us to further press into the Kingdom of God, working out our faith in humility and repentance.

আমাদের আধ্যাত্মিক পূর্বপুরুষরা তাদের সময়ের আমেরিকান মেনোনাইট চার্চকে ঘিরে বহু সমস্যার উপর অনেক কথা বলেছিলেন, এবং আমরা এখনও এই চার্চ নেতাদের ও ভাই-বোনদের সংকলিত রচনাগুলি থেকে শিখতে পারি। আমরা প্রথমে প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইট চার্চের ব্যাখ্যাবিদ্যা (hermeneutics) দেখব, এবং উদাহরণ টেনে এমন শিক্ষা আহরণ করার চেষ্টা করব যেগুলো আমরা, কুড়ি-এক শতাব্দীর খ্রীষ্টানরা, শিখতে পারি।

প্রথমত, বাইবেলের সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা এই আগের খ্রীষ্টানদের কাছে একটি অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ বিষয় ছিল। তারা সম্প্রতি এমন একটি অঞ্চল থেকে অভিবাসী হয়ে এসেছিল যেখানে বেশিরভাগই শত্রুভাবাপন্ন ছিল, যেখানে তারা বিশ্বাস নিয়ে পরীক্ষা-নিরীক্ষায় সর্বশেষ জীবনের বিনিময়ে পর্যন্ত পরীক্ষিত হয়েছে এবং এখন শান্তি ও ধর্মীয় স্বাধীনতার মুখোমুখি হয়ে অন্য ধরনের চ্যালেঞ্জ দেখেছিল। আমরা তাদের কয়েকটি মতবাদ ও অনুশীলনের অধ্যয়নের মাধ্যমে দেখতে চেষ্টা করব তারা কিভাবে এই চ্যালেঞ্জগুলোর মধ্য দিয়ে চলাফেরা করেছিল।

The Doctrine of Nonresistance

একটি বিষয় যা প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইট লেখকদের মধ্যে বহুজনই ভালভাবে ব্যাখ্যা ও প্রয়োগ করেছেন আর তা হলো অপ্রতিরোধী (nonresistant) খ্রীষ্টান নীতিমালা ও মতবাদ। যদিও আজকের অনেক অনাবাপটিস্ট উত্তরসূরি বিভিন্ন মাত্রায় এই মতবাদের প্রতি ধারণা রক্ষা করে, তা প্রায়ই তাঁদের পূর্বপুরুষদের মতো স্পষ্টতা ও গম্ভীরতার সঙ্গে করা হয় না। প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটরা অপ্রতিরোধীতাকে খ্রীষ্টীয় জীবনের একটি মৌলিক দিক হিসেবে বুঝতেন—যেমন হওয়া উচিত—এবং বিশ্বাসীর জীবনে অপ্রতিরোধীতার ব্যবহারিক প্রয়োগ ও রূপটি ব্যাপকভাবে শিখিয়েছেন। সহানুভূতিশীলভাবে শান্তিপূর্ণ ও পরের মানুষের প্রতি কোনো বিদ্বেষ ছাড়া জীবন যাপনের তাদের প্রধান প্রেরণা ছিল যীশুর প্রদত্ত উদাহরণ। খ্রীষ্ট সহিংসতা ও খারাপ ইচ্ছার উপস্থিতিতে গ্রহণযোগ্য প্রতিক্রিয়ার উদাহরণ ছিলেন: নম্রতা, বিনয়, এমন এক ব্যক্তির যোগ্যতা যাকে মেষশাবক বলা হয়।

The Emphasis of Biblical Foundations

প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইট লেখকদের মধ্যে এরাও শক্তভাবে বৈশিষ্ট্যযুক্ত ছিল যে তারা মানুষে রচিত লেখার উপর নির্ভর করে মতবাদের নির্মাণের বিরুদ্ধে স্থির মনোভাব রাখতেন। এই জোর তাদের রচনাগুলোতে স্পষ্টভাবে প্রকাশ পায়, কারণ তারা ব্যাপকভাবে বাইবেল উদ্ধৃত করেছেন। তারা একটি উপযুক্ত বাইবেলিক প্যাসেজ বা খ্রীষ্টের উদাহরণ এনে তাদের বক্তব্য প্রকাশ করতেন, বরং মানুষের মতামতের বালুকাময় মাটিতে ভিত্তি গড়তেন না। ভ্রূণভাবে এক ক্ষেত্র যেখানে তারা এভাবেই আচরণ করেছিলেন তা ছিল উদ্ধার (salvation)-এর বিষয়।

Importance of Practical Salvation

আমরা প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইটদের থেকে উদ্ধারপ্রক্রিয়ার ব্যবহারিক বিশ্লেষণ সম্পর্কে অনেক কিছু শিখতে পারি। প্রথমত, উদ্ধারকে ইঙ্গিত করা হয় যেন তা হোলো অভ্যন্তরীণ ও বাহ্যিক পরিবর্তন—দুইই। অভ্যন্তরীণ পরিবর্তন প্রথমে পবিত্র আত্মার কার্যক্রমের মাধ্যমে অভিলাষী পাপকেই প্রভাবিত করে। এটি একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ভেদ যে পাপী স্বেচ্ছাচারী (willful)। এই অবস্থান তখনকার অধিকাংশ প্রতিষ্ঠিত চার্চের বিপরীত ছিল। যদি পাপীকে স্বেচ্ছাচারী হতে হয়, তাহলে এর অর্থ হলো সমস্ত মানুষই স্বেচ্ছাপূর্বক রক্ষা গ্রহণ করতে পারে, একটি ধারণা যা আজকের চার্চে মৌলিকভাবে বিদ্যমান, যদিও সবসময় মৌখিকভাবে উচ্চারণ করা না-ও হতে পারে।

প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইটদের সময়ে, ক্যালভিনবাদ দ্বারা শেখানো নির্বাচন (predestination) সম্ভবত মানুষের মুক্ত ইচ্ছা গ্রহণের ওপর এই জোরকে প্রয়োজনীয় করেছিল, যা আজও সত্য। আরেকটি রূচি রয়েছে “অনিচ্ছাসন্ত্রীয়ে উদ্ধার” ব্যাখ্যার, যা চারিত্রিক আন্দোলনের পরিণতি এবং মেনোনাইট ও অ্যামিশ পরিধায় এর প্রভাব থেকে উদ্ভূত। এই “অনিচ্ছায় উদ্ধার” কোনোভাবে নির্বাচন থেকে উদ্ভূত নয়, বরং এটি এমন এক প্রায় বলপ্রয়োগী ডাকের মতো বর্ণিত হয় পবিত্র আত্মার দ্বারা। এটি বহু উদ্ধারের সাক্ষ্যপ্রদানে দেখা গেছে যেখানে সাক্ষী ব্যক্তিরা স্মরণ করে যে তারা তাদের পাপ এবং অসভ্যতার জীবন নিয়ে সম্পূর্ণ আরামে ছিল এবং হঠাৎ তারা শাউলের রূপে পতিত হয়েছিল এবং নিজেরাই থামতে পারে না; তাদের বাধ্য হয়ে ঈশ্বরের পিছনে চলে যেতে হয়েছিল এবং তাদের জীবন তেঁহাদের উদ্দেশ্যে উৎসর্গ করতে হয়েছিল। এই নাটকীয় রূপ ধারণা সম্পর্কে বহু জালতা বিদ্যমান, বিশেষত এটি রূপান্তরিত ব্যক্তির উপর তার রূপান্তর গ্রহণের দায়িত্ব থেকে অব্যাহতি দেয়। এটি খ্রিস্টীয়তায় ব্যয় গণনা না করার দিকে নিয়ে যায়—যা নিজেকে মরে ফেলা, অহংকারের মৃত্যু, এবং মানুষের অনুকম্পার মৃ্ত্যু। যদি বিশ্বাসী মাথায় কেবল ঝাঁপিয়ে পড়ে খ্রিস্টীয়তায় এসে, এই নানাবিধ আত্ম-সুখদায়ক স্বভাব ত্যাগ করতে হবে না ভেবে, সে কিভাবে আধ্যাত্মিকভাবে বৃদ্ধি পাবে যদি সে তার পূর্বের অভ্যাস ছাড়তে না পারে? যদিও এই ধরণের রূপান্তর শুরুতে সত্যিকারের হতে পারে, এটা প্রায়শই বাক্যের দুধ থেকে মাংসের দিকে অগ্রসর হয় না, যা পারিপক্ব খ্রীষ্টানকে গ্রহণ করতে হয়। মেনো সিমন্স থেকে শুরু করে অ্যব্রাহাম গোষাল্ক পর্যন্ত রচনায় একটি খ্রিষ্টানের এই পরিণতি প্রাপ্ত হওয়া জোর দিয়েছে। চার্চের কল্যাণের জন্যও এটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ যে বিশ্বাসী দৃড়ভাবে প্রতিশ্রুতিবদ্ধ ও তার বিশ্বাসের ধারাবাহিক বৃদ্ধিতে নিয়োজিত থাকুক।

The Seriousness of a Pure Church

প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটদের জন্য চার্চের ধারণা আরও গম্ভীর ছিল বলে মনে হয়—এটি আমাদের বর্তমান অবস্থার তুলনায় কমই ব্যক্তির উপর নির্ভরশীল ছিল। নামমাত্র খ্রিস্টীয়তার পীড়া হলো যে চার্চটি এখন একটি সামাজিক সংগঠনে পরিণত হয়েছে যেখানে সকল পাপ ও বিস্তারের জন্য জায়গা রয়েছে।

এটি আমাদের বুক কাঁপিয়ে দেয় যে আমরা যেই চার্চটি খ্রীষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠা করেছিলেন তার চরিত্রকে মনোযোগ সহকারে বিবেচনা করি এবং সেই সাথে সঠিক চার্চগুলোর চরিত্রও লক্ষ করি, যেগুলি বিস্তার বা আলশলতার দ্বারা দূষিত হয়নি। এই চরিত্র খ্রীষ্টের মতোই সরল এবং তবু অত্যন্ত গভীর অর্থ ও আধ্যাত্মিক প্রাণশক্তিতে পূর্ণ।

চার্চের প্রথম দিকটি স্বীকৃত করার মতো তার বিশুদ্ধ অবস্থায় অবস্থান হলো খ্রীষ্টের কনেরূপ। এখানে আবারও, আমাদের উচিত খ্রীষ্টের চরিত্র বিবেচনা করা। তিনি কি কখনও নিজের জন্য পাপের জায়গা রেখেছিলেন? কি আমরা তাকে মাঝে মাঝে কোনো সংক্ষিপ্ত “কৃতকর্মের আনন্দ” উপভোগ করতে দেখি? বোঝাপড়া সম্পন্ন পাঠক একমত হবেন যে খ্রীষ্ট সম্পূর্ণরূপে পবিত্র ছিলেন, এবং তাহলে কনে কেমন হওয়া উচিত যার সাথে তিনি ঘনিষ্ঠভাবে এবং চিরকালের জন্য মিলিত হবেন? আমাদের মনের জবাব দেওয়ার জন্য, আসুন আমরা এই স্বর্গীয় মিলনের ভূভিত্তিক প্রতীকটিকে বিবেচনা করি: একটি পুরুষ ও একটি নারী জীবনভর একত্রিত হওয়া। এই পৃথিবীর মিলন এমনকি অবিশ্বাসীরাও এমন কিছু হিসেবে স্বীকার করে যা কেবল সেই দুই ব্যক্তির জন্য পৃথক, একটি সম্পর্ক এবং পারস্পরিক ভাগাভাগি যা কোনোরকমভাবে বা কখনোই ঐ ঘনিষ্ঠ মিলনের বাইরে অন্য কেউ অংশগ্রহণ করবে না। এটি আমাদের পৃথিবীর মস্তিষ্কে স্পষ্টভাবে খ্রীষ্টের মনকে চিত্রায়িত করে, ফেবতু তরকা যে বিবাহ খ্রীষ্ট ও তাঁর কনের প্রতীক। কনে ও খ্রীষ্ট একে অপরের জন্য এবং নিজেদেরকে অন্য কোনো কিছুর বা কারো জন্য দেয় না।

এখন আমরা চার্চের পবিত্রতা দেখতে পেয়েছি, আসুন এটি পতিত মানুষের মধ্যে কিভাবে ব্যবহারিকভাবে কাজ করে তা পরীক্ষা করি। যদি চার্চ বিশুদ্ধ হতে হয়, আমরা কিভাবে এর অংশ হব? এখানে পুনর্জন্মের (regeneration) একটি স্পষ্ট বোঝাপড়ার প্রয়োজন দেখা দেয়—একটি মতবাদ যা এই মেনোনাইট পূর্বপুরুষদের দ্বারা উচ্চ মর্যাদায় ধারণ করা হতো। তারা শেখাতেন যে আত্মা আধ্যাত্মিক ধোয়া ও পরিস্কারের কাজকে প্রভাবিত করে যা বিশ্বাসীর চিন্তা ও কর্মে পরিবর্তন হিসাবে প্রকাশ পাবে। এই পরিবর্তন আমাদের পতিত স্বভাবের সঙ্গে এখনও বৈপরীত্যে থাকে, কিন্তু ধারাবাহিক সমর্পণ ও গভীর বিনয়ের মাধ্যমে, আত্মা বিশ্বাসীকে পূর্ণ করে তুলবে যতক্ষণ না পাপের প্রকৃতি প্রাধান্য নয়, বরং পরাভূত হয়। তবে বুঝতে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ যে পাপের উপর এই জয়টি কার্যকর করা হয় যখন বিশ্বাসী তাঁর ইচ্ছে ছেড়ে দেয় এবং আত্মাকে সম্পূর্ণ নিয়ন্ত্রণের অনুমতি দেয়।

অতএব, একটি বিশুদ্ধ চার্চ হলো আত্মসমর্পিত, আত্মায় পূর্ণ বিশ্বাসীদের একটি দল, যারা সচ্চরিত্রভাবে স্বীকার করে যে তাদের শক্তি কোনোভাবেই তাদের নিজের গুণের সঙ্গে যুক্ত নয়। অহংকারের অনুপস্থিতি, যা কেবলমাত্র আত্মার ধারাবাহিক সহায়তায় অর্জিত হয়, ইচ্ছুক বিশ্বাসীর পরিশুদ্ধতার জন্য আরও জায়গা দেয়। এইভাবে আমরা খ্রীষ্টীয় জীবনকে বাস্তব জুতো-চামড়ায় দেখতে পারি।

The Teachings of Practical Christianity

প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটদের বিশ্বাসের ব্যবহারিকতা নিয়মিতভাবে প্রকাশ পেত। তাঁর বই “Pride and Humility” তে, জন এম. ব্রেনেম্যান রক্ষা করেন যে একজন ব্যক্তির বাহ্যিক চেহারা সরাসরি তাঁর অভ্যন্তরীণ হৃদয়ের সাথে সম্পর্কিত, একটি দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি যা ব্যক্তির কর্মকাণ্ডেও প্রযোজ্য। স্বেচ্ছাচারী উদ্ধার, পুনর্জন্ম, এবং পূর্বোক্ত বিশুদ্ধ চার্চের বিশ্বাসের উপর ভিত্তি করে এই মনোভাব গঠন করা প্রয়োজন যাতে একটি মেনোনাইটের দৈনন্দিন জীবনে মিথস্ক্রিয়ার মানসিকতা ফ্রেম করা যায়।

এই গুরুতর-মনের খ্রীষ্টানদের কাছে রবিবারে প্রকাশিত ধর্মীয় বিশ্বাস এবং সপ্তাহের বাকি অংশে করা সাধারণ কাজগুলোর মধ্যে কোন গুরুত্বপূর্ণ পার্থক্য ছিল না। এটি তাদের সাধারণভাবে রাজনৈতিক বিষয় ও অন্যান্য জাগতিক উপাদান থেকে বিরত থাকার মাধ্যমে প্রমাণিত, যেগুলো তাদের ধারণাগুলোর উপর হস্তক্ষেপ করতে পারত। এটি তাদের সেইকালে অনেক চার্চের সঙ্গে সরাসরি বিরোধ তৈরি করেছিল, যেখানে দুইটি মতের স্কুল বিকশিত হয়েছিল: অথবা যে একজনের পৃথিবীজ চাকুরিগুলো রাজনৈতিকভাবে সম্পূর্ণভাবে তাঁর বিশ্বাস থেকে আলাদা থাকে, অথবা যে এই নাগরিক দায়িত্বগুলোর সফলতা ঈশ্বরের ইচ্ছার অংশ এবং তাই খ্রীষ্টানদের জন্য স্বাধীনভাবে ব্যবসা করা অনুমোদনীয়।

প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটদের জন্য এই ধরনের অবস্থানগুলি তাঁর খ্রিস্টীয়তার প্রকৃত অর্থকে খণ্ডন করতো: তিনি একজন নতুন ব্যক্তি ছিলেন, যিনি কেবল খ্রীষ্টের দ্বারা প্রবাহিত শক্তিতে জীবিত ছিলেন। এটি তাঁর জীবনের প্রতিটি দিককে প্রভাবিত ও নির্দেশিত করত—তার ব্যবসায়িক লেনদেনগুলো, যা কোনো পক্ষকে আরোপ করা থেকে বিরত রেখে পরিচালিত হতো; তার পোশাক ও আচরণ, যা বিনয় ও সরলতার উপর ভিত্তি করে হওয়া উচিত; এবং তার পরের মানুষের সঙ্গে আলাপ-আলোচনা করার পদ্ধতি, যা সত্যিকারের উদ্বেগ প্রদর্শন করে তাদের আধ্যাত্মিক মঙ্গল ও চিরস্থায়ী গন্তব্য সম্পর্কে।

Conclusion

এই সব ঔপনিবেশিক মেনোনাইটধর্মমতের সারাংশ ছিল কিভাবে একজন পরিণত, নম্র, অনুতপ্ত, কিন্তু আধ্যাত্মিকভাবে শক্তিশালী ঈশ্বরের দাস হিসেবে বৃদ্ধি পেতে হয় তার মতবাদ। তিনি চারপাশের বিশ্বের আকর্ষণকে অস্বীকার করতেন এবং তাঁর বিশ্বাসের পবিত্রতা ও পূর্বে যাঁর মধ্যে তিনি বাস করতেন সেই পাপের ইচ্ছাকরণ আন্তরিকভাবে পরিত্যাগ করার বিনিময়ে একটি চিরস্থায়ী পুরস্কারের প্রত্যাশায় বসবাস করতেন। আমাদের মত বিশ্বাসীবৃন্দ দ্বারা জীবিত এই উদাহরণটি আমাদের প্রেরণা হওয়া উচিত যাতে আমরা আরও গভীরভাবে ঈশ্বরের রাজ্যে প্রবেশ করি, নম্রতা ও তাড়না দ্বারা আমাদের বিশ্বাসকে কার্যকর করে তুলি।

“Get out of my shop! I don’t need people like you around me! And never come back!” My lips quivered as I looked into the dark, angry eyes of the yelling man. I blinked back the unbidden tears, realizing that once more, I had to leave this man that I loved. All night I could sense that we were coming to this, and I had tried so hard not to let it happen. With one last attempt, I feebly yelled above the tension, “Ken, we don’t want to ...” but once more, I was rudely cut off. With slumped shoulders and downcast eyes, I turned to escape the confines of his dingy, pawn shop, his ever-crescendoing voice drowning the last hope of respite.

The lingering smell of smoke and the echo of his angry voice joined the troubled thoughts of my emotionally overwrought mind, as I slowly walked up the street. “What do you think, Josh?” I asked my faithful, quiet friend.

“I don’t know, " he responded, and we fell back into silent anguish at the outcome of our supposed Bible study, grasping for an explanation for the terrible response. What could we have done differently? Why could he not accept the truth? What lay behind those flashing eyes, and what memories are stored beneath his ever-crowning beanie?

Ken was born on a country farm in the rolling hills of Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, a splendid place for a curious and adventurous little boy to live.

When Ken was four years old, his parents separated. He had heard them fighting a lot, but he didn’t know that it was possible for Mom and Dad to separate. It crushed his heart and confused his innocent soul. He did not know how to handle the stress and change that was tossed on his peaceful life.

The terror and confusion of his mom hurriedly packing their belongings, loading him and his siblings in the car, and driving away are still riveted in his mind. It made no sense! Why couldn’t they just go home? In his musty bedroom at their little, dingy apartment, he lay staring at the moldy ceiling, wondering endlessly what had gone so wrong.

Ken soon adjusted to his new home in the city of Pottsville with only cars, people, and sidewalks instead of cows, frogs, and mud. But fate did not leave the small security his new lifestyle provided him. His mom was not able to properly care for him and his siblings, and so the children were placed in different foster homes. That was even worse than leaving Dad! The clothes he wore were the only things familiar to him. Instead of understanding and loving him, each new family brought more yelling, hatred, and beating. Terror, tears, loneliness, and pain accompanied him.

Ken thought the second foster home that he was placed in would be a safe, loving home. The dad was tall and strong and appeared to be gentle. The mom was overweight, but her friendly smile resolved his fears. But the first night, when he reached for the food, he accidentally dumped a cup of water. She screamed at him and told him that he was worthless, and she wished they had never gotten him. The dad continued eating as if he didn't hear or care. Why didn’t the strong man stop her?

That evening, Ken crawled into his big, strange bed, already crying in loneliness, when he heard the mom yell. He quickly jumped out of bed and, with trembling legs, slipped behind the door to hide. She charged up the stairs bellowing angrily, and Ken was sure that he was in trouble. To his relief, she continued down the hall. He was still too scared to leave his hiding place for fear of receiving a beating. He wiped his tears as he began to sing under his breath a song he had heard in Sunday school, “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” He stopped to think, and his crying quit. “Then why am I here? " he wondered. “Have I done something wrong? God must not love little children. That song is not true! If God loved me I would not be here!" With that conclusion, he burst into tears and lost hope in God. He woke the next morning, still hidden behind the door.

Darkness had long fallen, and my family was all peacefully sleeping in our old farmhouse. I cried myself to sleep, crying for Ken's soul, crying because I didn’t know what to do, crying because my friend, the man I longed to see at peace with God, hated me.

Ken continued to fire questions. “How can God be good and allow so much bad? How could God let children suffer?” I listened on as he continued saying the same things that I heard so many times before, giving me no chance to talk.

Again, it was time to leave, and I was so glad to do so. He kept talking as we backed out the door. Once more, my friend and I walked up the street —tired, frustrated, and wishing never to come back.

Ken was 13 years old, and his life was no better than it had been when he was first put into the foster system. His life was in turmoil. He was continually yelled at and belittled at home. Ken was tired of crying. No one cared, and there was no one with whom he could share his problem. That’s when he came up with his clever plan. His school friend was a hippie, and his parents traveled a lot. They were called Gypsies. He heard that they were headed to California. So, Ken told them about his terrible life and asked if they would give him a ride. They were glad to help.

That exciting morning, he just did his usual thing. He left for school and instead went to California. He didn’t mind leaving all his stuff behind—he really didn’t have much anyway. His foster parents didn’t even care that he left.

In California, Ken lived on the beach and worked for fishermen, and whoever else needed help. He always had enough to eat and something to do. He had his fellow beach bums, but he was still alone inside. His heart was still empty. He longed for love.

Ken lived on the beach for a year and a half and then hitchhiked to Arizona. There he found a home in a homeless shelter and got a job. He did well and soon was on his own, but his search for love took him down the wrong roads. Ken really wanted to be married to a loving wife and have a family, but the girl he married did not marry him because of love. She was hurt, and Ken’s own hurt soul was attracted to her. They got married and all was well for a few years until he found out that his wife was seeing other men. His heart was broken, and his world was thrown into turmoil. Ken wanted desperately to provide security for the children that were born to them, and so he tried his best to stay together. He did not want to put his children through the life that he experienced. But after eight rough years, they got a divorce.

Ken moved on and tried to recover from the devastation of the divorce. His search for love brought him only more sadness and pain. Since Ken was hurt and unhappy, he found satisfaction in making others happy. He spent all his money on them, and when he had nothing more to offer, they left.

Now Ken is sitting in his pawn shop, alone, hurt, sad, and hiding. He found through his sad life that no one cared. Every time that he opened himself to love, he was always hurt. Deep down inside, he truly felt that God did not care. He lost hope in God, people, and last of all, he lost hope in love itself. That is why we were still visiting the dingy, smoke-stained shop after six years of very little apparent success. God kept bringing us back. He put in us a persistent love and relentless burden for this wounded soul. That is why we spent many hours hearing the same criticisms over and over. The same problems, the same confusion.

Nearly every month, he would fluctuate between hope and despair, love and hate, new life in God, and sadness and sin. We never knew what the next visit would bring. We could be swelling with hope and filled with blessing, or torn with angry words and sickened with dread. But we kept going back, and slowly he emerged from the pit of despair, and slowly allowed himself to be wrapped in the wonderful love of God and the glorious message of His redeeming grace. It was amazing to see the change in his life and to hear his ever-growing confidence in the love of Christ.

Today Ken loves the Lord. He is learning to walk with God. He has seen the love of God. He has found hope in God. He has experienced the unconditional love of God. He is still growing, and we are excited to see what God has for him.

I’m so glad that God brought Ken into my life. God had a plan for Ken and I. God wanted to show Ken that He loved him and that He would be there for him even when Josh turned his back on Him. God also wanted me to carry a burden in my youth. He knew how easily I would be distracted with money and fun. He knew that I needed a burden to carry, a soul to care for. He wanted me to be able to see beneath the shell of a hard soul and see a hurting child within. He wanted to give me a burden too big for me to carry so that I would learn to lean on Him. And most of all, He wanted to equip me to serve Him in broader ways.

Fellow Christians, open your lives to the work of God. Find an opportunity to love a hurting soul. Search out someone who needs a friend and love them, and wait and see what God has in store for you. Love until it hurts so badly that you don’t know what to do, and then turn to Jesus, who is there to help you through. God may be waiting for you to make the first step before He will use you. Your life is before you. You can choose to live a comfortable, happy life, or you can open yourself up to be hurt and find that after years pass, your life is overflowing with meaning and purpose. Jesus opened Himself to the pain and anguish of this world, and only through that do we have hope. He is asking us to follow His example, to open ourselves to pain so that others can have hope. And as He was glorified, so will we be glorified, in some measure, someday, and we will never regret the pain that we faced.
